reading.title: When a trial becomes a precedent
reading.text:
Als der Gemeinderat die Sperrung des Uferwegs für den Autoverkehr ankündigte, war ausdrücklich von einem Versuch die Rede. Nach sechs Monaten, so hiess es, werde man Bilanz ziehen. Im Abschlussbericht findet sich dieser Vorbehalt zwar noch, allerdings nur in einer Fussnote. Im Haupttext ist inzwischen von der «bewährten Verkehrsführung» die Rede. Man könnte darin eine sprachliche Nachlässigkeit sehen. Angesichts der Sorgfalt, mit der die Verfasser an anderer Stelle zwischen Prognosen und Messwerten unterscheiden, wäre das eine ausgesprochen grosszügige Lesart.

Die Zahlen selbst geben für eine so eindeutige Formulierung wenig her. Auf dem Uferweg ist es ruhiger geworden, während der Verkehr auf zwei Parallelstrassen zugenommen hat. Ob damit insgesamt weniger gefahren wurde oder bloss anderswo, lässt sich aus den vorgelegten Messungen nicht ableiten. Daraus folgt freilich ebenso wenig, dass der Versuch gescheitert ist. Wer Ruhe am Wasser als eigenständiges Ziel betrachtet, kann die Veränderung auch dann begrüssen, wenn sie an anderer Stelle Kosten verursacht.

Fragwürdig ist daher weniger das Ergebnis als die stillschweigende Verschiebung der Entscheidungsgrundlage. Der Rat hatte eine Abwägung angekündigt. Wer eine Verkehrsführung schon vor dieser Abwägung als bewährt bezeichnet, muss zumindest offenlegen, nach welchem Massstab sie sich bewährt haben soll.
reading.tr:
When the council announced the closure of the riverside road to cars, it explicitly described the measure as a trial, to be reviewed after six months. That caveat survives in the final report, but only in a footnote. The main text now calls the traffic arrangement proven. One could put this down to careless wording. Given how carefully the authors distinguish forecasts from measurements elsewhere, that would be a remarkably generous reading.

The figures give little support to such a definite formulation. The riverside road became quieter while traffic increased on two parallel streets. The measurements cannot establish whether people drove less overall or simply drove elsewhere. Of course, this does not establish failure either. Those who regard quiet by the water as a goal in itself may welcome the change even if it brings costs elsewhere.

The issue is thus less the outcome than the unacknowledged shift in how it is judged. The council promised to weigh the trade-offs. Anyone calling the arrangement proven before that assessment must at least say what standard it is supposed to have met.

ex.prompt: What does „eine ausgesprochen grosszügige Lesart“ imply here?
options: Die Autorin hält ein blosses Versehen für eher unwahrscheinlich.
Die Autorin lobt die sorgfältige Begründung des Rats.
Die Autorin behauptet, die Messungen seien erfunden.
ex.explain: The understatement expresses doubt without making a direct accusation.

ex.prompt: Which distinction is essential to the argument?
options: Der Bericht enthält keine Daten zu Parallelstrassen.
Eine lokale Entlastung belegt keine Abnahme des Gesamtverkehrs.
Eine lokale Entlastung schliesst jede Verlagerung aus.
ex.explain: A local benefit and a network-wide change are two different claims.

ex.prompt: What is the author ultimately asking the council to make explicit?
options: Die Zahl der nicht ausgewerteten Fussnoten.
Den Namen der Person, die den Bericht formuliert hat.
Den Massstab, nach dem die Massnahme beurteilt wird.
ex.explain: The last paragraph challenges the evaluation criterion behind the word bewährt.

ex.prompt: Rewrite the central criticism in neutral German for meeting minutes. In 60–90 words, keep the local benefit, the uncertainty about total traffic and the need for a clear criterion.
ex.model: Die Messungen zeigen eine Entlastung des Uferwegs und einen Anstieg des Verkehrs auf zwei Parallelstrassen. Sie erlauben keine Aussage darüber, ob das Verkehrsaufkommen insgesamt gesunken ist. Die lokale Verbesserung kann dennoch als Erfolg gewertet werden, sofern die Ruhe am Ufer als eigenständiges Ziel definiert wird. Vor einer endgültigen Entscheidung ist deshalb festzuhalten, nach welchen Kriterien der Versuch beurteilt wird und wie mögliche Belastungen an anderen Orten berücksichtigt werden.
checklist: Preserve the difference between a measured effect and an unknown overall effect.

reading.title: A panel weighs an attractive claim
reading.text:
Moderatorin: In der Pressemitteilung heisst es, das Projekt habe sich selbst finanziert. Würden Sie das so unterschreiben?

Analyst: Wenn man nur das erste Betriebsjahr betrachtet und die Anschaffungskosten ausklammert, ist die Aussage rechnerisch vertretbar. Ich bezweifle allerdings, dass die meisten Leserinnen und Leser unter Selbstfinanzierung genau das verstehen.

Projektleiterin: Wir wollten damit sagen, dass der laufende Betrieb ohne zusätzliche Zuschüsse ausgekommen ist. Die Investition war im Haushalt ohnehin vorgesehen.

Analyst: Das ist eine andere und durchaus bemerkenswerte Aussage. Ich würde sie genauso formulieren. Dann muss niemand aus einer positiven Jahresbilanz schliessen, dass sich die Anschaffung bereits bezahlt gemacht hat.

Moderatorin: Einigkeit besteht also beim laufenden Betrieb. Bei der Gesamtinvestition bleibt die Frage offen.

ex.prompt: Under what assumptions does the analyst concede the original claim?
options: Alle Jahre werden betrachtet und sämtliche Kosten einbezogen.
Nur das erste Betriebsjahr zählt und die Anschaffungskosten bleiben aussen vor.
Der Betrieb war nur dank neuer Zuschüsse möglich.
ex.explain: The analyst explicitly limits the period and excludes the initial purchase.

ex.prompt: What does „durchaus bemerkenswert“ do in the analyst’s response?
options: Es würdigt das engere Ergebnis, ohne die ursprüngliche Aussage zu bestätigen.
Es zieht die Kritik an der ursprünglichen Aussage vollständig zurück.
Es bestreitet, dass die Jahresbilanz positiv war.
ex.explain: The analyst grants the genuine achievement while keeping the broader claim separate.

options: Ob die Projektleitung die Pressemitteilung gelesen hat.
Ob die laufenden Kosten im ersten Jahr gedeckt waren.
Ob sich die Gesamtinvestition bereits amortisiert hat.
ex.explain: The panel agrees on operating costs and leaves the return on the initial investment unresolved.

ex.prompt: Draft two German sentences suitable for a corrected press release. State the confirmed operating result and make the scope of the finding clear.
ex.model: Im ersten Betriebsjahr kam der laufende Betrieb ohne zusätzliche Zuschüsse aus. Die Anschaffungskosten sind in dieser Betrachtung nicht enthalten, sodass daraus keine Aussage über die Amortisation der Gesamtinvestition abgeleitet werden kann.
checklist: Identify the period and the cost category.
State the positive result without upgrading it to self-financing.

lessons.title: Controlling scope with nur
lessons.rule: The position and stress of nur determine what is being restricted. Moving the particle can change the claim while leaving the rest of the sentence intact.
lessons.structure: Nur Lara … ↔ Lara … nur den Entwurf
examples: Nur Lara hat den Entwurf gelesen.
Lara hat nur den Entwurf gelesen.
lessons.tip: In speech, stress can help disambiguate focus. In writing, place nur next to the phrase you want to restrict.

ex.prompt: Everyone else read the final version as well. Which sentence says that Lara read the draft only?
options: Nur Lara hat den Entwurf gelesen.
Lara hat den Entwurf nur überflogen.
Lara hat nur den Entwurf gelesen.
ex.explain: The restriction applies to den Entwurf, the thing Lara read.

ex.prompt: What does „Nur am Montag war das Büro geschlossen“ restrict?
options: The person who closed the office.

lessons.title: Reading criticism in understatement
lessons.rule: A restrained phrase can convey criticism indirectly. In a review, formulations such as lässt zu wünschen übrig and dürfte schwerfallen let the reader infer the strength of the objection.
lessons.structure: lässt zu wünschen übrig · dürfte schwerfallen
examples: Die Begründung lässt zu wünschen übrig.
The reasoning leaves something to be desired.
Es dürfte schwerfallen, aus diesen Zahlen eine klare Empfehlung abzuleiten.
It will likely be difficult to draw a clear recommendation from these figures.
lessons.tip: The literal meaning sets a baseline. The context tells you how sharp the criticism is.

ex.prompt: What is the reviewer signalling with „Die Belege sind, gelinde gesagt, dünn“?
options: The evidence is weaker than the restrained wording suggests.
ex.explain: Gelinde gesagt signals that the speaker is understating the criticism.

ex.prompt: Which response keeps a critical but restrained tone in a formal review?
options: Die vorliegenden Daten tragen diese Schlussfolgerung nur bedingt.
ex.explain: Nur bedingt limits what the evidence supports without attacking the author.

lessons.rule: A mixed conditional combines different times. A past condition can have a present result, and a present situation can explain a past result.
lessons.structure: If I had taken the job, I would live in Berlin now. · If I spoke German, I would have understood.
examples: If I had slept more, I wouldn’t be so tired now.
If she were more careful, she wouldn’t have crashed.
If we had left earlier, we would be there by now.
lessons.tip: Check the time of each half separately and choose the matching form.

lessons.title: Inversion after negative openings
lessons.rule: In formal English, some negative or restrictive expressions at the front of a clause trigger subject–auxiliary inversion. Add do, does or did when there is no auxiliary.
lessons.structure: Rarely + auxiliary + subject · Not until + clause, then invert the main clause
examples: Rarely have we seen such a clear shift.
Not until the lights went out did we notice the storm.
lessons.tip: In the second example, inversion belongs in the main clause. The clause after until keeps its normal word order.

ex.prompt: Choose the formal version. „Only after the second vote ___ the result.“

lessons.title: Qualifying an evidence-based claim
lessons.rule: Modal verbs and reporting verbs let writers match the strength of a claim to the available evidence. Suggest and may indicate a plausible reading without asserting certainty.
lessons.structure: The findings suggest … · The difference may reflect …
examples: The findings suggest that cost influences uptake.
The difference may reflect how participants were recruited.
lessons.tip: Name a specific limitation when you can. The reader can then judge where the uncertainty comes from.

ex.prompt: A small survey found a pattern. Which conclusion matches that evidence?
options: The results prove that everyone responds to price.
Cost may be one factor in the pattern we observed.
ex.explain: The last option limits the claim to a plausible factor in the observed pattern.

ex.prompt: Which phrase makes the strongest commitment?
ex.explain: Demonstrates presents the claim as established.

lessons.title: Interpreting what goes unsaid
lessons.rule: A reply can communicate an evaluation by answering less than the question asks. This inference depends on the setting and can be cancelled explicitly.
lessons.structure: Question about quality → reply about a minor or unrelated merit
examples: “Would you recommend the talk?” “The slides were beautifully designed.”
“The slides were beautifully designed, and the argument was even better.”
lessons.tip: Separate what the speaker actually said from what a listener might reasonably infer.

ex.prompt: You ask whether a colleague’s proposal is convincing. “It’s very neatly formatted,” is the whole reply. What is the likeliest implication?
options: The colleague has reserved judgement or has doubts about the argument.
The colleague has explicitly endorsed the argument.
ex.explain: Praise for a peripheral feature can imply reluctance to praise the central one.

ex.prompt: Which addition cancels the implied reservation?
options: “… although that is all I can say for it.”
“… and the evidence is unusually strong.”
ex.explain: The added clause explicitly praises the evidence.

lessons.title: Distinguishing limits from exceptions
lessons.rule: The order of a negative and a quantifier can change the logical claim. Not all leaves room for exceptions, while none rules every member out.
lessons.structure: Not all X are Y ↔ At least one X is not Y · No X are Y ↔ None are Y
examples: Not all applicants met the criteria.
None of the applicants met the criteria.
lessons.tip: Not all does not establish that anyone passed. It only establishes that at least one person did not.

ex.prompt: Which sentence preserves the scope of “The exemption does not apply to all residents”?
options: The exemption applies to no residents.
At least one resident is outside the exemption.
ex.explain: Does not apply to all means there is at least one exception.

ex.prompt: Which statement explicitly rules out every case?
options: We did not review every case.
Every case was not reviewed, as far as I know.
We reviewed none of the cases.
ex.explain: None is explicit. The other formulations allow a different interpretation.

lessons.tip: A written accent shows the stressed syllable: café, jamón.

ex.explain: h is always silent in Spanish.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and the sound

lessons.title: ¡Hola! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: Say your name with "me llamo" and where you are from with "soy de".
lessons.structure: Me llamo … | Soy de … | ¡Mucho gusto!
lessons.tip: Questions and exclamations also start with an upside-down mark: ¿…? ¡…!

ex.prompt: I am from Italy. → ___ de Italia.

lessons.title: ser or estar
lessons.rule: Spanish has two verbs for 'to be'. 'ser' for identity, origin, profession and characteristics. 'estar' for states and locations.
lessons.structure: ser: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son · estar: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están
lessons.tip: Memory aid: how do you feel and where are you? → estar.
lessons.more: ser describes what something IS: origin, job, character, time, material. estar describes HOW or WHERE something is: location, state, feeling. Memory aid: ser = lasting, estar = right now. Careful: 'Es aburrido' means 'he is boring', 'Está aburrido' means 'he is bored'.

lessons.title: Articles and gender
lessons.rule: Nouns are masculine or feminine. Masculine usually ends in -o, feminine in -a.
lessons.structure: el / los (m) · la / las (f) · un / una
lessons.tip: Remember the exceptions: el día (the day), la mano (the hand), el problema.
lessons.more: Words ending in -o are mostly masculine, words ending in -a mostly feminine. Learn the exceptions with the article: el día, el problema, el mapa, la mano, la foto. Words ending in -ción, -dad and -tud are feminine: la canción, la ciudad. Plural: after a vowel add -s, after a consonant -es: el árbol, los árboles.

lessons.title: Verbs in -ar
lessons.rule: Regular -ar verbs drop -ar and add the personal ending. The pronoun is often left out.
lessons.structure: hablar → hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan
lessons.tip: The ending shows the person, so 'Hablo' is enough instead of 'Yo hablo'.

ex.prompt: Translate: I speak a little Spanish.

lessons.more: Drop -ar and add the ending: habl-ar → habl-o. The subject pronoun is usually left out because the ending shows the person: Hablo español is enough. The stress falls on the stem in hablo, hablas, habla, hablan and on the ending in hablamos and habláis.

reading.title: Me llamo Lucía
reading.text: **Soy** Lucía y **soy** de Valencia. **Estoy** en Zúrich por trabajo. **Hablo** español, inglés y un poco de alemán. Mi oficina **está** cerca del lago. **El** trabajo **es** interesante, pero hoy **estoy** muy cansada.
reading.tr: I'm Lucía and I'm from Valencia. I'm in Zurich for work. I speak Spanish, English and a little German. My office is near the lake. The work is interesting, but today I'm very tired.

lessons.title: tener
lessons.rule: 'tener' (to have) is irregular. You also need it for age and for expressions like hunger and thirst.
lessons.structure: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen
lessons.tip: Age always with tener: Tengo 30 años (not: Soy 30).
lessons.more: tener is used for age (tengo 30 años) and many set phrases where English uses 'to be': tener hambre (to be hungry), tener frío (to be cold), tener razón (to be right), tener prisa (to be in a hurry). 'tener que' + infinitive means 'to have to': Tengo que trabajar.

lessons.title: gustar
lessons.rule: 'gustar' works the other way round: the thing that is liked is the subject. One thing 'gusta', several things 'gustan'.
lessons.structure: me / te / le / nos / os / les + gusta (singular) / gustan (plural)
lessons.tip: With a verb always 'gusta': Me gusta leer.

ex.explain: Use gustan with the plural noun “films”.

ex.prompt: We like music: ___ gusta la música.

lessons.more: With gustar, the thing that pleases is the subject. So the verb agrees with the thing: Me gusta el libro, Me gustan los libros. With verbs it always stays singular: Me gusta bailar y cantar. For emphasis add 'a mí, a ti, a él': A mí me gusta, ¿y a ti? encantar and interesar work the same way.

lessons.title: Adjective agreement
lessons.rule: Adjectives usually come after the noun and agree in gender and number.
lessons.structure: el coche rojo · la casa roja · los coches rojos · las casas rojas
lessons.tip: Adjectives ending in -e or a consonant only change for number: grande → grandes, azul → azules.

ex.explain: -e stays the same in the singular

lessons.more: Adjectives usually come AFTER the noun and agree in gender and number. Adjectives ending in -e or a consonant only change for plural: un coche verde, una casa verde. Some go in front and get shortened: un buen amigo, un gran día. 'grande' in front means 'great', after the noun 'big'.

reading.title: Mi familia
reading.text: **Tengo** dos hermanos. Mi hermano Pablo **tiene** veinte años y **es** muy **alto**. Mi hermana Elena **es** **simpática** y **le gustan** los perros. A mí **me gusta** el fútbol, pero a Elena no **le gusta** nada.
reading.tr: I have two siblings. My brother Pablo is twenty and very tall. My sister Elena is nice and likes dogs. I like football, but Elena doesn't like it at all.

lessons.title: Verbs in -er and -ir
lessons.rule: Regular -er and -ir verbs have almost the same endings. They only differ in nosotros and vosotros.
lessons.structure: comer: como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen · vivir: vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, vivís, viven
examples: I eat a lot of fruit.
lessons.tip: The subject pronoun is usually dropped because the ending already shows the person.
lessons.more: -er and -ir verbs have almost the same endings. They only differ for nosotros and vosotros: comemos / vivimos, coméis / vivís. Important verbs: beber, leer, aprender, escribir, abrir, recibir.

lessons.title: ir a + infinitive
lessons.rule: You form the near future with ir (to go) + a + infinitive. ir is irregular.
lessons.structure: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van + a + infinitive · Voy a comer.
examples: What are you going to do?
We are going to the beach.
lessons.tip: a + el becomes al: Voy al cine.

ex.prompt: Translate: She is going to buy a car.
ex.answer: Ella va a comprar un coche

lessons.more: ir a + infinitive is the most common way to talk about the future, especially plans. The 'a' must never be left out: Voy a comer, not 'Voy comer'. 'vamos a' can also be a suggestion: ¡Vamos a bailar! means 'Let's dance!'.

head: Person
ir
+ a + Inf.
Meaning
rows: we are going to see / let’s see
they are going to go out

lessons.title: hay or está
lessons.rule: hay (there is) introduces something indefinite, usually with un/una or no article. está/están describes where something specific is.
lessons.structure: Hay un banco aquí. · El banco está en la plaza. · Hay dos hoteles. · Los hoteles están cerca.
lessons.tip: hay has only one form, for singular and plural.

ex.explain: Use hay with an indefinite article such as una.

ex.prompt: La farmacia ___ al lado del banco.
ex.explain: Use está for the location of a specific thing.
Indefinite → hay, also in the plural.

lessons.more: hay (there is / there are) introduces something new or indefinite: Hay un banco, Hay muchos turistas. estar says where something specific and known is: El banco está en la plaza. hay is never followed by el or la. hay never changes, even in the plural.

lessons.title: mi, tu, su
lessons.rule: Possessives agree with the thing owned, not with the owner. In the plural they take -s. nuestro and vuestro also have a feminine form.
lessons.structure: mi/mis · tu/tus · su/sus · nuestro/a/os/as · vuestro/a/os/as · su/sus
examples: Is that his / her / your car?
lessons.tip: su can mean his, her, your (polite) or your (ustedes). The context decides.

ex.explain: Plural → tus. tú with an accent is the pronoun.

lessons.more: mi, tu and su only agree in number with what is owned: mi libro, mis libros. nuestro and vuestro also agree in gender: nuestra casa. 'su' is ambiguous (his, her, your, their). To be clear say 'el coche de él' or 'el coche de ella'.

lessons.title: e → ie: querer
lessons.rule: In some verbs the stressed e becomes ie. This does not happen in nosotros and vosotros, because there the stress is on the ending.
lessons.structure: querer: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren · likewise: pensar, empezar, preferir, cerrar
examples: La clase empieza a las nueve.
lessons.tip: They are called boot verbs: if you mark the changed forms in the table, they form the shape of a boot.

ex.explain: The nosotros form keeps the original stem.

lessons.more: In these verbs the stressed e in the stem becomes ie. nosotros and vosotros are not stressed and stay regular: queremos, queréis. They are called 'boot verbs': if you write the six forms in a grid, the changed forms make the shape of a boot.

reading.title: Un sábado en Sevilla
reading.text: Los sábados **vivo** como un turista. **Como** en un bar de tapas y **bebo** un café. Esta noche **voy a salir** con mis amigos. En el centro **hay** muchos bares. **Mi** bar favorito **está** en la plaza. **Quiero** ver un concierto.
reading.tr: On Saturdays I live like a tourist. I eat at a tapas bar and drink a coffee. Tonight I'm going out with my friends. In the centre there are many bars. My favourite bar is on the square. I want to see a concert.

ex.explain: Voy a salir con mis amigos.

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 100
lessons.rule: From 16 to 29 Spanish numbers are one word (dieciséis, veintidós). From 31 the tens and units are joined with y. Uno becomes un before a masculine noun.
lessons.structure: uno, dos, tres … diez | once, doce, trece, catorce, quince | dieciséis … veinte, veintiuno | treinta y uno · cuarenta · cincuenta · cien
lessons.tip: Age uses tener: tengo 20 años (literally: I have 20 years).

ex.explain: Before a masculine noun uno becomes un: veintiún años.

lessons.title: The time and days
lessons.rule: Ask "¿Qué hora es?". One o’clock is singular (es la una), all other hours plural (son las dos). Days and months are written in lower case. El lunes means "on Monday".
lessons.structure: Es la una · Son las tres · las tres y cuarto · las tres y media · las cuatro menos cuarto | el lunes · en mayo · a las ocho
lessons.tip: For "at" a time use a las: a las nueve = at nine.

ex.explain: Only one o’clock is singular: es la una.

options: Son las cuatro y tres cuartos.
ex.explain: Count back from the next hour: las cinco menos cuarto.

ex.prompt: On Monday I work. → ___ lunes trabajo.
ex.explain: Days take the article el, no preposition.

lessons.title: o → ue: poder
lessons.rule: In another group the stressed o becomes ue, again except in nosotros and vosotros. jugar changes u → ue.
lessons.structure: poder: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden · likewise: dormir, volver, encontrar, costar
lessons.tip: jugar (to play): juego, juegas, juega, jugamos ...

ex.explain: The nosotros form keeps the original stem.

lessons.more: Here the stressed o becomes ue, again not for nosotros and vosotros. A special case is jugar: u → ue (juego, juegas). poder is used to ask politely for permission: ¿Puedo abrir la ventana?

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs
lessons.rule: Reflexive verbs have a pronoun that refers back to the subject. It comes before the conjugated verb.
lessons.structure: levantarse: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, os levantáis, se levantan
examples: What time do you get up?
lessons.tip: With an infinitive the pronoun is attached at the end: Voy a ducharme.

ex.explain: The pronoun is attached to the infinitive: sentarme.

lessons.more: The reflexive pronoun goes before the conjugated verb: Me levanto a las siete. With an infinitive or gerund it can be attached: Voy a ducharme. Many verbs are reflexive in Spanish but not in English: irse (to leave), quedarse (to stay), llamarse (to be called).

lessons.title: lo, la, los, las
lessons.rule: Direct object pronouns replace the direct object. They come before the conjugated verb or are attached to the infinitive.
lessons.structure: lo (him/it, masculine) · la (her/it, feminine) · los · las  |  ¿El libro? Lo leo. · Voy a comprarla.
examples: Do you have the key? Yes, I have it.
lessons.tip: The gender follows the Spanish noun: la llave → la, even if English says 'it'.

ex.explain: la pizza → la, attached to the infinitive: pedirla.

lessons.more: lo, la, los, las replace the direct object (whom or what?). They go before the conjugated verb: Lo compro. With infinitive, gerund and positive commands they are attached: Voy a comprarlo, ¡Cómpralo! In Spain you often hear 'le' instead of 'lo' for people: Le veo.

lessons.title: le and les
lessons.rule: Indirect object pronouns (to whom?) are le and les. When le/les meets lo/la, le becomes se.
lessons.structure: me, te, le, nos, os, les · Le doy el libro. · Se lo doy. (not: le lo)
examples: I explain it to him / her.
lessons.tip: Spanish often doubles: Le doy el regalo a Juan. The le stays despite 'a Juan'.

ex.prompt: ___ mando un mensaje a mis padres.
Match each English meaning to the Spanish form.

lessons.more: le and les are indirect objects (to whom?). The person is often added with 'a': Le doy el libro a Ana. When le/les meets lo/la, le becomes se: Se lo doy. Order: first to whom, then what: Me lo das.

lessons.title: este, ese, aquel
lessons.rule: este = this one here, ese = that one there (near the listener), aquel = that one over there (far away). All agree in gender and number.
lessons.structure: este/esta/estos/estas · ese/esa/esos/esas · aquel/aquella/aquellos/aquellas · esto, eso (neutral)
lessons.tip: esto and eso stand for unknown things or whole situations, never before a noun.

ex.prompt: Translate: That woman (over there) is a doctor.

lessons.more: Spanish has three levels: este (here, near me), ese (there, near you), aquel (over there, far away). For unknown things or ideas use the neutral forms esto, eso, aquello: ¿Qué es esto? 'Eso es' also means 'exactly'.

reading.title: La mañana de Diego
reading.text: Diego **se levanta** a las siete. **Se ducha** y **se viste**. **Puede** desayunar en casa, pero **prefiere** el café del bar. Su madre le llama: '¿Tienes las llaves?' 'Sí, **las** tengo.' Él **le** dice adiós y **se va**.
reading.tr: Diego gets up at seven. He showers and gets dressed. He could have breakfast at home, but he prefers the coffee at the bar. His mother calls him: 'Have you got the keys?' 'Yes, I've got them.' He says goodbye to her and leaves.

lessons.title: Indefinido -ar
lessons.rule: The pretérito indefinido tells completed actions in the past (ayer, el año pasado). -ar verbs:
lessons.structure: hablar: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron
lessons.tip: Accents matter: hablo (I speak) and habló (he spoke).
lessons.more: The indefinido tells completed actions at a specific time: ayer, el año pasado, en 2020. Watch the accent: hablo (I speak) and habló (he spoke) differ only in stress. With -car, -gar, -zar the yo form changes: busqué, llegué, empecé.

lessons.title: Indefinido -er/-ir
lessons.rule: -er and -ir verbs have the same endings in the indefinido.
lessons.structure: comer: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron · vivir: viví, viviste, vivió ...
examples: Did you go out last night?
lessons.tip: In leer and creer the i becomes y: leyó, leyeron.

ex.prompt: Translate: She drank a lot of water.

lessons.more: -er and -ir have the same endings in the indefinido. In verbs like leer and creer the i becomes y: leyó, leyeron. The nosotros form of -ir verbs is the same as in the present: vivimos means 'we live' or 'we lived', context decides.

lessons.title: Irregular indefinido
lessons.rule: Important verbs are irregular in the indefinido and have no accents. ser and ir have the same forms.
lessons.structure: ser/ir: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron · tener: tuve, tuviste, tuvo · hacer: hice, hiciste, hizo · estar: estuve
lessons.tip: Whether fue means 'was' or 'went' is shown by the context.

ex.prompt: El año pasado ___ a México. (ir, yo)

lessons.more: Irregular verbs have their own stem and endings without accents: tuve, tuvo. ser and ir share the same forms: Fui profesor (I was a teacher), Fui a Madrid (I went to Madrid). decir and traer end in -eron in the 3rd person plural: dijeron, trajeron.

lessons.title: Imperfecto
lessons.rule: The imperfecto describes habits, states and background in the past (in the past, always, when I was little).
lessons.structure: -ar: hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban · -er/-ir: comía, comías, comía ... · ser: era · ir: iba
examples: As a child I lived in Lima.
It was late and it was raining.
lessons.tip: Rule of thumb: imperfecto = the scenery, indefinido = the event. Llovía cuando llegué.

ex.explain: Use era for a background description.

ex.prompt: Translate: It was raining when I arrived.

lessons.more: The imperfecto describes background, habits and states in the past: Cuando era niño, jugaba mucho. The indefinido tells the action that happens: Leía cuando sonó el teléfono. Only three verbs are irregular: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía).

lessons.title: estar + gerundio
lessons.rule: What is happening right now is expressed with estar + gerund. -ar → -ando, -er/-ir → -iendo.
lessons.structure: Estoy trabajando. · ¿Qué estás haciendo? · leer → leyendo · dormir → durmiendo
examples: I am learning Spanish right now.
What are you reading right now?
lessons.tip: Spanish only uses this form for the action in the moment, not for plans.

ex.prompt: Translate: What are you doing right now?

lessons.more: estar + gerund describes what is happening right now. -ar becomes -ando, -er and -ir become -iendo. After a vowel, i becomes y: leyendo, oyendo. -ir boot verbs change here too: dormir → durmiendo, pedir → pidiendo.

reading.title: Un viaje a México
reading.text: El año pasado **fui** a México. **Viajé** con mi novia. Cuando **llegamos**, **hacía** mucho calor. **Visitamos** pirámides y **comimos** tacos todos los días. Una noche, mientras **cenábamos**, **empezó** a llover. **Fue** un viaje increíble.
reading.tr: Last year I went to Mexico. I travelled with my girlfriend. When we arrived it was very hot. We visited pyramids and ate tacos every day. One evening, while we were having dinner, it started to rain. It was an incredible trip.

options: es el fondo de la acción

lessons.title: por or para
lessons.rule: para names goal, purpose, recipient and deadline. por names reason, route, exchange, duration and means.
lessons.structure: para: Es para ti. · Estudio para aprender. · por: Gracias por todo. · Paseo por el parque. · Lo compré por 10 euros.
lessons.tip: Ask yourself: where is it heading? → para. Where does it come from or through what? → por.

ex.explain: Use por for movement through or along a place.

lessons.more: para shows goal, purpose, recipient and deadline: para ti, para aprender, para mañana. por shows cause, route, exchange and duration: por la lluvia, por el parque, por 10 euros, por la mañana. Rule of thumb: para looks forward to the goal, por looks at the cause or the way.

lessons.title: Comparing
lessons.rule: más/menos + adjective + que compares. tan + adjective + como means as ... as. Some forms are irregular.
lessons.structure: más alto que · menos caro que · tan grande como · bueno → mejor · malo → peor · el más alto (superlative)
examples: Madrid es más grande que Toledo.
Mi hermano es tan alto como yo.
My brother is as tall as me.
lessons.tip: Not 'más bueno', but mejor.

ex.prompt: El tren es ___ rápido que el bus.
Este hotel es ___ que el otro. (worse)
Translate: That is the highest mountain.

lessons.more: Comparisons use más ... que and menos ... que. Equality: tan + adjective + como, tanto/a + noun + como. Irregular: bueno → mejor, malo → peor, grande → mayor (for age), pequeño → menor. Superlative: el/la más + adjective + de: la ciudad más bonita de España.

lessons.title: Pretérito perfecto
lessons.rule: haber + participle for actions in a period that is still going on (hoy, esta semana, nunca, ya). Very common in Spain.
lessons.structure: he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + -ado / -ido · hacer → hecho · ver → visto · escribir → escrito · decir → dicho
examples: Have you ever been to Cuba?
lessons.tip: The participle does not change: Ella ha comido (not comida).
lessons.more: The perfecto is used for past events connected to the present: hoy, esta semana, nunca, ya, todavía no. It is very common in Spain; Latin America often uses the indefinido instead. Nothing may stand between haber and the participle: Ya lo he hecho.

lessons.title: Imperative with tú
lessons.rule: The positive tú imperative equals the 3rd person singular present. There are eight important exceptions. Pronouns are attached at the end.
lessons.structure: hablar → ¡Habla! · comer → ¡Come! · Exceptions: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven · ¡Dímelo!
lessons.tip: The negative imperative uses the subjuntivo: ¡No hables!
lessons.more: The positive tú command looks like the 3rd person present: habla, come, escribe. Pronouns are attached, which often needs an accent: ¡Dímelo!, ¡Levántate! The negative command uses the subjunctive: ¡No hables!, ¡No comas!

lessons.title: Subjuntivo after querer que
lessons.rule: After expressions of wishing with a change of subject (quiero que, espero que) the subjuntivo is used. Formation: yo form present, drop -o, opposite vowel.
lessons.structure: -ar → -e: hable, hables, hable · -er/-ir → -a: coma, comas, coma · tener → tenga · hacer → haga · ser → sea
examples: It is important that you study.
lessons.tip: Same subject → infinitive: Quiero ir. Different subject → que + subjuntivo: Quiero que vayas.

ex.explain: A wish with a new subject takes the subjunctive: hables.

ex.prompt: Translate: I hope you have time.

lessons.more: The subjunctive follows wishes, requests, feelings or doubt when the subject of the second clause is different: Quiero que vengas. With the same subject use the infinitive: Quiero venir. Typical triggers: querer que, esperar que, es importante que, para que, ojalá.

reading.title: Consejos para Zúrich
reading.text: Si vienes a Zúrich, **ven** en verano. **Para** moverte, el tranvía es **más** práctico **que** el coche. **He vivido** aquí tres años y nunca **he tenido** problemas. Te recomiendo **que aprendas** un poco de alemán. **Pasea por** el lago y **no olvides** probar la fondue.
reading.tr: If you come to Zurich, come in summer. To get around, the tram is more practical than the car. I've lived here three years and never had any problems. I recommend you learn a little German. Walk along the lake and don't forget to try fondue.

ex.prompt: ¿Qué es más práctico que el coche?
ex.explain: el tranvía es más práctico que el coche

lessons.title: Pluperfect
lessons.rule: The pluscuamperfecto describes what had already happened before another past event. Formation: imperfect of haber + participle.
lessons.structure: había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían + hablado / comido / vivido · Cuando llegué, el tren ya había salido.
examples: When I arrived, they had already eaten.
I had never seen the sea.
Me dijo que había perdido las llaves.
He told me he had lost his keys.
lessons.tip: ya (already) and nunca (never) often go with it. Nothing comes between haber and the participle.

ex.prompt: Cuando llegamos, la película ya ___ empezado.
Translate: I had already read the book.

lessons.more: The pluscuamperfecto is often used in reported speech: Dijo que había llegado tarde. Irregular participles are the same as in the perfecto: había hecho, había visto, había escrito, había dicho.

lessons.title: Conditional
lessons.rule: The conditional expresses polite requests, wishes, advice and guesses: would, could, should. Formation: infinitive + -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían.
lessons.structure: hablar → hablaría · comer → comería · tener → tendría · hacer → haría · poder → podría · decir → diría · querer → querría
examples: I'd like to travel to Chile.
Yo en tu lugar no lo haría.
I wouldn't do it if I were you.
lessons.tip: The irregular stems are the same as in the future: tendr-, har-, podr-, dir-, saldr-, vendr-.

ex.prompt: ¿___ abrir la ventana, por favor? (poder, usted)
Yo en tu lugar no lo ___. (hacer)
Translate: We would like to come.

lessons.more: For advice deberías (you should) is very common: Deberías descansar. The conditional also expresses guesses about the past: Serían las diez (it was probably ten o'clock).

lessons.title: If clauses: Si tuviera ...
lessons.rule: For unreal conditions the si-clause takes the imperfect subjunctive and the main clause the conditional: Si tuviera tiempo, iría. The imperfect subjunctive comes from the 3rd person plural indefinido: tuvieron → tuviera.
lessons.structure: hablaron → hablara · tuvieron → tuviera · fueron → fuera · pudieron → pudiera · Si fuera rico, viajaría.
examples: Si tuviera dinero, compraría una casa.
If I had money, I would buy a house.
If I were you, I wouldn't go.
What would you do if you won the lottery?
lessons.tip: Never use the conditional after si: Si tuviera (not 'Si tendría').

ex.prompt: Si fuera rico, ___ por el mundo.
Translate: If I had time, I would read.

lessons.more: There are two equivalent endings: -ra and -se (tuviera = tuviese). In speech -ra is more common. The imperfect subjunctive also follows past wishes: Quería que vinieras.

lessons.title: se: impersonal and passive
lessons.rule: With se + verb in the 3rd person you say what people generally do or what is done, without saying who: Se habla español. With a plural noun the verb is plural: Se venden pisos.
lessons.structure: Se habla inglés. · Se venden casas. · Aquí no se puede fumar. · ¿Cómo se dice ...? · Se come bien en Madrid.
examples: How do you say 'Gipfeli' in Spanish?
En Suiza se come mucho queso.
In Switzerland people eat a lot of cheese.
lessons.tip: This is much more common than the passive with ser: Se construyó el puente sounds more natural than El puente fue construido.
lessons.more: Impersonal se appears on signs and in instructions: Se ruega silencio (Silence please). With people the verb stays singular: Se ayuda a los clientes. In speech people often use 'uno' or the 3rd person plural instead: Dicen que va a llover.

reading.title: Una casa en la costa
reading.text: Cuando llegamos a Valencia, mis padres ya **habían vendido** la casa. **Me habría gustado** verla una última vez. **Si tuviera** dinero, **compraría** una casa en la costa. En el pueblo **se habla** valenciano y **se come** paella todos los domingos. **Se venden** muchas casas, pero son caras.
reading.tr: When we arrived in Valencia, my parents had already sold the house. I would have liked to see it one last time. If I had money, I would buy a house on the coast. In the village people speak Valencian and eat paella every Sunday. Lots of houses are for sale, but they're expensive.

lessons.title: Futuro simple
lessons.rule: The simple future adds the endings -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án to the whole infinitive. It expresses future actions and guesses about the present.
lessons.structure: hablaré · comerás · vivirá · tendremos · harán
examples: Tomorrow I will go to the doctor.
Where can Ana be? She is probably at home.
El año que viene tendremos más tiempo.
Next year we will have more time.
lessons.tip: Irregular stems: tener → tendr-, hacer → har-, poder → podr-, salir → saldr-, decir → dir-.

ex.prompt: What is the future of hacer (ellos)?
El próximo año ___ (nosotros, tener) vacaciones largas.
Match the infinitive with the future stem.

lessons.title: Subjunctive after feelings
lessons.rule: After expressions of emotion such as me alegra que, me molesta que or siento que, use the present subjunctive when the subject changes.
lessons.structure: Me alegra que vengas. · Siento que estés enfermo.
examples: I am glad you are here.
It bothers him that you arrive late.
lessons.tip: If the subject does not change, use the infinitive: Me alegra verte.

ex.prompt: Say it bothers you that he lies.

lessons.title: Doubt: dudo que, no creo que
lessons.rule: Use the subjunctive after expressions of doubt or denial: dudo que, no creo que, no es verdad que. Creo que and es verdad que take the indicative.
lessons.structure: Creo que viene. · No creo que venga.
examples: I doubt it will rain today.
No creo que sea tan fácil.
I don’t think it’s that easy.
lessons.tip: Positive belief: indicative. Negative belief or doubt: subjunctive.

ex.prompt: No creo que él ___ la verdad.

options: No es verdad que sea caro.
No es verdad que es caro.

lessons.title: lo que and el que
lessons.rule: Lo que means “what” or “the thing that” and refers to an idea. El que, la que, los que, las que refer to a person or thing already mentioned.
lessons.structure: Lo que dices es interesante. · Este libro es el que compré.
examples: I don’t understand what you want.
La chica con la que hablé es médica.
The girl I spoke with is a doctor.
Lo que más me gusta es viajar.
What I like most is travelling.
lessons.tip: After a preposition, use el/la que or quien for people: la persona con la que trabajo.

ex.prompt: Mi coche es rojo. ¿Y el tuyo? — El mío es ___ está allí.
ex.explain: Refers back to el coche: el que.

ex.prompt: Say that what you like most is reading.
ex.answer: Lo que más me gusta es leer

reading.title: Un nuevo trabajo
reading.text: Marta empezará un nuevo trabajo en Valencia. Su madre dice: «**Me alegra que** **tengas** esta oportunidad, pero **no creo que** **sea** fácil vivir sola». Marta responde: «**Lo que** más quiero es aprender. **Estaré** bien, ya **verás**».
reading.tr: Marta will start a new job in Valencia. Her mother says: “I’m glad you have this opportunity, but I don’t think it’s easy to live alone.” Marta replies: “What I want most is to learn. I’ll be fine, you’ll see.”

ex.explain: Empezará un nuevo trabajo en Valencia.

ex.prompt: Why is sea in the subjunctive?
ex.explain: No creo que triggers the subjunctive.

lessons.title: Choosing the mood after aunque
lessons.rule: The indicative often presents the concession as a fact. The subjunctive can present it as hypothetical, already granted or irrelevant to the outcome.
lessons.structure: aunque + indicative · aunque + subjunctive
examples: Although it was raining, we went out.
Even if it rains tomorrow, we will go out.
lessons.tip: A subjunctive concession can be true. The speaker may simply be treating it as something that does not alter the decision.

ex.prompt: Which option leaves the rain uncertain? „___, iremos al mercado.“
ex.explain: Llueva presents tomorrow’s rain as a possibility.

ex.prompt: Complete with the present subjunctive of tener. „Aunque el plan ___ defectos, merece una oportunidad.“
ex.explain: Tenga is the third-person singular present subjunctive.

lessons.title: Conceding sustained effort
lessons.rule: Por más que highlights effort or intensity that fails to produce the expected result. With the indicative it can refer to known efforts, and with the subjunctive it can leave future attempts open.
lessons.structure: Por más que + clause, result
examples: Por más que insistí, no cambiaron de opinión.
However much I insisted, they did not change their minds.
Por más que insistas, no cambiarán de opinión.
No matter how much you insist, they will not change their minds.
lessons.tip: Watch for the contrast between the effort in the first clause and the outcome in the second.

ex.prompt: Which sentence refers to repeated attempts in the past?
options: Por más que pregunté, nadie contestó.
Por más que preguntes, nadie contestará.
ex.explain: Pregunté and contestó locate the attempts and outcome in the past.

ex.prompt: Complete with the present subjunctive of intentar. „Por más que lo ___, no podrás hacerlo solo.“
ex.explain: Podrás addresses tú, and intentes is its matching subjunctive form.

lessons.title: Making a correction with sino
lessons.rule: After a negation, sino replaces the rejected idea with another. Use sino que before a finite clause. Pero typically contrasts two ideas without replacing the first.
lessons.structure: no + X, sino + Y · no + clause, sino que + clause
examples: No aplazaron la votación, sino que la cancelaron.
They did not postpone the vote. They cancelled it.
No fue un descuido, sino una decisión deliberada.
It was a deliberate decision, not an oversight.
lessons.tip: No solo … sino también is additive. It confirms the first item and adds a second.

ex.prompt: Which sentence corrects the claim that the committee refused?
options: No se negó, sino que pidió tiempo.
No solo se negó, sino que además pidió tiempo.
ex.explain: The first clause rejects the refusal and sino que supplies the correction.

ex.prompt: What does „No solo revisó el informe, sino que también verificó las cifras“ say?
options: She reviewed the report and verified the figures.
She verified the figures instead of reviewing the report.
ex.explain: No solo … también confirms both actions.

lessons.title: Conceding a point without yielding
lessons.rule: Si bien introduces a concession in a measured register. Phrases such as con todo and ahora bien can shift the argument from an acknowledged strength to its limits.
lessons.structure: Si bien X, Y · X. Ahora bien, Y.
examples: Si bien el informe es exhaustivo, no justifica la medida.
Although the report is thorough, it does not justify the measure.
La propuesta es viable. Ahora bien, el plazo resulta poco realista.
The proposal is feasible. The deadline, however, seems unrealistic.
lessons.tip: Keep the scope of a reservation clear. Challenging a deadline is a narrower claim than rejecting the proposal.

ex.prompt: Which response grants the evidence while disputing its interpretation?
options: Los datos son sólidos. Ahora bien, admiten más de una lectura.
Los datos no existen, de modo que no hay nada que discutir.
Los datos son sólidos y la conclusión es indiscutible.
ex.explain: The first sentence accepts the data, then qualifies the conclusion.

ex.prompt: What is being challenged in „Si bien el acuerdo es legítimo, su aplicación plantea dudas“?
options: The way the agreement is implemented.
ex.explain: The concession accepts legitimacy, and the objection concerns implementation.

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The French alphabet
lessons.rule: French has 26 letters plus accents and ç. Many letters at the end of a word are silent, and some vowels sound very different from English.
lessons.structure: h = silent | j = zh | u = "ee" with rounded lips | ç = s | é = ay · è = eh
lessons.tip: Final consonants are usually silent: petit sounds like "puh-tee". Remember the word CaReFuL: c, r, f and l at the end are often pronounced.

alphabet.sound: k, or s before e, i
g, or zh before e, i

ex.prompt: Which letter sounds like: zh as in "measure"?
ex.explain: J j: zh as in "measure" – jour.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and its sound

lessons.title: How French sounds
lessons.rule: In French, many letters at the end of a word are not pronounced. Some letter groups always make the same sound.
lessons.structure: final -s, -t, -d → silent (Paris, petit) | ou → "oo" (bonjour) | é → "ay" (café) | on / an / in → nasal vowels
lessons.tip: For u (tu), say "ee" while rounding your lips.

ex.prompt: Match the spelling and the sound

lessons.title: Bonjour ! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: Say your name with "je m'appelle" and where you are from with "je viens de".
lessons.structure: Je m'appelle … | Je viens de … | Enchanté(e) !
lessons.tip: Use vous with strangers: "Comment vous appelez-vous ?"

ex.prompt: My name is Marc. → Je m'___ Marc.
I come from Germany. → Je ___ d'Allemagne.

lessons.title: être
lessons.rule: 'être' (to be) is irregular and used constantly.
lessons.structure: je suis · tu es · il/elle est · nous sommes · vous êtes · ils/elles sont
lessons.tip: Nationalities and professions have no article: Il est médecin.

ex.explain: Omit the article when naming a profession in this construction.

lessons.more: être is the most important verb and completely irregular. No article is used with professions: Je suis médecin. c'est introduces things and people: C'est mon frère. With adjectives use il/elle est: Il est sympa. In casual speech 'tu es' often becomes 't'es'.

lessons.title: Article
lessons.rule: Nouns are masculine or feminine. Before a vowel and silent h, le and la become l'.
lessons.structure: le / la / l' / les · un / une / des
lessons.tip: In the plural the article is the same for both genders: les, des.
lessons.more: Before a vowel or silent h, le and la become l': l'ami, l'hôtel. In the plural there is only les and des, whatever the gender. The s of les and des is linked before a vowel: les_amis [lezami]. For likes and dislikes use the definite article: J'aime le café.

lessons.title: Verbs in -er
lessons.rule: Most French verbs end in -er. The endings -e, -es and -ent are not pronounced.
lessons.structure: parler → je parle · tu parles · il parle · nous parlons · vous parlez · ils parlent
lessons.tip: je becomes j' before a vowel: j'aime, j'habite.
lessons.more: The endings -e, -es, -e and -ent all sound the same, they are silent: je parle, tu parles, ils parlent sound identical. Only -ons and -ez are heard. Verbs in -ger and -cer change in the nous form: nous mangeons, nous commençons.

reading.title: Je m'appelle Claire
reading.text: Bonjour ! Je **suis** Claire et je **suis** française. J'**habite** à Lausanne. Je **parle** français et anglais. Mon mari **est** suisse, il **est** ingénieur. Le soir, nous **regardons** **un** film ou nous **écoutons** **de la** musique.
reading.tr: Hello! I'm Claire and I'm French. I live in Lausanne. I speak French and English. My husband is Swiss, he's an engineer. In the evening we watch a film or listen to music.

lessons.title: avoir
lessons.rule: 'avoir' (to have) is irregular. Age is expressed with avoir.
lessons.structure: j'ai · tu as · il a · nous avons · vous avez · ils ont
lessons.tip: Don't confuse: ils ont (have) and ils sont (are).
lessons.more: avoir is used for possession and many expressions where English uses 'to be': avoir faim (to be hungry), avoir froid (to be cold), avoir raison (to be right), avoir 30 ans (to be 30). 'Il y a' means 'there is / there are' and never changes.

lessons.title: Negation ne … pas
lessons.rule: Negation surrounds the conjugated verb: ne before the verb, pas after it. Before a vowel ne becomes n'.
lessons.structure: ne + verb + pas · n' + vowel
lessons.tip: In speech 'ne' is often dropped: Je sais pas. In writing it belongs there.

ex.prompt: Make the sentence negative: Je travaille.

lessons.more: ne and pas go around the conjugated verb. In compound tenses they go around the auxiliary: Je n'ai pas mangé. With an infinitive both come first: ne pas fumer. After a negation un, une, des become de: Je n'ai pas de voiture. In speech ne is often dropped: Je sais pas.

lessons.title: Asking questions
lessons.rule: The simplest question: a statement with rising intonation. A bit more formal: Est-ce que + sentence.
lessons.structure: Tu viens ? · Est-ce que tu viens ? · Qu'est-ce que c'est ?
lessons.tip: Before a vowel que becomes qu': Est-ce qu'il vient ?

ex.prompt: Where is the hotel? → ___ est l'hôtel ?

lessons.more: There are three levels of questions: intonation only (Tu viens ?, very common in speech), est-ce que (Est-ce que tu viens ?, neutral) and inversion (Viens-tu ?, formal, written). With inversion and il/elle a -t- is added when the verb ends in a vowel: Parle-t-il français ?

head: Style
example
rows: Est-ce que tu viens ce soir ?

reading.title: Au café
reading.text: Marc **a** trente ans. Il **a** faim, mais il **n'a pas** beaucoup de temps. **Est-ce qu'**il y a une table libre ? Oui ! Il **ne** prend **pas de** dessert, juste un sandwich. 'Vous **avez** du café ?' 'Bien sûr, monsieur.'
reading.tr: Marc is thirty. He's hungry, but he doesn't have much time. Is there a free table? Yes! He doesn't take a dessert, just a sandwich. 'Do you have coffee?' 'Of course, sir.'

ex.prompt: Pourquoi 'pas de dessert' et pas 'pas un dessert' ?

lessons.title: aller and futur proche
lessons.rule: aller (to go) is irregular. With aller + infinitive you form the near future, like 'going to' in English.
lessons.structure: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont · Je vais manger.
examples: We are going to leave tomorrow.
What are you going to do?
lessons.tip: à + le becomes au, à + les becomes aux: au marché, aux États-Unis.

ex.prompt: Translate: We are going to eat.

lessons.more: The futur proche (aller + infinitive) is the most common future in speech: Je vais appeler. After aller use à for places: Je vais à Genève, au cinéma, à la gare. For countries: en France (feminine), au Canada (masculine), aux États-Unis (plural).

lessons.title: faire
lessons.rule: faire (to make, to do) is irregular and appears in many expressions: weather, sport, shopping.
lessons.structure: je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font
lessons.tip: vous faites ends in -tes like vous êtes and vous dites, not in -ez.
lessons.more: faire means to make or to do and appears in many expressions: faire du sport, faire les courses (to go shopping), faire la cuisine (to cook). For the weather: Il fait beau, il fait froid. Careful: vous faites (not 'faisez') and ils font.

lessons.title: Partitive article
lessons.rule: For unspecified quantities (some bread, water) you use the partitive article. After negation and quantities only de is used.
lessons.structure: du pain (m) · de la soupe (f) · de l'eau (vowel) · des pâtes (pl) · Je ne mange pas de viande. · beaucoup de sucre
examples: Il n'y a pas de lait.
lessons.tip: After aimer, adorer, détester the definite article is used: J'aime le café.

ex.explain: Negation → de, before a vowel d'.
Use de l’ before a vowel.

ex.answer: Je ne mange pas de viande
ex.explain: Use pas de in the negative.

lessons.more: The partitive article is used for an unspecified amount of something you don't count: du pain, de l'eau. German and English leave the article out here, French never does. After a negation and quantities only de is used: pas de lait, beaucoup de lait, un kilo de pommes.

lessons.title: mon, ma, mes
lessons.rule: Possessives agree with the thing owned. Before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, mon, ton, son replace ma, ta, sa.
lessons.structure: mon/ma/mes · ton/ta/tes · son/sa/ses · notre/nos · votre/vos · leur/leurs · mon amie (not ma amie)
lessons.tip: son/sa says nothing about the owner: sa mère means his or her mother.

ex.explain: Feminine starting with a vowel → mon.

lessons.more: The possessive agrees with what is owned, not with the owner: son vélo can mean 'his bike' or 'her bike'. Before feminine words starting with a vowel use mon, ton, son instead of ma, ta, sa: mon amie, son école. For several owners: notre, votre, leur.

lessons.title: Adjective agreement
lessons.rule: Adjectives agree in gender and number: + e for feminine, + s for plural. Most come after the noun.
lessons.structure: un livre intéressant · une ville intéressante · Before the noun: beau, bon, grand, petit, jeune, vieux, nouveau
lessons.tip: Irregular: beau → belle, nouveau → nouvelle, vieux → vieille, blanc → blanche.

ex.explain: grand usually comes before the noun.

lessons.more: Most adjectives come after the noun and add -e (feminine) and -s (plural). Short common adjectives go in front (BAGS: Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size): un beau jardin, une petite maison. Irregular: beau → belle, nouveau → nouvelle, vieux → vieille, bon → bonne.

reading.title: Le week-end
reading.text: Ce week-end, je **vais** à la montagne avec **mes** amis. Nous **allons faire** une randonnée. Il **fait** beau. Dans **mon** sac, il y a **du** pain, **du** fromage et **de l'**eau. **Ma** copine prend **une** **petite** tente **verte**.
reading.tr: This weekend I'm going to the mountains with my friends. We're going to go hiking. The weather is nice. In my bag there's bread, cheese and water. My girlfriend is taking a small green tent.

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 100
lessons.rule: 21, 31, 41 … use et: vingt et un. From 70 French counts in twenties: 70 = 60 + 10, 80 = 4 × 20, 90 = 4 × 20 + 10. In Switzerland and Belgium you hear septante and nonante; in Switzerland also huitante.
lessons.structure: un, deux, trois … dix | onze, douze, treize, quatorze, quinze, seize | dix-sept · vingt · trente · quarante · cinquante · soixante | soixante-dix · quatre-vingts · quatre-vingt-dix · cent
lessons.tip: Age uses avoir: j’ai 20 ans.

lessons.title: The time and days
lessons.rule: Ask "Quelle heure est-il ?". Answer with il est … heure(s), then et quart, et demie or moins le quart. Timetables use the 24-hour clock. Days and months are written in lower case.
lessons.structure: Il est une heure · deux heures · deux heures et quart · deux heures et demie · trois heures moins le quart · midi · minuit | lundi · en mai · à huit heures
examples: Il est huit heures et demie.
lessons.tip: lundi = this Monday; le lundi = every Monday.

ex.prompt: My birthday is in May. → Mon anniversaire est ___ mai.

lessons.title: Verbs in -ir
lessons.rule: Regular -ir verbs (finir, choisir) add the syllable -iss- in the plural.
lessons.structure: finir: je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent
lessons.tip: Not all -ir verbs follow this pattern: partir, dormir, sortir are different (je pars, nous partons).
lessons.more: Regular -ir verbs like finir, choisir and réussir add -iss- in the plural: nous finissons, ils finissent. Careful: many -ir verbs are different, for example partir (je pars, nous partons), dormir and sortir. Learn those one by one.

lessons.title: pouvoir, vouloir, devoir
lessons.rule: The three modal verbs are irregular. They are followed by the infinitive.
lessons.structure: pouvoir: je peux, tu peux, il peut, nous pouvons, vous pouvez, ils peuvent · vouloir: je veux ... ils veulent · devoir: je dois ... ils doivent
lessons.tip: Ask politely with je voudrais (I would like) or pourriez-vous (could you).

ex.prompt: Je ___ un croissant, s'il vous plaît. (polite)

lessons.more: The three modal verbs take an infinitive: Je peux venir. To ask politely use the conditional: Je voudrais un café, Pourriez-vous m'aider ? 'Il faut' (one must) is impersonal and very common: Il faut partir.

lessons.title: au, du, aux
lessons.rule: The prepositions à and de merge with the articles le and les. With la and l' they stay separate.
lessons.structure: à + le → au · à + les → aux · de + le → du · de + les → des · à la, à l', de la, de l' stay
lessons.tip: Countries: feminine → en France, masculine → au Portugal, plural → aux Pays-Bas.

ex.prompt: I live in Portugal: J'habite ___ Portugal.

lessons.more: à and de merge with le and les, but never with la or l': au marché, à la gare, à l'hôtel. Verbs like parler de, jouer à and venir de need this all the time: Je joue au foot, Je joue du piano (instruments take de), Il revient du travail.

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs
lessons.rule: Pronominal verbs have a reflexive pronoun before the verb. Before a vowel me/te/se become m', t', s'.
lessons.structure: se lever: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons, vous vous levez, ils se lèvent
lessons.tip: Negation surrounds pronoun and verb: Je ne me lève pas.
lessons.more: The reflexive pronoun goes before the verb: Je me lève. Before a vowel: je m'appelle, il s'habille. In the passé composé all reflexive verbs take être: Je me suis levé(e). In commands it is attached: Lève-toi ! Assieds-toi !

lessons.title: le, la, les as pronouns
lessons.rule: Direct object pronouns replace the direct object and come before the conjugated verb (with an infinitive, before the infinitive).
lessons.structure: le (him/it) · la (her/it) · l' (before a vowel) · les (them) · Je le vois. · Je vais la voir.
examples: Tu connais Marc ? Oui, je le connais.
Do you know Marc? Yes, I know him.
lessons.tip: Indirect objects (to whom?) are lui and leur: Je lui parle.

ex.prompt: Le film ? Je ___ regarde ce soir.
Les clés ? Je ne ___ trouve pas.

lessons.more: le, la, les replace the direct object and go before the verb: Je le connais. With a modal or aller they go before the infinitive: Je vais le faire. In the passé composé they go before the auxiliary, and the participle agrees: Ces photos ? Je les ai prises.

head: Sentence
with pronoun
rows: Je n'ai pas vu le film.

reading.title: Une journée de Sophie
reading.text: Sophie **se lève** à six heures. Elle **finit** son travail à cinq heures et elle **va au** marché. Elle **veut** acheter des fruits. Les pommes ? Elle **les** trouve trop chères. Le soir, elle **doit** préparer le dîner **pour** ses enfants.
reading.tr: Sophie gets up at six. She finishes work at five and goes to the market. She wants to buy fruit. The apples? She finds them too expensive. In the evening she has to make dinner for her children.

lessons.title: Passé composé with avoir
lessons.rule: The most important past tense: avoir + participle. -er → -é, -ir → -i, -re → -u. Many participles are irregular.
lessons.structure: J'ai mangé. · Tu as fini. · Il a vendu. · faire → fait · prendre → pris · voir → vu · avoir → eu · être → été
lessons.tip: Negation: ne ... pas surrounds avoir: Je n'ai pas mangé.
lessons.more: The passé composé tells completed actions. Participle: -er → -é, -ir → -i, -re → -u. Many common verbs are irregular: fait, pris, mis, dit, écrit, vu, lu, bu, eu, été. In speech it completely replaces the passé simple.

lessons.title: Passé composé with être
lessons.rule: Verbs of movement and change of state (aller, venir, partir, arriver, naître, mourir ...) and all reflexive verbs form the passé composé with être. The participle agrees with the subject.
lessons.structure: Je suis allé(e). · Elle est partie. · Nous sommes arrivés. · Ils se sont levés.
examples: Je me suis réveillé à 7 heures.
lessons.tip: Memory aid: the 'house' of verbs that you go in and out of: entrer, sortir, monter, descendre ...
lessons.more: Verbs of movement and change of state (memory word DR MRS VANDERTRAMP: devenir, revenir, mourir, retourner, sortir, venir, arriver, naître, descendre, entrer, rentrer, tomber, rester, aller, monter, partir) and all reflexive verbs take être. The participle agrees like an adjective: elle est partie, ils sont venus.

lessons.title: Imparfait
lessons.rule: The imparfait describes habits and states in the past. Stem of the nous form without -ons + endings.
lessons.structure: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient · parler: je parlais · faire: je faisais · être (exception): j'étais
examples: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais au foot.
When I was little, I played football.
lessons.tip: imparfait = scenery and habit, passé composé = one-off event: Il pleuvait quand je suis arrivé.

ex.prompt: Hier soir, je ___ un film. (voir, one-off)

lessons.more: The imparfait describes background, habits and states: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais au foot. The passé composé tells what then happens: Je lisais quand le téléphone a sonné. Stem: nous form without -ons (nous parlons → je parlais). Only exception: être → j'étais.

lessons.title: Futur simple
lessons.rule: The futur simple: infinitive + the endings of avoir. With -re the e is dropped. Some stems are irregular.
lessons.structure: -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont · parler → je parlerai · prendre → je prendrai · être → je serai · avoir → j'aurai · aller → j'irai · faire → je ferai
examples: Tomorrow the weather will be nice.
lessons.tip: After quand French uses the future, not the present: Quand je serai grand ...

ex.prompt: Infinitive and je form in the future

lessons.more: The futur simple is the infinitive + ending: parler → je parlerai. With -re the e is dropped: prendre → je prendrai. Important irregular stems: ser- (être), aur- (avoir), ir- (aller), fer- (faire), pourr- (pouvoir), viendr- (venir), verr- (voir). After 'quand' French uses the future: Quand je serai grand ...

lessons.title: ne ... jamais, plus, rien
lessons.rule: Besides ne ... pas there are other negations. They surround the conjugated verb.
lessons.structure: ne ... jamais (never) · ne ... plus (no longer) · ne ... rien (nothing) · ne ... personne (nobody)
examples: He doesn't live here any more.
lessons.tip: In spoken French ne is often dropped: Je sais pas.

ex.prompt: Translate: We don't work any more.

lessons.more: These negations work like ne ... pas: Je ne fume plus. 'personne' and 'rien' can also be the subject: Personne n'est venu, Rien ne marche. In the passé composé personne comes after the participle: Je n'ai vu personne, but Je n'ai rien vu.

reading.title: Souvenirs de vacances
reading.text: Quand j'**étais** petit, nous **allions** chaque été en Bretagne. Il **faisait** souvent froid. Une année, nous **sommes partis** en Italie. J'**ai mangé** des glaces tous les jours ! L'année prochaine, je **retournerai** en Bretagne avec mes enfants. Je **ne** l'ai **jamais** oubliée.
reading.tr: When I was little we went to Brittany every summer. It was often cold. One year we went to Italy. I ate ice cream every day! Next year I'll go back to Brittany with my children. I've never forgotten it.

ex.explain: nous allions chaque été en Bretagne

ex.prompt: 'nous sommes partis' est au passé composé avec être parce que ...
options: partir est un verbe de mouvement

lessons.title: y and en
lessons.rule: y replaces places and complements with à. en replaces quantities and complements with de. Both come before the verb.
lessons.structure: Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'y vais. · Tu as du pain ? Oui, j'en ai. · J'en ai deux.
examples: Je pense à mon examen. J'y pense.
lessons.tip: With quantities the number stays: J'ai trois frères → J'en ai trois.

ex.prompt: Tu vas au cinéma ? Oui, j'___ vais.
Tu veux du café ? Oui, j'___ veux.
Elle a deux chats. Elle ___ a deux.
ex.explain: Use en with a quantity and keep the number.

ex.prompt: Il habite à Lyon. Il ___ habite.
Translate: I don't talk about it.

lessons.more: y replaces places and phrases with à: Je vais à Paris → J'y vais. Je pense à mon examen → J'y pense. en replaces phrases with de and quantities: Je viens de Lyon → J'en viens. J'ai trois frères → J'en ai trois. Both go before the verb. Set phrases: Il y a, Allons-y, Je m'en vais.

lessons.title: qui and que
lessons.rule: Relative pronouns: qui is the subject of the relative clause (a verb follows), que is the object (a subject follows).
lessons.structure: l'homme qui parle · le livre que je lis · que becomes qu' before a vowel · où for places and time
examples: La femme qui chante est ma sœur.
The woman who is singing is my sister.
Le film que j'ai vu était bien.
The film I saw was good.
La ville où j'habite est belle.
The town where I live is beautiful.
lessons.tip: Test: a verb follows directly → qui. A subject follows (je, tu, Marie) → que.

ex.prompt: Le garçon ___ joue est mon fils.
La robe ___ tu portes est belle.
ex.explain: Use que when the subject tu follows.

ex.prompt: Le café ___ nous allons est fermé.
C'est le livre ___ elle a écrit.
Translate: The man who is coming.

lessons.more: qui is the subject of the clause and comes right before the verb: l'homme qui parle. que is the object and is followed by a new subject: le livre que je lis. qui never becomes qu'. où is used for place and time: le jour où je suis né. dont replaces de + noun: le film dont je parle.

lessons.title: Comparing
lessons.rule: plus / moins / aussi + adjective + que. bon becomes meilleur, bien becomes mieux. Superlative: le / la / les plus + adjective.
lessons.structure: plus grand que · moins cher que · aussi beau que · bon → meilleur · bien → mieux · le plus grand
examples: Paris est plus grand que Lyon.
That is the most beautiful town.
lessons.tip: meilleur is an adjective (describes a noun), mieux an adverb (describes a verb): Il chante mieux.

ex.prompt: Le TGV est ___ rapide que le bus.
Il est ___ grand que son frère. (genauso)
Translate: That is the most expensive hotel.

lessons.more: plus / moins / aussi + adjective + que. With nouns: plus de / moins de / autant de: J'ai plus de temps que toi. Irregular: bon → meilleur (adjective), bien → mieux (adverb). Superlative with article: le plus grand, la plus belle. If the adjective follows the noun, the article is repeated: la ville la plus belle.

lessons.title: Imperative
lessons.rule: The imperative has three forms: tu, nous, vous, without subject pronoun. With -er verbs the -s is dropped in the tu form.
lessons.structure: parler: Parle ! Parlons ! Parlez ! · finir: Finis ! · être: Sois ! Soyez ! · avoir: Aie ! Ayez ! · Pronomen: Regarde-moi !
lessons.tip: aller loses the -s in the tu form: Va ! Only before y does it come back: Vas-y !

ex.explain: Use the nous form without the subject pronoun.

lessons.more: The imperative has three forms without a subject: Parle ! Parlons ! Parlez ! In -er verbs the s of the tu form is dropped: Mange ! (but before y and en: Vas-y !). Pronouns are attached, me becomes moi: Aide-moi ! In the negative they go in front: Ne me regarde pas !

lessons.title: Subjonctif after il faut que
lessons.rule: After il faut que, je veux que, bien que the subjonctif is used. Stem: ils form present without -ent, endings -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent.
lessons.structure: parler → que je parle · finir → que je finisse · être → que je sois · avoir → que j'aie · faire → que je fasse · aller → que j'aille
examples: Je veux que vous soyez là.
I want you to be there.
lessons.tip: Same subject → infinitive: Je veux partir. Different subject → que + subjonctif.
lessons.more: The subjonctif follows expressions of necessity, wish, emotion and doubt: il faut que, je veux que, je suis content que, bien que. Stem: ils form without -ent (ils finissent → que je finisse). With the same subject use the infinitive: Je veux partir, but Je veux que tu partes.

reading.title: Vivre à Genève
reading.text: Genève est **plus** petite **que** Paris, mais c'est une ville **où** il y a beaucoup de choses à faire. Le lac ? J'**y** vais chaque dimanche. Des musées ? Il y **en** a beaucoup. **Il faut que** tu **viennes** me voir ! **Viens** en été, c'est la **meilleure** saison.
reading.tr: Geneva is smaller than Paris, but it's a city where there's a lot to do. The lake? I go there every Sunday. Museums? There are lots. You must come and see me! Come in summer, it's the best season.

lessons.title: Pluperfect
lessons.rule: The plus-que-parfait describes what had already happened before another past event. Formation: imparfait of avoir or être + participle.
lessons.structure: j'avais mangé · tu étais parti(e) · Quand je suis arrivé, le film avait déjà commencé.
examples: Quand je suis arrivé, ils avaient déjà mangé.
When I arrived, they had already eaten.
Il m'a dit qu'il avait perdu ses clés.
He told me he had lost his keys.
lessons.tip: The choice between avoir and être is the same as in the passé composé.

ex.prompt: Quand nous sommes arrivés, le train ___ parti.
Translate: I had already read the book.

lessons.more: It is often needed in past reported speech: Il a dit qu'il était malade et qu'il avait raté le bus. With être the participle agrees: elles étaient arrivées.

lessons.title: Conditional and si clauses
lessons.rule: The conditionnel présent expresses polite requests, wishes and unreal situations. Formation: future stem + imparfait endings. The si-clause takes the imparfait: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais.
lessons.structure: je parlerais · je serais · j'aurais · je pourrais · je voudrais · Si j'étais riche, je voyagerais.
examples: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
Si j'avais une voiture, j'irais à la montagne.
If I had a car, I'd go to the mountains.
lessons.tip: Never use the conditional after si: Si j'avais (not 'Si j'aurais').

ex.prompt: Si j'___ le temps, je viendrais.
Translate: If I were you, I would go.

lessons.more: The three si types: Si + présent, futur (real: S'il pleut, je resterai). Si + imparfait, conditionnel (unreal now). Si + plus-que-parfait, conditionnel passé (unreal past: Si j'avais su, je serais venu).

lessons.title: Gerund: en + -ant
lessons.rule: The gérondif (en + present participle) describes two actions by the same person at the same time, or the manner: Je chante en cuisinant. Formation: nous form without -ons + -ant.
lessons.structure: nous parlons → en parlant · nous finissons → en finissant · nous faisons → en faisant · être → en étant · avoir → en ayant · savoir → en sachant
examples: Il écoute de la musique en travaillant.
He listens to music while working.
On my way out, I saw Marie.
lessons.tip: Both actions must have the same subject. tout stresses a contrast: Tout en étant fatigué, il a continué.

ex.prompt: Il est tombé en ___ du vélo. (descendre)
Translate: I learn French by watching films.
ex.answer: J'apprends le français en regardant des films

lessons.more: The gérondif expresses simultaneity (en mangeant), manner (en courant), means (en travaillant dur) and condition (En partant maintenant, tu arriveras à l'heure). Only three verbs are irregular: étant, ayant, sachant.

lessons.title: Reported speech
lessons.rule: In reported speech the tenses shift when the reporting verb is in the past: présent → imparfait, passé composé → plus-que-parfait, futur → conditionnel. Pronouns adapt.
lessons.structure: « Je suis fatigué. » → Il a dit qu'il était fatigué. · « Je viendrai. » → Elle a dit qu'elle viendrait. · « Tu viens ? » → Il m'a demandé si je venais.
examples: Elle a dit qu'elle était malade.
Il m'a demandé si j'avais faim.
He asked me if I was hungry.
Ils ont dit qu'ils arriveraient demain.
They said they would arrive tomorrow.
lessons.tip: Yes/no questions are introduced with si; questions with qu'est-ce que become ce que: Il m'a demandé ce que je voulais.

ex.prompt: « Je suis prêt. » → Il a dit qu'il ___ prêt.
« Tu as faim ? » → Elle m'a demandé ___ j'avais faim.
« Je viendrai. » → Il a dit qu'il ___. (venir)
Translate: She asked me what I wanted.
ex.answer: Elle m'a demandé ce que je voulais

lessons.more: Time expressions change: aujourd'hui → ce jour-là, demain → le lendemain, hier → la veille, ici → là. Commands become de + infinitive: « Ferme la porte ! » → Il m'a dit de fermer la porte.

head: direct speech
reported speech
rows: Il a dit qu'il avait fini.

reading.title: Le mystère du voisin
reading.text: Hier, **en rentrant** du travail, j'ai vu que mon voisin **était** déjà **parti**. Il m'**avait dit** qu'il **partirait** en voyage, mais pas si tôt. **Si j'avais** son numéro, je l'**appellerais**. Sa fille m'a demandé **si** je **savais** où il était. Je lui ai dit que je n'en **savais** rien.
reading.tr: Yesterday, on my way home from work, I saw that my neighbour had already left. He had told me he would go travelling, but not so soon. If I had his number, I would call him. His daughter asked me if I knew where he was. I told her I knew nothing about it.

ex.prompt: Quand a-t-il vu que le voisin était parti ?
Si j'avais son numéro, je l'___. (appeler)

lessons.title: Subjonctif after feelings and doubt
lessons.rule: Use the subjunctive after expressions of emotion (je suis content que, j’ai peur que) and doubt (je doute que, je ne pense pas que) when the subject changes.
lessons.structure: Je suis content que tu viennes. · Je doute qu’il soit là.
examples: Je suis contente que tu sois là.
I am glad you are here.
J’ai peur qu’il fasse trop froid.
I’m afraid it will be too cold.
Je ne pense pas qu’elle puisse venir.
I don’t think she can come.
lessons.tip: Je pense que takes the indicative. Only the negative or question form takes the subjunctive.

ex.prompt: Say you are afraid he is late.
ex.answer: J’ai peur qu’il soit en retard

lessons.title: lequel, auquel, duquel
lessons.rule: After a preposition, use lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles for things. With à they become auquel, à laquelle, auxquels; with de they become duquel, de laquelle, desquels.
lessons.structure: la table sur laquelle … · le projet auquel je pense …
examples: Voici le stylo avec lequel j’écris.
Here is the pen I write with.
C’est le problème auquel je pense.
That’s the problem I’m thinking about.
La raison pour laquelle je pars est simple.
The reason why I’m leaving is simple.
lessons.tip: For people you can also use qui after a preposition: la femme avec qui je travaille.

ex.prompt: La chaise sur ___ tu es assis est cassée.
Le film ___ je pense est très long.
Voilà la raison pour ___ je suis venu.
Match à + pronoun with the contracted form.

lessons.title: The passive voice
lessons.rule: The passive uses être + past participle. The participle agrees with the subject. The agent is introduced with par.
lessons.structure: La lettre est écrite par Paul. · Les maisons ont été construites en 1900.
examples: Le gâteau est préparé par ma sœur.
The cake is made by my sister.
La décision a été prise hier.
Les invités seront accueillis à 20 h.
The guests will be welcomed at 8 pm.
lessons.tip: French often prefers on instead of the passive: On a pris la décision hier.

ex.prompt: Le livre a été écrit ___ Victor Hugo.
ex.explain: The agent is introduced with par.

ex.prompt: Say the museum was built in 1900.
ex.answer: Le musée a été construit en 1900

lessons.title: Futur antérieur
lessons.rule: The futur antérieur (avoir/être in the future + past participle) describes an action that will be finished before another future moment.
lessons.structure: Quand tu arriveras, j’aurai fini. · Elle sera partie avant midi.
examples: Quand tu rentreras, j’aurai préparé le dîner.
When you get home, I will have made dinner.
By 6 pm we will have left.
Dès que j’aurai fini, je t’appellerai.
As soon as I have finished, I will call you.
lessons.tip: After quand and dès que, French uses the future, not the present: quand tu arriveras.

ex.prompt: Demain à midi, j’___ fini ce travail.
Dès que nous ___ mangé, nous sortirons. (avoir)
Quand tu ___, je serai déjà parti.

reading.title: Le nouveau quartier
reading.text: La mairie a annoncé que le vieux marché **sera rénové**. Beaucoup d’habitants **ont peur que** les prix **soient** trop élevés. Le projet **auquel** la ville tient tant **aura été terminé** avant 2028, dit le maire. **Je doute qu’il ait** raison, répond une voisine.
reading.tr: The town hall announced that the old market will be renovated. Many residents are afraid that prices will be too high. The project the city cares so much about will have been finished before 2028, says the mayor. I doubt he is right, replies a neighbour.

ex.prompt: Why is soient in the subjunctive?

lessons.title: Choosing mood with avant que and après que
