lessons.rule: Avant que takes the subjunctive. In standard edited French, après que takes the indicative because it presents its event as preceding the main event.
lessons.structure: avant que + subjunctive · après que + indicative
examples: Prévenez-moi avant que la réunion commence.
Let me know before the meeting starts.
Après que la réunion s’est terminée, nous avons rédigé le compte rendu.
After the meeting ended, we wrote the minutes.
lessons.tip: An optional ne after avant que can be stylistic and need not negate the verb.

ex.prompt: Which form fits standard edited French? „Après que les invités ___, nous avons fermé la porte.“
ex.explain: Après que takes the indicative in this register.

ex.prompt: Complete with the present subjunctive of être. „Agissons avant qu’il ne ___ trop tard.“
ex.explain: Soit follows avant que. Here ne does not reverse the meaning.

lessons.title: Referring to an unspecified idea
lessons.rule: Use ce qui for a subject, ce que for a direct object and ce dont when the underlying construction requires de. The pronoun can pick up an idea or refer to an unspecified thing.
lessons.structure: ce qui + verb · ce que + subject + verb · ce dont … de
examples: Ce qui m’étonne, c’est son silence.
What surprises me is her silence.
Voilà ce dont nous avons besoin.
lessons.tip: Rebuild the base phrase to find the missing role: nous avons besoin de quelque chose.

ex.prompt: Complete: „Ce ___ ils se souviennent, c’est son accueil.“
ex.explain: Se souvenir de requires de, which dont supplies.

ex.prompt: Supply only the missing word. „Ce ___ compte, c’est le résultat.“
ex.explain: The missing element is the subject of compte.

lessons.title: Shifting the focus of a restriction
lessons.rule: Ne … que expresses a restriction. The phrase after que tells you which part of the message is limited.
lessons.structure: ne + verb + que + restricted phrase
examples: Elle n’a consulté que les annexes.
Elle n’a consulté les annexes que lundi.
She consulted the appendices only on Monday.
lessons.tip: In informal speech, ne is often dropped. The placement of que still signals the focus.

ex.prompt: Which sentence restricts who was consulted?
options: Nous n’avons consulté les experts que mardi.
Nous n’avons consulté que les experts.
Nous n’avons pas consulté les experts.
ex.explain: Les experts immediately follows que, so the restriction applies to the people.

ex.prompt: What does „Il n’a fait que reformuler la question“ imply?
options: He refused to rephrase the question.
ex.explain: Que introduces the action that exhausts what he did.

lessons.title: Reading diplomatic reservations
lessons.rule: Measured disagreement often acknowledges a benefit before naming a limitation. Il reste que can introduce the issue that still needs attention after a concession.
lessons.structure: Certes X, mais Y · Il reste que Y
examples: Certes, le projet est ambitieux, mais son financement reste incertain.
The project is certainly ambitious, but its funding remains uncertain.
Il reste que les délais ne sont pas tenables.
The fact remains that the deadlines are unrealistic.
lessons.tip: A reservation aimed at the evidence or timetable leaves space for agreement on the rest.

ex.prompt: Which response grants the goal while challenging the method?
options: L’objectif est irréprochable, donc la méthode l’est aussi.
L’objectif est contestable, mais la méthode est parfaite.
L’objectif est louable. Il reste que la méthode pose problème.
ex.explain: The first sentence grants the goal, while the second identifies the method as the problem.

ex.prompt: In „Le texte gagnerait à être précisé“, what does the reviewer imply?
options: The text will win a prize.
The text has already been clarified.
ex.explain: Gagnerait à is an indirect way to recommend an improvement.

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The Russian alphabet
lessons.rule: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet with 33 letters. Some look like Latin letters but sound different (Р = r, Н = n, В = v, С = s). Once you know them, Russian is read almost as it is written.
lessons.structure: Look-alikes: В = v · Н = n · Р = r · С = s · У = oo · Х = kh | ъ ь have no sound of their own
lessons.tip: Unstressed о sounds like a: молоко (milk) is said "ma-la-KO".

alphabet.sound: soft sign: softens the letter before

ex.prompt: Which letter sounds like: rolled r?

ex.explain: Х х: kh as in Scottish "loch" – хлеб.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and its sound

lessons.title: Cyrillic: letters you can read
lessons.rule: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet. Some letters look and sound like English. Some look familiar but sound different: these "false friends" are the key to reading.
lessons.structure: same: А К М О Т | false friends: В = v · Н = n · Р = r · С = s · У = u · Х = kh
lessons.tip: Unstressed о sounds like а: вода is said "vada".

ex.explain: К = k, О = o, Т = t.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and the sound

lessons.title: Привет! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: In Russian you say "they call me": Меня зовут … Where you are from: Я из …
lessons.structure: Меня зовут … | Я из … | Очень приятно!
lessons.tip: With strangers ask politely: "Как вас зовут?"

ex.prompt: My name is Ivan. → Меня ___ Иван.
Polite: What is your name? → Как ___ зовут?

lessons.title: Greetings
lessons.rule: Russian distinguishes between informal and formal 'you'. 'Привет' is casual, 'Здравствуйте' polite.
lessons.structure: Привет (privét) · Здравствуйте (zdrávstvujte) · Спасибо (spasíbo) · Пожалуйста (pozhálujsta)
examples: Hi! How are you? (privét, kak delá)
lessons.tip: 'Пожалуйста' means please and also you're welcome.
lessons.more: Здравствуйте is polite and used for several people, Привет is casual among friends. The first в in здравствуйте is silent: [zdrástvujte]. Пожалуйста means 'please' and also 'you're welcome'. Saying goodbye: До свидания (formal), Пока (casual).

lessons.title: No 'to be' in the present
lessons.rule: In the present tense 'to be' is simply left out. 'Это' means 'this is / these are'.
lessons.structure: Я студент. = I am a student. · Это мой дом. = This is my house.
lessons.tip: Russian has no articles: 'Это книга' can mean 'a book' or 'the book'.

ex.explain: In the present 'to be' is left out.

lessons.more: In the present tense 'to be' is dropped: Я врач (I am a doctor). In writing a dash stands between two nouns: Москва — столица России. There are no articles: дом means 'house', 'a house' or 'the house'. In the past and future you need быть: Я был врачом.

lessons.title: Three genders
lessons.rule: You can usually tell the gender by the ending: consonant masculine, -а/-я feminine, -о/-е neuter.
lessons.structure: он: дом, стол · она: мама, книга · оно: окно, море
lessons.tip: Watch out: папа (dad) ends in -а but is masculine.
lessons.more: You can almost always tell the gender by the ending: consonant = masculine, -а/-я = feminine, -о/-е = neuter. With -ь (soft sign) you have to learn it: день (m), ночь (f). Male people in -а stay masculine: папа, дедушка. Gender decides adjective and past-tense endings.

reading.title: Меня зовут Анна
reading.text: **Привет!** Меня зовут Анна. **Я** студентка. **Это** мой город, Цюрих. **Мой** **дом** маленький, но **окно** большое. **Спасибо**, что читаешь!
reading.tr: Hi! My name is Anna. I'm a student. This is my city, Zurich. My house is small, but the window is big. Thanks for reading!

lessons.title: Verbs: 1st conjugation
lessons.rule: Many verbs in -ать follow the 1st conjugation. The ending shows the person.
lessons.structure: читать: я читаю · ты читаешь · он читает · мы читаем · вы читаете · они читают
lessons.tip: Same pattern: знать (to know), работать (to work), делать (to do).
lessons.more: The 1st conjugation has -е- in the endings (читаешь, читает). When the ending is stressed, е becomes ё: идёшь, живёт. Many verbs in -ать and -ять belong here: знать, делать, гулять. After a vowel use -ю, after a consonant -у: читаю, but живу.

lessons.title: Verbs: 2nd conjugation
lessons.rule: Verbs in -ить usually belong to the 2nd conjugation. The -и- in the endings is typical.
lessons.structure: говорить: я говорю · ты говоришь · он говорит · мы говорим · вы говорите · они говорят
lessons.tip: 'по-русски', 'по-немецки' means 'in Russian', 'in German'.

ex.prompt: Which ending fits 'ты' in the 2nd conjugation?

lessons.more: The 2nd conjugation has -и- in the endings (говоришь, говорит) and -ят/-ат in the plural. Most verbs in -ить and some in -еть belong here: смотреть, видеть. In some the consonant changes in the я form: любить → люблю, видеть → вижу.

lessons.title: Feminine accusative
lessons.rule: As a direct object feminine nouns change their ending: -а becomes -у, -я becomes -ю. Masculine things and neuter nouns stay the same.
lessons.structure: книга → книгу · Таня → Таню · дом, окно bleiben
lessons.tip: Ask 'whom or what?'. Feminine words in -а/-я change their ending.
lessons.more: The accusative marks the direct object (whom or what?). Only feminine words in -а/-я change: -а → -у, -я → -ю. Feminine words in -ь and inanimate masculine and neuter words stay the same: Я вижу дом, Я люблю ночь. The accusative also follows в/на for direction: Я иду в школу.

reading.title: Вечер дома
reading.text: Вечером я **читаю** книгу, а мой брат **смотрит** фильм. Мама **говорит** по телефону. Папа **делает** ужин. Я **люблю** **книгу**, которую **читаю**. Мы **живём** в маленькой квартире.
reading.tr: In the evening I read a book and my brother watches a film. Mum is on the phone. Dad makes dinner. I love the book I'm reading. We live in a small flat.

lessons.title: Plural of nouns
lessons.rule: Masculine and feminine nouns form the plural with -ы. After г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч you write -и. Neuter nouns: -о → -а, -е → -я.
lessons.structure: стол → столы · мама → мамы · книга → книги · окно → окна · море → моря · Exceptions: друг → друзья, человек → люди
examples: These are my books. (éto moí knígi)
lessons.tip: The spelling rule: after г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч you never write ы, always и.
lessons.more: Plural: masculine and feminine mostly -ы; after г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч and after soft consonants -и (книги, дни). Neuter: -о → -а, -е → -я. Some masculine words take stressed -а: дом → дома, город → города. Irregular: друг → друзья, человек → люди, ребёнок → дети.

lessons.title: мой, моя, моё
lessons.rule: Possessive pronouns agree with the gender of the thing owned. его (his), её (her) and их (their) never change.
lessons.structure: мой брат (m) · моя сестра (f) · моё окно (n) · мои друзья (Pl) · твой / твоя / твоё / твои · наш / наша / наше / наши
lessons.tip: его is pronounced [yevó], the г sounds like в.
lessons.more: The possessive agrees with what is owned, like an adjective: мой брат, моя сестра. For 'his', 'her' and 'their' there are invariable forms: его (his), её (her), их (their): его мама, её брат. When it refers back to the subject use свой: Он любит свою маму.

lessons.title: у меня есть: to have
lessons.rule: A verb for 'to have' is rarely used in everyday speech. You say: at me there is ... (у + genitive + есть + nominative).
lessons.structure: у меня · у тебя · у него · у неё · у нас · у вас · у них + есть
lessons.tip: After у, он becomes него and она becomes неё (with н at the start).

ex.prompt: Translate: Do you have a computer?

lessons.more: Russian hardly uses a verb for 'to have'. You say 'by me there is': У меня есть машина. The owner is in the genitive after у. With он, она, они an н is added after prepositions: у него, у неё, у них. When it's about a quality rather than existence, есть is dropped: У меня большая квартира.

lessons.title: Prepositional: в and на
lessons.rule: For the question where? (где?) the prepositional case follows в (in) and на (on, at). The noun usually ends in -е. Nouns in -ия, -ие end in -ии.
lessons.structure: Москва → в Москве · парк → в парке · работа → на работе · Россия → в России · здание → в здании
lessons.tip: на is used for events and open spaces: на концерте, на улице, на вокзале.
lessons.more: The prepositional case only follows prepositions, mainly в and на for 'where?' and о for 'about'. Almost all words end in -е: в парке, на работе. Words in -ия and -ие end in -ии: в России, в здании. на is used for open areas, events and some fixed words: на улице, на концерте, на работе, на почте.

lessons.title: Adjective agreement
lessons.rule: Adjectives agree in gender and number. The dictionary form is masculine.
lessons.structure: новый дом · новая машина · новое окно · новые книги · хороший / хорошая / хорошее / хорошие · большой (stressed: -ой)
lessons.tip: After г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч the rule applies again: и instead of ы (хороший, русские).
lessons.more: Adjectives agree in gender, number and case. Basic endings: -ый/-ий/-ой (m), -ая/-яя (f), -ое/-ее (n), -ые/-ие (pl). After г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч use и instead of ы: русский, хороший. If the ending is stressed it is -ой: большой, молодой.

reading.title: Моя семья
reading.text: **У меня есть** брат и две **сестры**. **Мои** сёстры живут **в Москве**. Брат работает **на почте**. **У него** **новая** машина и **большой** дом. **Наша** мама — врач.
reading.tr: I have a brother and two sisters. My sisters live in Moscow. My brother works at the post office. He has a new car and a big house. Our mother is a doctor.

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 100
lessons.rule: The number decides the form of the noun: after 1 singular (один год), after 2–4 genitive singular (два года), after 5–20 genitive plural (пять лет). Один and два change with gender: одна книга, две книги.
lessons.structure: один, два, три, четыре, пять … десять | одиннадцать, двенадцать … двадцать | тридцать · сорок · пятьдесят · сто
lessons.tip: Age uses the dative: мне 20 лет (literally: to me 20 years).

ex.explain: год is masculine: два. After 2–4: года.

lessons.title: The time and days
lessons.rule: Ask "Который час?". The word час follows the number rule: час, два часа, пять часов. "At" a time and "on" a day are both в: в восемь часов, в понедельник. Days and months are written in lower case.
lessons.structure: час · два часа · пять часов · половина девятого (8:30) | в понедельник · в мае · в восемь часов
examples: I get up at seven o’clock.
lessons.tip: половина девятого (8:30) literally means "half of the ninth hour".

lessons.title: genitive after нет
lessons.rule: нет (there is no, I have no) requires the genitive. Masculine and neuter: -а/-я. Feminine: -ы/-и.
lessons.structure: брат → нет брата · окно → нет окна · сестра → нет сестры · книга → нет книги · время → нет времени
lessons.tip: Foreign words ending in -е, -и, -о, -у never change: кафе, метро, такси.
lessons.more: After нет (there isn't, I don't have) use the genitive. Masculine and neuter: -а/-я (брата, окна). Feminine: -ы/-и (сестры, книги). Quantities also take the genitive: много работы, мало времени. Careful: время → времени, мать → матери.

lessons.title: Dative: мне нравится
lessons.rule: 'To like' is formed with the dative of the person: to me pleases ... Age is also given with the dative.
lessons.structure: мне · тебе · ему · ей · нам · вам · им + нравится (Sg.) / нравятся (Pl.) · Мне 30 лет.
lessons.tip: The thing that is liked is the subject. Plural → нравятся.
lessons.more: With нравиться the thing that pleases is the subject and the person is in the dative: Мне нравится музыка, Мне нравятся фильмы. Age is also given with the dative: Мне 30 лет (1 год, 2 to 4 года, from 5 лет). More dative phrases: мне холодно (I'm cold), мне скучно (I'm bored).

lessons.title: Masculine animate accusative
lessons.rule: Masculine living beings take the ending -а/-я in the accusative (like the genitive). Inanimate masculine nouns stay unchanged.
lessons.structure: Я вижу брата. · Я знаю учителя. · but: Я вижу дом. · Я люблю чай.
examples: I am waiting for a friend.
lessons.tip: Ask yourself: is it alive? Then like the genitive. Otherwise the basic form stays.

ex.explain: The animate noun takes the form кота.
папа ends in -а → like feminine: папу.
Watch out: звонить takes the dative → брату.

lessons.more: With animate masculine words (people, animals) the accusative equals the genitive: Я вижу брата, Я люблю кота. Inanimate things stay the same: Я вижу стол. In the plural this applies to all animate words: Я знаю этих людей.

lessons.title: Instrumental with с
lessons.rule: After с (with) the instrumental is used. Masculine and neuter: -ом/-ем. Feminine: -ой/-ей.
lessons.structure: друг → с другом · молоко → с молоком · мама → с мамой · Таня → с Таней · я → со мной · ты → с тобой
examples: Я иду в кино с другом.
I'm going to the cinema with a friend.
lessons.tip: Also after быть for a profession in the past: Он был врачом.
lessons.more: After с (with) use the instrumental. Masculine and neuter: -ом/-ем (с братом, с чаем). Feminine: -ой/-ей (с мамой, с Таней). Without a preposition it shows the tool: писать ручкой (to write with a pen), ехать поездом. Also after быть and работать: Я работаю врачом.

lessons.title: идти and ехать
lessons.rule: Russian distinguishes going on foot (идти) and going by vehicle (ехать). Both are irregular.
lessons.structure: идти: иду, идёшь, идёт, идём, идёте, идут · ехать: еду, едешь, едет, едем, едете, едут
lessons.tip: For the question where to? в/на + accusative follows: в школу, на работу.
lessons.more: идти means to go on foot, ехать to go by vehicle. Both describe movement in one direction, now or planned: Я иду домой. For regular movement or round trips use ходить and ездить: Я хожу в спортзал. The vehicle takes на: ехать на метро.

reading.title: В выходные
reading.text: В субботу у меня **нет** **времени**. Я **еду** **с другом** на дачу. **Мне нравится** природа. Мой друг **любит** **кота**, и кот всегда **едет** **с нами**. Домой мы **идём** пешком.
reading.tr: On Saturday I have no time. I'm going to the dacha with a friend. I like nature. My friend loves the cat, and the cat always comes with us. We walk home.

ex.prompt: С кем он едет на дачу?

lessons.title: past
lessons.rule: The past tense is simple: infinitive without -ть + -л. It agrees with gender, not with person.
lessons.structure: он читал · она читала · оно читало · они читали · быть: был, была, было, были
lessons.tip: A woman always says я была, a man я был.

ex.prompt: Translate: They were at the cinema.

lessons.more: The past tense agrees with gender and number, not with the person: stem + -л, -ла, -ло, -ли. A woman says я читала, a man я читал. вы always takes the plural, even for one person: Вы были в Москве? Irregular: идти → шёл, шла, шли.

lessons.title: Aspect
lessons.rule: Almost every verb has two forms: imperfective (process, repetition) and perfective (completed result, one-off).
lessons.structure: делать / сделать · читать / прочитать · писать / написать · покупать / купить · говорить / сказать
examples: I read the book for two hours. (process)
lessons.tip: Signal words: каждый день, часто, долго → imperfective. уже, наконец → often perfective.
lessons.more: Almost every verb has a pair: imperfective (process, repetition) and perfective (one-time result). Я читал книгу = I was reading the book (for a while). Я прочитал книгу = I finished the book. Perfective verbs have no present: their present form is future (я прочитаю = I will finish reading).

lessons.title: future
lessons.rule: Imperfective verbs: буду + infinitive. Perfective verbs: the present endings already give the future.
lessons.structure: буду, будешь, будет, будем, будете, будут + читать · perfective: я прочитаю, ты сделаешь, он купит
examples: What are you going to do?
lessons.tip: Never буду + perfective verb. 'Я буду сделать' is wrong.

ex.explain: Use the perfective for a completed result: напишу.

lessons.more: For imperfective verbs the future is буду + infinitive: Я буду работать (I will be working, process). Perfective verbs are simply conjugated in the 'present': Я сделаю (I'll get it done). буду + perfective infinitive is wrong.

lessons.title: Verbs in -ся
lessons.rule: Reflexive verbs end in -ся (after a vowel -сь). The ending is attached to the conjugated verb.
lessons.structure: учиться: я учусь, ты учишься, он учится, мы учимся, вы учитесь, они учатся · заниматься: я занимаюсь ...
examples: Как тебя зовут? Меня зовут Фабио.
What's your name? My name is Fabio.
lessons.tip: -тся and -ться are both pronounced [tsa].
lessons.more: -ся is the reflexive ending; after a vowel it becomes -сь: учусь, учитесь. Many verbs have -ся without being reflexive in English: нравиться, смеяться (to laugh), бояться (to be afraid), заниматься (to do, to study). The -ся always comes at the very end.

lessons.title: Imperative
lessons.rule: The imperative is formed from the present stem: after a vowel -й, otherwise -и. The polite or plural form adds -те.
lessons.structure: читать → читай / читайте · говорить → говори / говорите · смотреть → смотри · садиться → садись / садитесь
lessons.tip: With пожалуйста every request becomes polite.
lessons.more: The imperative comes from the present stem (они form without ending): читают → читай, говорят → говори. For вы and politely add -те: читайте, говорите. Imperfective sounds like a friendly invitation (Садитесь!), perfective is a specific request (Скажите, пожалуйста ...). In the negative use mostly imperfective: Не говори!

reading.title: Как я учил русский
reading.text: Раньше я **учил** русский язык каждый день. Сначала я **читал** простые тексты, потом **прочитал** целую книгу. Летом я **буду жить** в Петербурге. Там я **найду** работу. **Не бойся** ошибок, **говори** больше!
reading.tr: I used to study Russian every day. First I read simple texts, then I read a whole book. In summer I'll live in Petersburg. There I'll find a job. Don't be afraid of mistakes, speak more!

lessons.title: можно, нельзя, надо
lessons.rule: These words express permission, prohibition and necessity. The person is in the dative.
lessons.structure: можно (one may) · нельзя (one may not) · надо / нужно (one must) · Мне надо работать.
lessons.tip: With the dative it becomes personal: мне надо = I must.
lessons.more: можно, нельзя, надо and нужно are impersonal; the person is in the dative: Мне надо работать, Тебе нельзя курить. можно is used to ask permission: Можно войти? нужно can also take a noun: Мне нужна помощь (I need help), the form agrees: нужен, нужна, нужно, нужны.

lessons.title: хотеть: to want
lessons.rule: хотеть is mixed: singular like the 1st conjugation (with ч), plural like the 2nd conjugation.
lessons.structure: я хочу · ты хочешь · он хочет · мы хотим · вы хотите · они хотят
lessons.tip: More polite: я хотел бы / я хотела бы (I would like).
lessons.more: хотеть is mixed: in the singular like the 1st conjugation with т → ч (хочу, хочешь, хочет), in the plural like the 2nd conjugation (хотим, хотите, хотят). With a noun it often takes the accusative, or the genitive for amounts: Я хочу чаю. More polite: Я бы хотел(а) ...

lessons.title: где, куда, откуда
lessons.rule: где asks for the place (prepositional), куда for the direction (accusative), откуда for the origin (из + genitive).
lessons.structure: Где ты? В школе. · Куда ты идёшь? В школу. · Откуда ты? Из Германии.
lessons.tip: Likewise with на: на работе (where), на работу (where to), с работы (where from).
lessons.more: где (where?) takes the prepositional: в школе. куда (where to?) takes the accusative: в школу. откуда (where from?) takes the genitive with из or с: из школы, с работы. Remember the pairs: в → из, на → с. For people: к врачу (to the doctor), от врача (from the doctor).

lessons.title: Comparative
lessons.rule: The comparative usually ends in -ее. Many common adjectives are irregular. 'than' is чем.
lessons.structure: быстрый → быстрее · интересный → интереснее · хороший → лучше · плохой → хуже · большой → больше · маленький → меньше · дорогой → дороже
examples: The train is faster than the bus.
lessons.tip: Instead of чем the genitive can be used: быстрее автобуса.
lessons.more: The simple comparative ends in -ее and doesn't change: Этот дом новее. It is followed by 'чем' or the genitive: Он старше, чем я = Он старше меня. Many common adjectives are irregular: лучше, хуже, больше, меньше, дешевле, дороже. Superlative: самый + adjective: самый большой город.

lessons.title: который
lessons.rule: который introduces relative clauses. Gender and number follow the noun it refers to, the case follows its role in the relative clause.
lessons.structure: человек, который ... · девушка, которая ... · окно, которое ... · люди, которые ... · feminine accusative: которую
examples: Это друг, который живёт в Риме.
This is the friend who lives in Rome.
The book I am reading is interesting.
Where are the people who work here?
lessons.tip: In Russian there is always a comma before который.

ex.prompt: Translate: The man who lives here.

lessons.more: который agrees in gender and number with the word it refers to, but its case depends on its role in the clause: Девушка, которую я знаю (accusative). Дом, в котором я живу (prepositional). A comma always comes before который.

reading.title: Город, который я люблю
reading.text: Петербург — город, **который** я очень люблю. Он **красивее**, **чем** Москва, но зимой там **холоднее**. **Куда** пойти? В Эрмитаж! **Откуда** лучший вид? С Исаакиевского собора. Туда **можно** подняться, но **нельзя** фотографировать внутри. **Мне надо** поехать туда снова.
reading.tr: Petersburg is a city I love very much. It's more beautiful than Moscow, but in winter it's colder there. Where to go? To the Hermitage! Where's the best view from? From St Isaac's Cathedral. You can go up, but you can't take photos inside. I have to go there again.

ex.prompt: Какой город красивее, по мнению автора?

options: accusative (same as nominative for inanimate nouns)

lessons.title: genitive plural
lessons.rule: The genitive plural is needed after numbers from 5, after много, мало, сколько and after нет. The ending depends on the word: -ов/-ев (masculine), zero ending (feminine in -а, neuter in -о), -ей (words in -ь, ж, ш, ч, щ).
lessons.structure: стол → столов · музей → музеев · книга → книг · окно → окон · день → дней · врач → врачей · пять столов, много книг
examples: I have a lot of friends.
There are no museums in the town.
lessons.tip: Zero-ending words often get a fill vowel: окно → окон, ручка → ручек, девушка → девушек.

ex.prompt: Translate: I don't have much time and I have many questions.
ex.answer: У меня мало времени и много вопросов

lessons.more: Numbers overview: 1 + nominative singular (один стол), 2 to 4 + genitive singular (два стола), from 5 + genitive plural (пять столов). Irregular: человек → много людей, but пять человек; год → пять лет; ребёнок → детей.

lessons.title: Verbs of motion with prefixes
lessons.rule: Prefixes give идти and ехать a direction and make them perfective: прийти (to arrive), уйти (to leave), войти (to go in), выйти (to go out), перейти (to cross). With a prefix идти becomes -йти.
lessons.structure: при- (arriving) · у- (away) · в- (into) · вы- (out of) · пере- (across) · по- (setting off) · прийти → приду, придёшь · уехать → уеду, уедешь
examples: We're getting off at the next stop.
lessons.tip: Imperfective partners with prefix: приходить, уходить, входить, выходить, приезжать, уезжать. The prefix вы- is always stressed in the perfective: вы́йти.

ex.prompt: Он ___ на работу в 9 часов. (arrive, past)
Translate: I'll come tomorrow at eight.

lessons.more: The prefixes need matching prepositions: прийти в/на + acc. (where to), уйти из/с + gen. (from where), подойти к + dat. (up to someone), перейти через + acc. (across). With ехать: приехать, уехать, въехать, выехать, переехать (also: to move house).

lessons.title: Conditional with бы
lessons.rule: For wishes and unreal conditions use the past form + бы. There is no separate tense: Если бы у меня было время, я бы пришёл can mean 'would come' or 'would have come'.
lessons.structure: Я бы хотел(а) ... · Если бы я знал, я бы сказал. · Было бы хорошо ... · Я бы на твоём месте ...
examples: Если бы я был богат, я бы путешествовал.
If I were rich, I would travel.
На твоём месте я бы не ходил туда.
If I were you, I wouldn't go there.
lessons.tip: бы usually comes after the first stressed word or after the verb. In the если clause it comes right after если: если бы.

ex.prompt: Если бы она знала, она ___ пришла.
Если ___ у меня было время, я бы читал. (particle)
Translate: If I had time, I would come.
ex.answer: Если бы у меня было время я бы пришёл

lessons.more: Real conditions don't need бы: Если будет время, я приду (future). чтобы expresses purpose and wishes for others, also with the past form: Я хочу, чтобы ты пришёл. With the same subject: чтобы + infinitive: Я учу русский, чтобы читать Толстого.

head: Type
Russian
Meaning
rows: If I have time, I will come.
Если бы было время, я бы пришёл.
If I had time, I would come.

lessons.title: Verbs of motion: round trips
lessons.rule: Russian distinguishes one-way movement (идти, ехать, лететь) from multi-directional or habitual movement (ходить, ездить, летать). In the past ходил/ездил means 'went and came back': Вчера я ходил в кино.
lessons.structure: идти / ходить · ехать / ездить · лететь / летать · Я иду в парк. · Я часто хожу в парк. · Летом мы ездили в Сочи.
examples: Каждый день я хожу на работу пешком.
Every day I walk to work.
I'm going to the airport now.
Have you ever flown to Japan?
lessons.tip: Rule of thumb: on the way now or a one-way plan → идти/ехать. Regularly, in general or round trip → ходить/ездить.

ex.prompt: Летом мы ___ в Италию. (ездить, мы, past)
Translate: I often go to Bern.

lessons.more: Watch the change д → ж in the я form: ездить → езжу, ходить → хожу. по- expresses the start of a movement (пойти, поехать): Пойдём в кафе! Children and transport: Ребёнок уже ходит (can already walk).

reading.title: Переезд
reading.text: В прошлом году мы **переехали** в Цюрих. Сначала я **ходил** на курсы немецкого три раза в неделю. **Если бы** у меня **было** больше времени, я **бы** учил и швейцарский немецкий. Каждое утро я **выхожу** из дома в семь и **еду** на трамвае на работу. В нашем доме живёт **много** **детей** и **пять** **собак**.
reading.tr: Last year we moved to Zurich. At first I went to German classes three times a week. If I had more time, I would learn Swiss German too. Every morning I leave home at seven and take the tram to work. Lots of children and five dogs live in our building.

ex.prompt: Если ___ у меня было время, я бы учил. (particle)

lessons.title: Numbers with nouns
lessons.rule: After 1 the noun stays in the nominative singular. After 2, 3 and 4 it takes the genitive singular. From 5 to 20 it takes the genitive plural. The last digit decides: 21 like 1, 22 like 2.
lessons.structure: один стол · два стола · пять столов · двадцать один стол
examples: There are twenty-one students in the group.
lessons.tip: With years of age: 1 год, 2–4 года, 5+ лет.

ex.prompt: Match the number with the right phrase.

lessons.title: свой: one’s own
lessons.rule: Свой refers back to the subject of the same clause. It replaces мой, твой, его, её when the owner is the subject. It agrees like an adjective.
lessons.structure: Он любит свою машину. · Она звонит своей маме.
lessons.tip: With его/её the owner is a different person. Свой always points to the subject.

ex.explain: The subject owns it: свою (accusative feminine).

ex.prompt: Иван видел Петра и ___ сестру. (Peter’s sister)
ex.explain: The sister belongs to Peter, not the subject: его.

ex.prompt: Мы живём в ___ доме. (our own, prepositional)
Say that she is calling her (own) mother.

lessons.title: Short adjectives: рад, готов, должен
lessons.rule: Some adjectives have a short form used after the subject: рад (glad), готов (ready), должен (must), занят (busy), болен (ill). They agree in gender and number.
lessons.structure: он рад · она рада · они рады · я должен / должна
examples: I am glad to see you.
lessons.tip: A woman says: я рада, я должна, я готова.

lessons.title: чтобы: purpose and wishes
lessons.rule: Чтобы + infinitive expresses purpose when the subject is the same. With a different subject, чтобы + past tense expresses a wish or request.
lessons.structure: Я учусь, чтобы работать. · Я хочу, чтобы ты пришёл.
examples: Speak louder so that everyone hears.
lessons.tip: Different subject after хотеть: always чтобы + past tense, never the infinitive.

ex.prompt: Учитель хочет, чтобы мы ___. (читать, past plural)
Say you want them to stay.

reading.title: День рождения
reading.text: Завтра моему брату будет **двадцать два года**. Мама хочет, **чтобы** мы **приготовили** **свой** знаменитый торт. Я **рад**, но очень **занят**. Мне нужно купить **пять свечей** и **три подарка**.
reading.tr: Tomorrow my brother turns twenty-two. Mum wants us to make our famous cake. I am glad, but very busy. I need to buy five candles and three presents.

ex.prompt: How old will the brother be?
Why is приготовили in the past tense?
options: After чтобы with a different subject

lessons.title: Condensing a relative clause
lessons.rule: A past passive participle can condense a clause with который in formal writing. Its ending agrees with the noun being described, even when the phrase names an agent.
lessons.structure: доклад, который подготовила комиссия → доклад, подготовленный комиссией
examples: We discussed the report prepared by the committee.
Она сослалась на статьи, опубликованные в мае.
She referred to articles published in May.
lessons.tip: Find the noun the participle modifies before choosing its ending. An explicitly named agent can take the instrumental.

ex.prompt: Complete the phrase. «Мы ознакомились с отчётом, ___ вчера».
ex.explain: С отчётом is masculine singular instrumental, and the participle agrees with it.

ex.prompt: Who prepared the document in «Документ, подготовленный комиссией, опубликовал секретарь»?
ex.explain: Комиссией is the agent of подготовленный. Секретарь published it.

lessons.title: Tracking the actor in a participial phrase
lessons.rule: A Russian adverbial participle generally shares its actor with the main verb. A perfective form often sets up a completed action before the main event.
lessons.structure: прочитав письмо, она ответила
examples: After reading the letter, she replied immediately.
While discussing the plan, the colleagues spotted an error.
lessons.tip: In formal writing, check that the main clause supplies a subject who can carry out both actions.

ex.prompt: Which sentence makes the same person both the reader and the decision-maker?
ex.explain: Анна is the explicit actor of both actions.

ex.prompt: What is the sequence in «Закончив проверку, инженер выключил прибор»?
options: The engineer switched off the device before the check.
The actions took place in different years.
The engineer finished the check before switching off the device.
ex.explain: Закончив marks completion before the main event.

lessons.title: Inferring stance from particles
lessons.rule: Short particles can reveal how the speaker treats the shared context. Ведь often invokes a reason or a fact the listener is expected to recognise. Разве in a question often signals surprise or doubt.
lessons.structure: Ведь + statement · Разве + question?
examples: Не спеши, ведь у нас ещё есть время.
Do not rush. After all, we still have time.
lessons.tip: The inference depends on intonation and context. In a transcript, look at the previous turn to see what expectation the speaker is reacting to.

ex.prompt: What does the speaker signal with «Разве вы уже закончили?»?
options: The speaker had expected that the work was not yet finished.
The speaker explicitly confirms that the work is finished.
The speaker gives an order to finish.
ex.explain: Разве indicates that finishing already would conflict with an expectation.

ex.prompt: Which reply explicitly reminds the listener of a reason they should recognise?
options: Ведь вы сами предложили перенести заседание.
ex.explain: Ведь presents the listener’s own proposal as a shared reason.

lessons.title: Keeping a contested claim attributed
lessons.rule: По словам attributes information to a named source. Якобы can add distance or doubt, especially when the surrounding text questions the claim.
lessons.structure: по словам + genitive · якобы + reported claim
examples: По словам свидетеля, дверь была открыта.
According to the witness, the door was open.
В письме утверждается, что документ якобы подделали.
The letter claims that the document was supposedly forged.
lessons.tip: When summarising competing accounts, preserve the attribution. Dropping it can turn a disputed statement into your own assertion.

ex.prompt: Which summary keeps a disputed claim attributed to one side?
options: По утверждению подрядчика, срок нарушен, но заказчик это оспаривает.
Заказчик и подрядчик согласны, что срок нарушен.
ex.explain: The sentence keeps the contractor as the source and explicitly records the disagreement.

ex.prompt: Which word most directly adds distance in «Документ якобы подписали вчера»?
ex.explain: Якобы signals that the signing is alleged.

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The Polish alphabet
lessons.rule: Polish has 32 letters. The extra ones (ą, ć, ę, ł, ń, ó, ś, ź, ż) have their own sounds. Polish is read the way it is written, and the stress is almost always on the second-to-last syllable.
lessons.structure: ł = w | w = v | ą ę = nasal | c = ts | ó = u | sz = sh · cz = ch · rz = ż
lessons.tip: Letter pairs: sz (sh), cz (ch), rz (zh), ch (kh) and dz, dż, dź count as one sound.

ex.explain: Ł ł: w as in "water" – łódź.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and its sound

lessons.title: How Polish sounds
lessons.rule: Polish is written the way it is spoken. Some letter pairs make one sound, and a few letters have little marks that change them.
lessons.structure: sz → sh | cz → ch | rz, ż → zh (as in "measure") | w → v | ł → w | c → ts | ó → u
lessons.tip: The stress is almost always on the second-to-last syllable.

ex.prompt: Match the spelling and the sound

lessons.title: Cześć! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: Say your name with "mam na imię" (literally "I have as a name") and where you are from with "jestem z".
lessons.structure: Mam na imię … | Jestem z … | Miło mi!
lessons.tip: With strangers use Pan (man) or Pani (woman): "Jak Pani ma na imię?"

ex.prompt: My name is Piotr. → Mam na ___ Piotr.
ex.explain: Mam na imię … = my name is …

lessons.title: Greetings
lessons.rule: 'Cześć' is casual (hi and bye). 'Dzień dobry' is polite and works all day until the evening.
lessons.structure: Cześć · Dzień dobry · Dobry wieczór · Dziękuję · Proszę · Do widzenia
lessons.tip: Pronunciation: cz like 'ch', ę nasal, ł like English w.

ex.explain: Jak się masz? = How are you?

lessons.more: Dzień dobry is used during the day with anyone you address formally, Dobry wieczór from the evening. Cześć is casual and means both 'hi' and 'bye'. Proszę is versatile: please / here you are, you're welcome, and 'pardon?' (Proszę?). Formal address uses Pan (sir) and Pani (madam) + 3rd person: Czy Pan ma czas?

lessons.title: być: to be
lessons.rule: 'być' is irregular. The pronoun is usually dropped because the ending shows the person.
lessons.structure: jestem · jesteś · jest · jesteśmy · jesteście · są
lessons.tip: 'To jest …' means 'This is …'. Polish has no articles.
lessons.more: The subject pronoun is usually dropped: Jestem z Zurychu. After być a noun takes the instrumental (Jestem studentem), but an adjective stays in the nominative (Jestem zmęczony). With 'to' you can introduce without the instrumental: To jest Anna. Polite: Pan jest / Pani jest.

lessons.title: Three genders
lessons.rule: Masculine usually ends in a consonant, feminine in -a, neuter in -o, -e or -ę.
lessons.structure: ten dom (m) · ta kawa (f) · to okno (n)
lessons.tip: Possessives agree: mój dom, moja kawa, moje okno.
lessons.more: You can tell the gender by the ending: consonant = masculine (dom), -a = feminine (kawa), -o, -e, -ę, -um = neuter (okno, morze, imię, muzeum). Men in -a stay masculine: mężczyzna, kolega. Words in -ść are feminine: miłość, kość. ten, ta, to mean 'this'.

reading.title: Cześć, jestem Ola
reading.text: **Cześć!** **Jestem** Ola. **Jestem** z Krakowa, ale teraz mieszkam w Zurychu. **To** **jest** **mój** kot. **Ten** kot **jest** bardzo leniwy. **Dziękuję** za uwagę!
reading.tr: Hi! I'm Ola. I'm from Kraków, but now I live in Zurich. This is my cat. This cat is very lazy. Thanks for your attention!

lessons.title: mieć: to have
lessons.rule: 'mieć' (to have) belongs to the group with -m, -sz. After a negation the object is in the genitive.
lessons.structure: mam · masz · ma · mamy · macie · mają  |  nie mam czasu = I have no time
lessons.tip: czas (time) becomes czasu after 'nie'. That is the genitive.

ex.explain: The affirmative form ty masz takes czas.

lessons.more: mieć has the endings -m, -sz, -, -my, -cie, -ją, like many verbs. After a negation use the genitive: Mam czas → Nie mam czasu. Useful expressions: mieć ochotę na (to feel like), mieć rację (to be right), mieć na imię (to be called). Age is given with mieć: Mam 30 lat.

lessons.title: Verbs in -ać
lessons.rule: Many verbs in -ać conjugate like mieć: -am, -asz, -a, -amy, -acie, -ają.
lessons.structure: czytać: czytam · czytasz · czyta · czytamy · czytacie · czytają
examples: We are waiting for the bus.
lessons.tip: Same pattern: mieszkać (to live), czekać (to wait), grać (to play).
lessons.more: Verbs in -ać belong to the easiest group (-m, -sz): czytam, czytasz. Likewise: mieszkać, słuchać, pytać, grać. Polish stress almost always falls on the second-to-last syllable: czy-TA-my, czy-TA-cie.

lessons.title: Feminine accusative
lessons.rule: As a direct object feminine nouns in -a change their ending to -ę.
lessons.structure: kawa → kawę · książka → książkę · herbata → herbatę
lessons.tip: Masculine things and neuter nouns stay the same in the accusative: Mam dom, mam okno.
lessons.more: The accusative marks the direct object. Feminine words in -a take -ę: kawa → kawę. Feminine words ending in a consonant and neuter words stay the same. Masculine words for things stay the same (Mam dom); for people and animals they take -a: Mam brata, Widzę psa.

reading.title: Niedziela
reading.text: W niedzielę **mam** czas. Rano **czytam** gazetę i **piję** **kawę**. Mój mąż **słucha** muzyki. Dzieci **grają** w ogrodzie. **Nie mam** ochoty gotować, więc jemy w restauracji.
reading.tr: On Sunday I have time. In the morning I read the paper and drink coffee. My husband listens to music. The children play in the garden. I don't feel like cooking, so we eat at a restaurant.

lessons.title: Verbs in -ić / -yć
lessons.rule: Verbs in -ić and -yć form their own group: -ę, -isz/-ysz, -i/-y, -imy/-ymy, -icie/-ycie, -ą.
lessons.structure: robić: robię, robisz, robi, robimy, robicie, robią · mówić: mówię, mówisz, mówi ... · uczyć: uczę, uczysz, uczy ...
lessons.tip: 'po polsku', 'po niemiecku' means in Polish, in German.
lessons.more: Verbs in -ić and -yć have the endings -ę, -isz/-ysz, -i/-y, -imy, -icie, -ią/-ą. Watch out for sound changes: chodzić → chodzę, płacić → płacę, prosić → proszę. After cz, sz, rz, ż use y instead of i: uczysz, tańczysz.

lessons.title: Verbs in -ować
lessons.rule: In verbs in -ować, -ować becomes -uj- + ending in the present.
lessons.structure: pracować: pracuję, pracujesz, pracuje, pracujemy, pracujecie, pracują · kupować · studiować · gotować
lessons.tip: This is one of the biggest groups: almost all loanwords in -ować follow the pattern.
lessons.more: In all verbs in -ować, -ować becomes -uj- in the present: pracować → pracuję. This is one of the most reliable rules in Polish. Many loanwords belong here: studiować, organizować, telefonować, akceptować.

lessons.title: Negation with genitive
lessons.rule: After a negated verb the object is in the genitive instead of the accusative. Feminine -a → -y/-i, masculine and neuter usually -a or -u.
lessons.structure: Mam siostrę → Nie mam siostry. · Piję kawę → Nie piję kawy. · Mam samochód → Nie mam samochodu. · Mam czas → Nie mam czasu.
lessons.tip: After k and g you write -i: książka → nie ma książki.

ex.prompt: Translate: I don't have a car.

lessons.more: After a negation the direct object becomes genitive. Feminine -a → -y/-i (kawy, herbaty, książki). Masculine usually -u for things (samochodu, czasu) and -a for people and many objects (brata, chleba, psa). Neuter -o/-e → -a (okna). This also applies to 'nie ma' (there isn't): Nie ma mleka.

lessons.title: Plural of nouns
lessons.rule: Most masculine and feminine nouns take -y, after k and g -i. Neuter nouns take -a.
lessons.structure: kot → koty · kobieta → kobiety · książka → książki · okno → okna · dziecko → dzieci (irregular)
lessons.tip: Masculine persons have their own plurals: student → studenci, Polak → Polacy.
lessons.more: Plural: masculine and feminine mostly -y; after k, g and soft consonants -i or -e: koty, książki, pokoje. Neuter: -a (okna, morza). Male persons have their own form: student → studenci, Polak → Polacy. Irregular: dziecko → dzieci, człowiek → ludzie, rok → lata.

lessons.title: Adjective agreement
lessons.rule: Adjectives agree with the noun: masculine -y/-i, feminine -a, neuter -e. They usually come before the noun.
lessons.structure: nowy dom · nowa szkoła · nowe okno · tani / tania / tanie · drogi / droga / drogie
lessons.tip: After k and g the masculine form ends in -i: wielki, drogi.
lessons.more: Adjectives agree and usually come before the noun: nowy dom. Basic forms: -y/-i (m), -a (f), -e (n). After k and g use -i: drogi, tani. In the plural there are two forms: -e for everything except male persons (nowe domy, nowe kobiety), and a special form for men (nowi studenci, dobrzy ludzie).

reading.title: Nowe mieszkanie
reading.text: **Pracuję** w banku i **kupuję** nowe mieszkanie. Mieszkanie jest **małe**, ale **tanie**. **Nie ma** **windy** i **nie mam** **balkonu**. Mam za to dwa **duże** **okna**. Sąsiedzi **mówią**, że okolica jest **cicha**.
reading.tr: I work at a bank and I'm buying a new flat. The flat is small but cheap. There's no lift and I don't have a balcony. But I do have two big windows. The neighbours say the area is quiet.

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 100
lessons.rule: After 2, 3 and 4 the noun stands in the nominative plural (dwa koty), after 5 and more in the genitive plural (pięć kotów). Jeden and dwa change with gender: jedna kawa, dwie kawy.
lessons.structure: jeden, dwa, trzy, cztery, pięć … dziesięć | jedenaście, dwanaście … dwadzieścia | trzydzieści · czterdzieści · pięćdziesiąt · sto
lessons.tip: Age uses mieć: mam 20 lat.

lessons.title: The time and days
lessons.rule: Ask "Która godzina?". Polish uses ordinal numbers for the hours: jest pierwsza (1:00), jest druga (2:00). "At" a time is o + locative: o ósmej. Half past uses the next hour: wpół do dziewiątej = 8:30. Days and months are written in lower case.
lessons.structure: Jest pierwsza · Jest druga · o ósmej · wpół do dziewiątej (8:30) | w poniedziałek · w maju
lessons.tip: On a day: w + accusative — w poniedziałek, w sobotę.

lessons.title: instrumental after być
lessons.rule: After być (to be) a noun is in the instrumental: profession, nationality, role. Masculine and neuter: -em, feminine: -ą.
lessons.structure: Jestem nauczycielem. · Ona jest lekarką. · On jest studentem. · Jestem Niemcem / Niemką.
lessons.tip: With 'to jest' the nominative stays: To jest student. But: On jest studentem.
lessons.more: After być, professions, nationalities and roles take the instrumental: Jestem lekarzem. Masculine and neuter: -em (nauczycielem, studentem). Feminine: -ą (lekarką, Polką). With 'to' it stays nominative: To jest lekarz. Adjectives alone stay nominative: On jest wysoki.

lessons.title: Locative: w and na
lessons.rule: For the question where? (gdzie?) the locative follows w and na. Common endings: -e (with consonant change) or -u.
lessons.structure: Warszawa → w Warszawie · Kraków → w Krakowie · szkoła → w szkole · dom → w domu · praca → w pracy · uniwersytet → na uniwersytecie
examples: I work at the post office.
lessons.tip: Before the -e consonants often change: t → ci, d → dzi, r → rz, k → c (w Polsce).
lessons.more: The locative follows w, na, o and przy. Common ending: -e, often with a sound change: Warszawa → w Warszawie, szkoła → w szkole, miasto → w mieście. After k, g, ch and in many words -u: w domu, w parku. Feminine after soft consonants or -ja: -i: w pracy, w kuchni, w Polsce (exception).

lessons.title: mój, moja, moje
lessons.rule: Possessive pronouns agree with the gender of the thing owned. jego (his), jej (her) and ich (their) never change.
lessons.structure: mój brat · moja siostra · moje dziecko · twój / twoja / twoje · nasz / nasza / nasze · wasz / wasza / wasze
lessons.tip: For the subject's own possession there is swój: Kocham swoją żonę (my own wife).
lessons.more: The possessive agrees like an adjective: mój brat, moja siostra, moje dziecko. For 'his', 'her' and 'their' there are invariable forms: jego, jej, ich: jego mama, jej brat. When it refers back to the subject use swój: Kocham swoją pracę.

lessons.title: Dative: podoba mi się
lessons.rule: 'To like' is formed with the dative of the person: podoba mi się (it pleases me). In the plural: podobają.
lessons.structure: mi · ci · mu · jej · nam · wam · im + podoba się / podobają się
lessons.tip: lubić (to like) is a normal verb with the accusative: Lubię kawę.
lessons.more: podobać się works like 'to please': the thing that pleases is the subject and the person is in the dative: Podoba mi się ten film, Podobają mi się te buty. For food and habits Polish usually uses lubić (to like) + accusative: Lubię kawę. Stressed dative forms: mnie, tobie, jemu.

lessons.title: Numbers 2 to 4 and from 5
lessons.rule: After 2, 3, 4 the nominative plural is used. From 5 the genitive plural is used. With feminine nouns 2 is dwie.
lessons.structure: dwa koty · trzy koty · cztery koty · pięć kotów · dwie kawy · pięć kaw · sześć lat
lessons.tip: From 5 the verb is also singular: Pięć osób przyszło.
lessons.more: After 2, 3, 4 (and 22, 23, 24 ...) use the nominative plural: dwa koty. From 5 (and 11 to 21) use the genitive plural: pięć kotów. For feminine words 2 is 'dwie': dwie kawy. For years: rok, dwa lata, pięć lat. Groups of men have special forms: dwóch studentów.

reading.title: Moja praca
reading.text: **Jestem** **nauczycielką**. Pracuję **w szkole** **w Warszawie**. **Moja** szkoła jest stara. **Podoba mi się** moja praca. Mam **pięć** **klas** i **dwóch** kolegów, **którzy** też uczą angielskiego.
reading.tr: I'm a teacher. I work at a school in Warsaw. My school is old. I like my job. I have five classes and two colleagues who also teach English.

lessons.title: past
lessons.rule: The past tense: stem + -ł (masculine) / -ła (feminine) + personal ending. The ending shows person and gender.
lessons.structure: być: byłem / byłam · byłeś / byłaś · był / była · byliśmy / byłyśmy · byliście / byłyście · byli / były
examples: Yesterday I was at the cinema. (man)
What did you do? (to a woman)
lessons.tip: byli is used as soon as there is a man in the group. były only for women or things.
lessons.more: The past tense distinguishes gender: a man says byłem, a woman byłam. In the plural there's one form for groups with at least one man (byliśmy) and one for everyone else (byłyśmy). Formation: stem + ł/ła/ło + person ending: czytałem, czytałaś, czytał.

lessons.title: Aspect
lessons.rule: Almost every verb has a pair: imperfective (process, repetition) and perfective (result, one-off). Often with a prefix.
lessons.structure: robić / zrobić · czytać / przeczytać · pisać / napisać · kupować / kupić · pić / wypić
lessons.tip: Signal words: codziennie, często, długo → imperfective. już, w końcu → often perfective.
lessons.more: Almost every verb has a pair: imperfective (process, repetition) and perfective (one-time result). Czytałem książkę = I was reading the book. Przeczytałem książkę = I finished the book. Perfective verbs have no present: their present form means future (zrobię = I'll get it done).

lessons.title: future
lessons.rule: Imperfective: będę + infinitive (or + past form). Perfective: the present form is already the future.
lessons.structure: będę, będziesz, będzie, będziemy, będziecie, będą + pracować · perfective: zrobię, kupisz, napisze
examples: What are you going to do?
lessons.tip: Never będę + perfective verb: 'będę zrobić' is wrong.
lessons.more: For imperfective verbs the future is będę + infinitive or będę + past form: będę pracować or będę pracował(a). Perfective verbs are simply conjugated in the present: kupię (I will buy). będę + perfective verb is wrong.

lessons.title: Verbs with się
lessons.rule: Reflexive verbs have the word się. It never comes first in the sentence and usually follows the verb or the first word.
lessons.structure: uczyć się: uczę się, uczysz się, uczy się, uczymy się, uczycie się, uczą się · nazywać się · myć się
lessons.tip: się stays the same for all persons.

ex.explain: się never comes first in the sentence.

lessons.more: się is the same for all persons and moves freely in the sentence, often after the first stressed word: Jak się nazywasz? Uczę się polskiego. Many verbs have się without being reflexive in English: bać się (to be afraid), śmiać się (to laugh), podobać się (to please).

lessons.title: Imperative
lessons.rule: The imperative is formed from the 3rd person present, usually without an ending. Plural: + -cie. Polite: proszę + infinitive.
lessons.structure: czytać → czytaj / czytajcie · robić → rób / róbcie · mówić → mów · iść → idź · Proszę usiąść.
lessons.tip: The negative imperative usually uses imperfective verbs: Nie rób tego!
lessons.more: The imperative is formed from the 3rd person plural without the ending: czytają → czytaj, robią → rób. For wy add -cie: czytajcie, róbcie. Politely to strangers use proszę + infinitive: Proszę usiąść. Proszę wejść. Negative: Nie rób tego!

reading.title: Wakacje nad morzem
reading.text: Latem **byłam** nad morzem. **Pływałam** codziennie i **przeczytałam** trzy książki. Mój brat **był** ze mną. W przyszłym roku **będziemy** **jechać** w góry. **Pojedziemy** pociągiem. Już **uczę się** trasy na pamięć!
reading.tr: In summer I was at the seaside. I swam every day and read three books. My brother was with me. Next year we're going to the mountains. We'll go by train. I'm already learning the route by heart!

lessons.title: chcieć and móc
lessons.rule: chcieć (to want) and móc (can) are irregular. They are followed by the infinitive.
lessons.structure: chcieć: chcę, chcesz, chce, chcemy, chcecie, chcą · móc: mogę, możesz, może, możemy, możecie, mogą
lessons.tip: Polite: Chciałbym / Chciałabym (I would like).
lessons.more: chcieć and móc take an infinitive: Chcę spać, Mogę pomóc. To ask politely use the conditional: Chciałbym (man) / Chciałabym (woman) kawę. Czy mogę ...? is the usual way to ask permission: Czy mogę zapłacić kartą?

lessons.title: gdzie, dokąd, skąd
lessons.rule: gdzie asks for the place, dokąd for the direction, skąd for the origin (z + genitive).
lessons.structure: Gdzie jesteś? W domu. · Dokąd idziesz? Do domu. · Skąd jesteś? Z Niemiec / ze Szwajcarii.
lessons.tip: Direction towards buildings and cities: do + genitive: do szkoły, do Krakowa.

ex.explain: Use skąd to ask where someone is from.

lessons.more: gdzie (where?) takes w/na + locative: w domu, na poczcie. dokąd (where to?) takes do + genitive or na + accusative: do domu, do Polski, na pocztę. skąd (where from?) takes z + genitive: z domu, z Polski, ze Szwajcarii. Before difficult consonant clusters z becomes ze.

lessons.title: Comparative
lessons.rule: Comparative with -szy, superlative with naj- in front. Some forms are irregular. 'than' is niż.
lessons.structure: tani → tańszy → najtańszy · nowy → nowszy · dobry → lepszy → najlepszy · zły → gorszy · duży → większy · mały → mniejszy
examples: That is the best pizza in town.
lessons.tip: Long adjectives: bardziej + adjective: bardziej interesujący.
lessons.more: Comparative: stem + -szy or -ejszy, often with a sound change: tani → tańszy, ładny → ładniejszy. Superlative: naj- + comparative: najtańszy. With long adjectives: bardziej / najbardziej + adjective: bardziej interesujący. Then use 'niż' or od + genitive: starszy niż ja = starszy ode mnie.

lessons.title: z + instrumental
lessons.rule: After z (with) the instrumental is used: masculine and neuter -em, feminine -ą, plural -ami.
lessons.structure: brat → z bratem · mama → z mamą · mleko → z mlekiem · przyjaciele → z przyjaciółmi · ja → ze mną · ty → z tobą
examples: I'm going to the cinema with my sister.
lessons.tip: z with the genitive means from instead: z Polski.
lessons.more: After z (with) use the instrumental. Masculine and neuter: -em (z bratem, z mlekiem). Feminine: -ą (z mamą, z siostrą). Plural: -ami (z dziećmi and z przyjaciółmi are irregular). Without a preposition the instrumental shows the means of transport: jechać autobusem, pociągiem.

lessons.title: który
lessons.rule: który introduces relative clauses. It agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to.
lessons.structure: człowiek, który ... · kobieta, która ... · dziecko, które ... · ludzie, którzy ... · feminine accusative: którą
examples: To jest kolega, który mieszka w Gdańsku.
This is the colleague who lives in Gdańsk.
The book I am reading is exciting.
Ludzie, którzy tu pracują, są mili.
The people who work here are nice.
lessons.tip: There is always a comma before który.

ex.prompt: Translate: The film that is good.

lessons.more: który agrees in gender and number with the word it refers to; its case depends on its role in the clause: Kobieta, którą znam (accusative). Dom, w którym mieszkam (locative). Plural: którzy for male persons, które for everything else. A comma always comes before który.

reading.title: Gdańsk czy Kraków?
reading.text: Kraków jest **starszy niż** Gdańsk, ale Gdańsk jest **większy**. **Dokąd** pojechać? **Do** Krakowa, jeśli lubisz historię. **Skąd** najlepszy widok? **Z** wieży kościoła. **Chcę** tam wrócić **z** **przyjaciółmi**. **Jedź**, nie pożałujesz!
reading.tr: Kraków is older than Gdańsk, but Gdańsk is bigger. Where to go? To Kraków if you like history. Where's the best view from? From the church tower. I want to go back with friends. Go, you won't regret it!

lessons.title: Conditional: -bym
lessons.rule: For wishes, requests and unreal conditions use the past form + by + person ending: zrobiłbym, zrobiłabyś. The if-clause uses gdyby: Gdybym miał czas, przyszedłbym.
lessons.structure: chciałbym / chciałabym · mógłbyś / mogłabyś · byłby · Gdybym był bogaty, kupiłbym dom.
examples: I'd like to order a coffee.
Could you help me? (to a woman)
Gdybym miał czas, pojechałbym w góry.
If I had time, I'd go to the mountains.
lessons.tip: The ending shows the speaker's gender: a man says chciałbym, a woman chciałabym.

ex.prompt: Translate (woman): I would like to travel.

lessons.more: Real conditions don't need by: Jeśli będę miał czas, przyjdę. żeby + past form expresses a wish for others: Chcę, żebyś przyszedł. With the same subject: żeby + infinitive: Uczę się, żeby zdać egzamin.

lessons.title: Verbs of motion: iść and chodzić
lessons.rule: Polish distinguishes a concrete movement now (iść, jechać) from regular or general movement (chodzić, jeździć). iść and chodzić mean to go on foot, jechać and jeździć to go by vehicle.
lessons.structure: idę, idziesz, idzie · chodzę, chodzisz, chodzi · jadę, jedziesz, jedzie · jeżdżę, jeździsz, jeździ
examples: I'm going to the shop now.
I go to the gym every day.
lessons.tip: Rule of thumb: on the way now → iść/jechać. Regularly, often, in general → chodzić/jeździć. By vehicle always jechać/jeździć, even for short trips.

ex.prompt: Translate: Tomorrow I'm going to Warsaw.

lessons.more: With prefixes the verbs become perfective: pójść, pojechać (to set off), przyjść, przyjechać (to arrive), wyjść, wyjechać (to go out, to leave). The past of iść is irregular: szedłem, szłam, szli.

lessons.title: genitive plural
lessons.rule: The genitive plural is needed after numbers from 5, after dużo, mało, ile and after negation. Masculine mostly -ów (kotów), feminine in -a and neuter in -o mostly zero ending (kaw, okien), words ending in soft consonants -i/-y (nocy, pokoi).
lessons.structure: kot → kotów · dom → domów · kawa → kaw · książka → książek · okno → okien · noc → nocy · ludzie → ludzi · pięć kotów, dużo książek
examples: I have a lot of friends.
W tym mieście nie ma muzeów.
There are no museums in this town.
lessons.tip: Zero-ending words often add an e or change the vowel: książka → książek, okno → okien, ręka → rąk.
lessons.more: Numbers overview: 1 + nominative singular (jeden kot), 2 to 4 + nominative plural (dwa koty), from 5 + genitive plural (pięć kotów). Irregular: rok → lat, dziecko → dzieci, człowiek → ludzi (but pięciu ludzi).

lessons.title: żeby: purpose and wish
lessons.rule: żeby means 'so that' or 'in order to'. With the same subject it takes the infinitive: Uczę się, żeby zdać egzamin. With a different subject it takes the past form with person ending: Chcę, żebyś przyszedł.
lessons.structure: żeby + infinitive · żebym, żebyś, żeby, żebyśmy, żebyście, żeby + past form · Chcę, żebyś wiedział.
examples: I want you to help me.
lessons.tip: The person ending attaches to żeby; the verb is in the 3rd person past: żebyś przyszedł (man), żebyś przyszła (woman).

ex.prompt: Uczę się polskiego, ___ rozmawiać z babcią.

lessons.more: Difference: że introduces a fact (Wiem, że jesteś zmęczony), żeby a wish or purpose (Chcę, żebyś odpoczął). After prosić, kazać, mówić (meaning to tell someone to) use żeby: Prosił, żebym zadzwonił.

reading.title: Nowa praca
reading.text: Od miesiąca **jeżdżę** do pracy rowerem. Dziś **jadę** autobusem, bo pada. Szef chce, **żebym** **zrobił** prezentację. **Gdybym** **miał** więcej czasu, **przygotowałbym** ją lepiej. W biurze pracuje **dwudziestu** ludzi i mamy **dużo** **projektów**.
reading.tr: For a month I've been cycling to work. Today I'm taking the bus because it's raining. My boss wants me to give a presentation. If I had more time, I'd prepare it better. Twenty people work in the office and we have lots of projects.

lessons.title: The vocative case
lessons.rule: Use the vocative when you address someone directly. Feminine -a becomes -o, many masculine nouns add -e or -u. Pan and pani become panie and pani.
lessons.structure: Anna → Anno! · mama → mamo! · Piotr → Piotrze! · pan → panie
lessons.tip: In casual speech people often use the nominative of first names, but the vocative is always polite.

ex.prompt: Match the nominative with the vocative.

lessons.title: swój: one’s own
lessons.rule: Swój refers to the subject of the clause and replaces mój, twój, jego, jej when the owner is the subject. It declines like an adjective.
lessons.structure: Mam swój pokój. · On kocha swoją żonę.
lessons.tip: Jego and jej point to someone other than the subject.

ex.prompt: Say that she loves her (own) job.

lessons.title: The passive: jest robiony, został zrobiony
lessons.rule: Form the passive with być or zostać + passive participle. Być describes a state or ongoing process; zostać describes a completed action.
lessons.structure: Dom jest budowany. · Dom został zbudowany w 2010.
examples: The shop is opened at eight.
The book was written by Szymborska.
lessons.tip: The agent is introduced with przez + accusative.

ex.prompt: Say the window was broken yesterday.

lessons.title: Impersonal forms: mówi się, można
lessons.rule: Polish expresses general statements with się + 3rd person singular, or with -no/-to forms in the past. Można (one can) and trzeba (one must) take an infinitive.
lessons.structure: Tu się nie pali. · Mówi się, że … · Zrobiono to wczoraj.
examples: W Polsce je się dużo zup.
People eat a lot of soup in Poland.
lessons.tip: The -no/-to form (zrobiono, powiedziano) is common in news and formal writing.

ex.explain: Mówi się, że … = people say that …

reading.title: Stary dom
reading.text: **Babciu**, kiedy ten dom **został zbudowany**? – pyta Kasia. – W 1935 roku. **Mówi się**, że był to najładniejszy dom we wsi. Dziadek kochał **swój** ogród. Dziś **trzeba** go odnowić, ale **można** tu jeszcze mieszkać.
reading.tr: “Grandma, when was this house built?” asks Kasia. “In 1935. People say it was the most beautiful house in the village. Grandpa loved his garden. Today it needs renovating, but you can still live here.”

ex.prompt: Which word is in the vocative?

lessons.title: Using adverbial participles precisely
lessons.rule: Forms in -ąc normally describe a simultaneous action. Forms such as przeczytawszy present a completed prior action and are more formal. The two actions generally share a subject.
lessons.structure: czytając → simultaneous · przeczytawszy → completed earlier
examples: While reading the report, Anna took notes.
After reading the report, Anna sent her comments.
lessons.tip: An explicit subordinate clause is clearer if the two actions have different actors.

ex.prompt: Which sentence makes the reviewer the actor of both actions?
options: Czytając raport, recenzent zaznaczał wątpliwe fragmenty.
ex.explain: Recenzent is the subject and can both read and mark passages.

ex.prompt: What happened first in „Podpisawszy umowę, Marta zadzwoniła do prawnika“?
ex.explain: Podpisawszy sets up the completed action that preceded the call.

lessons.title: Choosing case inside a relative clause
lessons.rule: Który takes its gender and number from the noun it describes. Its case comes from its role within the relative clause, including any preposition required by the verb.
lessons.structure: zależeć od → od którego · polegać na → na którym
examples: To dostawca, na którym można polegać.
This is a supplier you can rely on.
To decyzja, od której zależy wynik.
This is the decision the result depends on.
lessons.tip: Work out the preposition and case from inside the relative clause before checking the antecedent’s gender and number.

ex.prompt: Complete: „To dokument, do ___ odnosi się załącznik.“
ex.explain: Do takes the genitive, and dokument is masculine singular.

ex.prompt: Supply only the missing relative pronoun. „To umowa, o ___ rozmawialiśmy.“
ex.explain: Rozmawiać o takes the locative, and umowa is feminine singular.

lessons.title: Expressing conditions and exceptions
lessons.rule: Chyba że introduces an exception to a default. O ile can introduce a condition that must hold. Reading the relationship correctly is essential when paraphrasing rules.
lessons.structure: default + chyba że + exception · result + o ile + condition
examples: Spotkanie odbędzie się w piątek, chyba że zabraknie kworum.
The meeting will take place on Friday unless there is no quorum.
Wniosek zostanie rozpatrzony, o ile wpłynie w terminie.
The application will be considered provided it arrives on time.
lessons.tip: When checking a rule, ask what happens in the ordinary case and what changes it.

ex.prompt: What does „Opłatę pobiera się, chyba że wniosek zostanie wycofany“ mean?
options: The fee is charged only if the application is withdrawn.
The fee is charged by default, with an exception for withdrawal.
ex.explain: Chyba że introduces the situation in which the default no longer applies.

ex.prompt: Which version makes approval a condition for publication?
options: Opublikujemy tekst, mimo że redakcja go nie zatwierdziła.
Opublikujemy tekst bez względu na decyzję redakcji.
Opublikujemy tekst, o ile redakcja go zatwierdzi.
ex.explain: O ile sets editorial approval as the condition.

lessons.title: Acknowledging a point before qualifying it
lessons.rule: Co prawda signals an acknowledgement that will often be followed by a qualification. Trudno uznać offers a restrained way of challenging a description or conclusion.
lessons.structure: co prawda X, jednak Y · trudno uznać X za Y
examples: Co prawda próba była mała, jednak wyniki są spójne.
Admittedly the sample was small, but the results are consistent.
Trudno uznać tę poprawkę za wystarczającą.
It is hard to regard this amendment as sufficient.
lessons.tip: The clause after jednak often carries the main point. Preserve that emphasis when you summarise.

ex.prompt: What is the main reservation in „Co prawda projekt jest tani, jednak jego utrzymanie będzie kosztowne“?
options: The project is expensive to start.
ex.explain: Jednak introduces the contrast and shifts the focus to maintenance.

ex.prompt: Which reply diplomatically questions whether the evidence is sufficient?
options: Trudno uznać te dane za rozstrzygające.
Te dane rozstrzygają sprawę bez żadnych wątpliwości.
Nie ma sensu z wami rozmawiać.
ex.explain: The phrasing limits the criticism to what the evidence can establish.

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The Zurich German alphabet
lessons.rule: Zurich German uses the German alphabet, but many words sound different from Standard German. The throaty ch is everywhere, and k is often said with a little "kch".
lessons.structure: ch = throaty kh (Chuchi) | k = kch | ä = open, like "cat" | ie, ue, üe = two sounds
lessons.tip: Swiss German has no fixed spelling: people write it the way they speak, so spellings can vary.

ex.explain: Ch ch: throaty kh as in "loch" – Chuchi.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and its sound

lessons.title: How Zurich German sounds
lessons.rule: Zurich German has no fixed spelling: people write it the way they speak. ch is always throaty, long vowels are often doubled, and ie, ue, üe are two sounds in a row.
lessons.structure: ch → throaty, like "Bach" (Chind) | uu, aa → long vowels (Huus) | ue → u + e (guet) | üe → ü + e (Grüezi)
examples: child: throaty ch at the start
lessons.tip: Spoken Swiss German never uses ß. In writing, Swiss people use ss: heisse.

ex.prompt: In Zurich German, "ch" at the start (Chind) sounds…
Match the word and its meaning

lessons.title: Hoi! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: Say your name with "ich heisse" and where you are from with "ich chume us".
lessons.structure: Ich heisse … | Ich chume us … | Freut mi!
lessons.tip: Say Grüezi to strangers and Hoi to friends.

ex.prompt: My name is Sara. → Ich ___ Sara.

lessons.title: Grüezi and Hoi
lessons.rule: Strangers and older people are greeted with 'Grüezi', friends with 'Hoi' or 'Sali'. When leaving you say 'Uf Widerluege' or 'Tschüss'.
lessons.structure: Grüezi (mitenand) · Hoi / Sali · Merci vilmal · Uf Widerluege · Tschüss / Ciao
lessons.tip: 'Merci' is the normal thank you. 'Danke' is understood too, but 'Merci' sounds more like Zurich.

ex.prompt: You greet a shop assistant you don't know:
ex.explain: Use Grüezi to greet people you do not know.
Use mitenand when addressing several people.

ex.prompt: Write 'How are you?' in Swiss German:

lessons.more: In Switzerland people greet strangers too, in shops, in the lift and when hiking. 'Grüezi' is for one person, 'Grüezi mitenand' for several. Among colleagues and younger people it is almost always 'Hoi' or 'Sali'. Goodbye: 'Uf Widerluege' (formal), 'Tschüss', 'Ciao' or 'Adie'.

lessons.title: sii: to be
lessons.rule: The verb 'sii' (to be) is shorter than in Standard German. In the plural all persons have the same form.
lessons.structure: ich bi · du bisch · er/si/es isch · mir sind · ihr sind · si sind
lessons.tip: 'mir' means 'we' here. So 'Mir sind' = 'We are'.
lessons.more: 'sii' is often shortened and attached to the next word: 'Wo bisch?' instead of 'Wo bisch du?'. The pronoun is often dropped completely in questions. In the plural there is only one form for all persons: mir, ihr and si sind. This is a key pattern of Zurich German.

lessons.title: de, d, s
lessons.rule: The definite articles are de (masculine), d (feminine) and s (neuter). Use en, e and es for the corresponding indefinite articles. The plural definite article is d.
lessons.structure: de Maa · d Frau · s Chind · en Maa · e Frau · es Chind · plural: d Chind
lessons.tip: Typical Zurich words: s Velo (bicycle), s Trottoir (pavement), s Rüebli (carrot).
lessons.more: The feminine article 'd' merges with the word: 'd Frau' sounds almost like 'tFrau'. Before a vowel 's' is attached directly: 's Auto'. The indefinite article is 'en' (masculine), 'e' (feminine) and 'es' (neuter): en Maa, e Frau, es Chind.

reading.title: At the café
reading.text: **Grüezi mitenand!** Ich **bi** de Marco. Ich **bi** us Züri. **D** Serviceangestellti seit: '**Grüezi**, was **hetted** Si gärn?' Ich säg: 'Es Kafi, bitte.' Und mini Fründin seit: 'Für mich au. **Merci vilmal**!'
reading.tr: Hello everyone! I'm Marco. I'm from Zurich. The waitress says: 'Good day, what would you like?' I say: 'A coffee, please.' And my girlfriend says: 'Same for me. Thank you very much!'

lessons.title: haa: to have
lessons.rule: 'haa' (to have) is short too. Again one form for all persons in the plural.
lessons.structure: ich ha · du häsch · er/si/es hät · mir händ · ihr händ · si händ
lessons.tip: Before a vowel people often say 'han': Ich han en Hund.
lessons.more: Before a vowel 'ha' becomes 'han': 'Ich han es Auto'. In questions the pronoun is attached: 'Häsch' (have you), 'Händ ihr'. For the perfect you need 'haa' just like in Standard German: Ich ha gässe.

lessons.title: Diminutive with -li
lessons.rule: With '-li' you make things small or cute. The word always becomes neuter, and a, o, u often become ä, ö, ü.
lessons.structure: s Huus → s Hüüsli · d Chatz → s Chätzli · de Hund → s Hündli
examples: A small piece of chocolate, please.
lessons.tip: 'Chuchichäschtli' is the famous test word. It simply means little kitchen cupboard.

ex.explain: Chuchi means kitchen and Chäschtli means little cabinet.

lessons.more: The diminutive is much more common in Swiss German than in Standard German and often just sounds friendly, not necessarily small: es Kafi, es Gipfeli, es Müntschi (kiss). Some words exist almost only in the -li form: Guetsli, Rüebli, Chüeli.

lessons.title: Zahle (numbers)
lessons.rule: The numbers sound different from Standard German. 'Two' traditionally has three forms depending on gender.
lessons.structure: eis · zwei · drü · vier · föif · sächs · sibe · acht · nüün · zää · elf · zwölf · zwee Manne · zwo Fraue · zwei Chind
lessons.tip: Today many people simply say 'zwei' for everything. With 'zwee' and 'zwo' you sound very Zurich.
lessons.more: The old form of 'two' depends on gender: zwee Manne, zwo Fraue, zwei Chind. Today many simply say 'zwei'. Bigger numbers: zwänzg (20), driissg (30), vierzg (40), füfzg (50), hundert (100). Twenty-one is 'einezwänzg'.

lessons.title: Uhrziit (telling the time)
lessons.rule: Telling the time has its own words: 'Viertel ab' (quarter past), 'halbi' (half) and 'Viertel vor' (quarter to). Hours often end in -i: drüü, vieri, föifi.
lessons.structure: Es isch drüü. · Viertel ab drüü (3:15) · halbi vieri (3:30) · Viertel vor vieri (3:45)
examples: Mir träffed üs am Viertel ab nüüni.
We meet at a quarter past nine.
lessons.tip: As in Standard German: 'halbi drüü' is 2:30, so half an hour BEFORE three.

ex.explain: Halbi points to the next hour, so halbi föifi is 4:30.

ex.prompt: Translate: It is half past six (6:30).
ex.explain: Use halbi with the next hour.

lessons.more: For hours you use a form with -i: eis, zwei, drüü, vieri, föifi, sächsi, sibni, achti, nüüni, zääni, elfi, zwölfi. 'Viertel ab' means quarter past. With 'am' you give the time: am drüü (at three).

lessons.title: Frogewörter (question words)
lessons.rule: The question words are similar to Standard German but sound different. 'Wieso' and 'wäge was' mean why.
lessons.structure: Was? · Wer? · Wo? · Wänn? · Wie? · Wieso? · Wohäre? (where to) · Vo wo? (where from) · Wie vill?
lessons.tip: In Zurich German 'where from' is usually asked with 'Vo wo?'.
lessons.more: In questions the pronouns attach to the verb: 'Wo wohnsch?' (Where do you live?), 'Was machsch?' (What are you doing?). 'Gäll?' or 'Oder?' at the end of a sentence means roughly 'isn't it?': Das isch guet, oder?

reading.title: S Wochenend (the weekend)
reading.text: Am Samschtig **han** ich Ziit. Ich **gaa** am Morge **go poschte**. Am Namittag **chunnt** mini Schwöschter. Mir **trinked** es Kafi und **ässed** es **Stück Chueche**. Am Abig **gönd** mir **is** Kino.
reading.tr: On Saturday I have time. In the morning I go shopping. In the afternoon my sister comes. We drink a coffee and eat a piece of cake. In the evening we go to the cinema.

ex.prompt: What does the person do in the morning?

lessons.title: gaa: to go
lessons.rule: 'gaa' (to go) is irregular and very common. Again there is only one form in the plural.
lessons.structure: ich gaa (gang) · du gaasch · er/si/es gaat · mir gönd · ihr gönd · si gönd
examples: We are going to the cinema.
lessons.tip: Instead of 'ich gaa' you often hear 'ich gang' in Zurich. Both are correct.
lessons.more: 'gaa' almost always comes with a direction: 'hei' (home), 'is Kino', 'uf Bärn'. With 'go' plus infinitive you say what you go to do: Ich gaa go poschte. The participle is 'gange': Ich bi gange.

lessons.title: choo: to come
lessons.rule: 'choo' (to come) starts with ch and has the stem 'chumm' in the singular and 'chöm' in the plural.
lessons.structure: ich chume · du chunnsch · er/si/es chunnt · mir chömed · ihr chömed · si chömed
lessons.tip: A Standard German k at the start of a word almost always becomes ch in Zurich German: Chind, Chuchi, Chäs.
lessons.more: 'choo' has the stem 'chumm' in the singular and 'chöm' in the plural. The participle is very short: 'cho'. With 'cho' plus infinitive you invite someone: Chunnsch cho ässe? (Are you coming to eat?).

lessons.title: One plural for all
lessons.rule: In Zurich German all three plural persons have the same ending: -ed. In the singular the endings are like Standard German.
lessons.structure: mache: ich mache · du machsch · er macht · mir mached · ihr mached · si mached
lessons.tip: The Standard German -st becomes -sch: du machsch, du trinksch, du wohnsch.
lessons.more: The single plural pattern is one of the biggest simplifications compared to Standard German. You only learn four forms: ich -e, du -sch, er -t and plural -ed. With 'ich' the -e is often dropped: ich mach, ich schaff.

lessons.title: nöd and kei
lessons.rule: Negation uses 'nöd' (not) and 'kei' (no, none). Add 'nüt' (nothing) and 'niemer' (nobody).
lessons.structure: Ich bi nöd müed. · Ich ha kei Ziit. · Ich weiss nüt. · Es isch niemer da.
lessons.tip: 'Nöd' is typical of Zurich. In Bern and Basel you hear 'nid' or 'nit'.
lessons.more: Like 'nicht', 'nöd' usually goes at the end of the sentence or before the word being negated. 'kei' hardly changes: kei Ziit, kei Hund, kei Auto. You sometimes hear double negation in casual speech: 'Ich ha nüt nöd gseh', but it is not standard.

lessons.title: Pronouns
lessons.rule: The personal pronouns are similar to Standard German. Important: 'wir' (we) is 'mir', 'uns' (us) is 'üs', 'euch' (you pl.) is 'eu'.
lessons.structure: Nominative: ich · du · er · si · es · mir · ihr · si · Dative: mir · dir · ihm · ire · üs · eu · ine
lessons.tip: Watch out: 'mir' can mean 'we' or 'me'. The sentence shows what is meant.
lessons.more: Unstressed pronouns are shortened and attached: 'Häsch es gseh?' becomes 'Häschs gseh?', 'Gib mir' becomes 'Gimmer'. 'si' can mean she, they or polite you. Polite 'Si' takes the plural form of the verb: Chömed Si au?

reading.title: Uf em Märt (at the market)
reading.text: Ich **gaa** mit **em** Tram uf **de** Märt. Dete chaufe ich **de** Chäs und **d** Rüebli. De Verchäufer seit: '**Wotsch** no öppis?' Ich säg: 'Nei, **das** isch alles. **Mis** Täschli isch scho voll.'
