reading.tr: I take the tram to the market. There I buy the cheese and the carrots. The seller says: 'Do you want anything else?' I say: 'No, that's all. My little bag is already full.'

ex.prompt: How does the person get to the market?
'Ich chaufe de Chäs': why 'de' and not 'den'?
options: The article does not change in the accusative

ex.prompt: Ich fahr mit ___ Tram. (neuter definite article after mit)

lessons.title: No accusative
lessons.rule: In Zurich German the nominative and accusative of the article are the same. 'den' simply becomes 'de'.
lessons.structure: De Hund schlaft. · Ich gseh de Hund. · Ich han en Hund. (en = a)
lessons.tip: That makes it easier for learners: only nominative and dative.

ex.explain: The masculine indefinite article is en.
The masculine definite article is de.
The masculine definite article is de.
The masculine definite article is de.

lessons.more: The article has no accusative: 'de' stays 'de', 'en' stays 'en'. Pronouns do have it: Ich gseh en (him), Ich gseh si (her). So for nouns you only need to learn the dative.

lessons.title: Dative: em and de
lessons.rule: The dative article is 'em' for masculine and neuter, 'de' for feminine and plural. Indefinite: 'emene' and 'ere'.
lessons.structure: mit em Zug · i de Stadt · bi de Lüüt · mit emene Fründ · mit ere Fründin
examples: She lives in the old town.
Ich gib em Chind es Guetsli.
I give the child a biscuit.
lessons.tip: After 'i' (in), 'mit' (with), 'bi' (at), 'vo' (from) the dative is used.

ex.prompt: Ich hilf ___ Mueter. (feminine definite article, dative)
Mir reded mit ___ Fründin. (feminine indefinite article, dative)

lessons.more: The dative is the only case you need to learn for the article. It follows prepositions like i (in), mit (with), bi (at), vo (from), uf (on, where?) and verbs like hälfe (help), gee (give), ghöre (belong). 'em' often sounds like 'im' or merges with the preposition: imene (in a).

lessons.title: min, mini, mis
lessons.rule: Possessives agree with gender: masculine 'min', feminine and plural 'mini', neuter 'mis'.
lessons.structure: min Vatter · mini Mueter · mis Auto · mini Chind · din / dini / dis · sin / sini / sis · üse / üsi / üses
lessons.tip: 'z Bärn' means in Bern. With place names people often say 'z' instead of 'in'.
lessons.more: The possessives follow the same pattern: masculine without ending (min), feminine and plural with -i (mini), neuter with -s (mis). In the dative: mim Vatter, minere Mueter, mim Chind. 'sin' (his) and 'ire' (her) work the same way.

lessons.title: go + infinitive
lessons.rule: After 'gaa' (go) and 'choo' (come) a little 'go' (or 'cho') comes before the infinitive. Standard German doesn't have this.
lessons.structure: Ich gaa go poschte. · Mir gönd go schwümme. · Chunnsch cho ässe?
examples: Are you coming for a coffee?
lessons.tip: 'poschte' means to go shopping, not to take something to the post.

ex.prompt: Translate: We are going to eat.

lessons.more: The little 'go' (after gaa) or 'cho' (after choo) comes before the infinitive and has no meaning of its own. It only shows: I go in order to do something. Typical verbs: go poschte, go schwümme, go ässe, go luege, go schaffe.

lessons.title: Relative clause with wo
lessons.rule: For all relative clauses you use 'wo', whether person or thing, masculine or feminine.
lessons.structure: de Maa, wo dete staat · d Frau, wo singt · s Buech, wo ich lise
examples: Das isch de Maa, wo mir ghulfe hät.
That is the man who helped me.
D Frau, wo dete wohnt, isch nett.
The woman who lives there is nice.
S Restaurant, wo mir gange sind, isch guet gsi.
The restaurant we went to was good.
lessons.tip: Use wo with people and things in relative clauses.

ex.prompt: D Lüüt, ___ do schaffed, sind nett.
S Auto, ___ ich gchauft han, isch rot.
Translate: The man who is coming.

lessons.more: Use wo to introduce a relative clause. When a preposition is needed, it can go at the end: S Huus, wo-n-ich drin wohne (the house I live in). The -n- is a linking sound before a vowel.

head: English meaning
Zurich German
rows: d Lüüt, wo-n-ich mit ine schaffe

reading.title: Es Telefon (a phone call)
reading.text: 'Hoi Lisa, **chasch** du morn **cho**? Mir **wänd** go wandere.' 'Ich **wott** scho, aber ich **mues** schaffe. Ich **cha** erscht am Sunntig.' 'Kei Problem, dänn **gömmer** am Sunntig. Ich **mues** nur no s Zugbillet chaufe.'
reading.tr: 'Hi Lisa, can you come tomorrow? We want to go hiking.' 'I'd like to, but I have to work. I can only on Sunday.' 'No problem, then we'll go on Sunday. I just need to buy the train ticket.'

ex.prompt: Wieso cha d Lisa morn nöd?

lessons.title: wele: to want
lessons.rule: 'wele' (to want) is very short in the singular: ich wott. In the plural: mir wänd.
lessons.structure: ich wott · du wotsch · er/si/es wott · mir wänd · ihr wänd · si wänd
lessons.tip: More polite than 'ich wott' is 'ich hett gärn' (I would like).
lessons.more: 'wele' means to want, but is often used for 'would like' too. The subjunctive sounds more polite: 'Ich wett gärn' or 'Ich hett gärn'. After 'wott' the infinitive goes at the end: Ich wott morn uf Bärn gaa.

lessons.title: chöne: can
lessons.rule: 'chöne' (can) starts with ch. Singular: cha, plural: chönd.
lessons.structure: ich cha · du chasch · er/si/es cha · mir chönd · ihr chönd · si chönd
lessons.tip: Ask politely with 'Chönnted Si ...?' (Could you ...?).

ex.prompt: Polite: ___ Si mir säge, wo de Bahnhof isch?

lessons.more: 'chöne' means can and may (colloquial): 'Cha-n-ich cho?' (Can/may I come?). Polite: 'Chönnted Si ...?' or 'Chöntsch ...?' (Could you ...?). The participle is 'chöne': Ich ha nöd chöne cho.

lessons.title: müese: must
lessons.rule: 'müese' (must) has the plural form 'müend' (often also 'münd').
lessons.structure: ich mues · du muesch · er/si/es mues · mir müend · ihr müend · si müend
examples: Do you still have to go today?
lessons.tip: 'pressiere' means to hurry, from French.
lessons.more: In the plural you hear both 'müend' and 'münd'. For 'don't have to' you say 'nöd müese': Du muesch nöd cho. For a prohibition use 'nöd törfe' (must not): Do törf mer nöd rauche.

lessons.title: Past without simple past
lessons.rule: Swiss German has no 'ich war' or 'ich ging'. The past is always told in the perfect.
lessons.structure: ich bi gsi (I was) · ich ha gässe (I ate) · ich bi gange (I went)
examples: Ich bi geschter z Bern gsi.
lessons.tip: 'gsi' (been) is one of the most important words of all: Wo bisch gsi? = Where were you?

ex.explain: gsi takes a form of sii. With du, use bisch.

lessons.more: Zurich German has no simple past. 'Ich ging', 'ich kam', 'ich sah' do not exist. You form everything in the past with the perfect: Ich bi gange, Ich bi cho, Ich ha gseh. The only exception in some regions is 'ich war', but even there people mostly say 'ich bi gsi'.

lessons.title: Perfect with sii
lessons.rule: As in Standard German, verbs of movement form the perfect with 'sii'. The participles are often short: gange, cho, gsi.
lessons.structure: Ich bi gange. · Er isch cho. · Mir sind dihei gsi. · Si isch gfahre.
examples: Ich bi geschter uf Basel gfahre.
lessons.tip: 'gsi' means been. 'cho' means come, without any ge-.

ex.prompt: Translate: Yesterday I was at home.

lessons.more: Participles in Zurich German are often shorter than in Standard German: gsi (been), cho (come), gange (gone), gseh (seen), gää (given), gno (taken).

lessons.title: uf, is, i
lessons.rule: Direction to cities is expressed with 'uf', not with 'nach'. 'is' means into the, 'i' means in.
lessons.structure: Ich gaa uf Bärn. · Mir fahred uf Genf. · Ich gaa is Kino. · Si isch i de Stadt.
examples: Are you coming to the concert too?
lessons.tip: For countries you say 'in': Ich gaa in Italie.

ex.explain: Use uf when going to a city.
Use in when going to a country.
Use uf for movement towards a city.

lessons.more: 'uf' for cities is typically Swiss: uf Bärn, uf Basel, uf Paris. For places in a building you use 'i': i de Schuel, i de Migros. 'is' is 'in das': is Kino, is Bett. Where someone lives is said with 'z': Ich wohne z Züri.

reading.title: Geschter (yesterday)
reading.text: Geschter **bin** ich uf Luzärn **gfahre**. Ich **bi** am See **gsi** und **ha** es Glace **gässe**. Am Abig **bin** ich spaat hei **cho**. Ich **bi** müed **gsi**, aber es **isch** en schöne Tag **gsi**.
reading.tr: Yesterday I went to Lucerne. I was at the lake and ate an ice cream. In the evening I came home late. I was tired, but it was a beautiful day.

ex.prompt: Am Abig bin ich spaat hei ___. (come)

lessons.title: am + infinitive
lessons.rule: What is happening right now is said with 'am' + infinitive. It corresponds to English -ing.
lessons.structure: Ich bi am Ässe. · Er isch am Schaffe. · Mir sind am Luege.
examples: She is on the phone right now.
What are you doing right now?
lessons.tip: 'grad' (right now) goes well with it: Ich bi grad am Läse.

ex.prompt: Translate: He is working right now.
What does 'Si isch am Schlafe' mean?

lessons.more: 'am + infinitive' is very common in Swiss German; in Standard German it counts as colloquial. It only works with 'sii': Ich bi am Schaffe. With an object, the object comes first: Ich bi s Znacht am Mache.

lessons.title: hett gärn and wär
lessons.rule: For polite wishes and conditions the subjunctive is used: ich hett (would have), ich wär (would be), ich würd (would).
lessons.structure: Ich hett gärn es Bier. · Das wär super. · Ich würd cho, wänn ich Ziit hett.
examples: Wänn ich riich wär, würd ich reise.
If I were rich, I would travel.
lessons.tip: In a restaurant the most natural way to order is 'Ich hett gärn ...'.

ex.prompt: Wänn ich Ziit ___, würd ich cho.
ex.explain: Use hett for “had” in this hypothetical condition.

lessons.more: The most important subjunctive forms: ich wär (would be), ich hett (would have), ich würd (would), ich chönnt (could), ich müesst (would have to). For wishes in shops and restaurants 'Ich hett gärn ...' or 'Ich nimm ...' is enough.

reading.title: At the restaurant
reading.text: 'Grüezi, **ich hett gärn** e Röschti und es Bier.' 'Gärn. **Wänn** **wär** Ihne s Dessert recht?' 'Spöter, merci.' Ich **bi** grad **am Ässe**, wo mini Fründin **aalüütet**: '**Wo bisch**? Ich **würd** au gärn **cho**!'
reading.tr: 'Good day, I'd like a rösti and a beer.' 'Sure. When would you like the dessert?' 'Later, thanks.' I'm eating when my girlfriend calls: 'Where are you? I'd like to come too!'

lessons.title: Comparing: als and wie
lessons.rule: The comparative works like in Standard German: -er and often an umlaut. After the comparative Zurich speakers say 'als' or very often 'wie': Er isch grösser wie ich.
lessons.structure: gross → grösser → am grööschte · guet → besser → am beschte · vill → mee → am meischte · grösser als / grösser wie
examples: Mis Velo isch schnäller wie dis.
My bike is faster than yours.
lessons.tip: Mee means more: Ich möcht mee Ziit. For less, use weniger or wäniger.

ex.prompt: Translate: The tram is faster than the bus.
ex.answer: S Tram isch schnäller als de Bus

lessons.more: Equality: so ... wie: Er isch so alt wie ich. Common superlatives: am beschte, am liebschte, am meischte, am grööschte. Before a noun: de gröscht Berg, di bescht Fründin. 'gärn, lieber, am liebschte' is used for preferences: Ich trink lieber Tee.

lessons.title: Reported speech: er heig, si seig
lessons.rule: In Zurich German the subjunctive of reported speech is still used every day: Er hät gseit, er heig kei Ziit. Si hät gseit, si seig chrank. Er hät gseit, er chöm spööter.
lessons.structure: sii → seig · haa → heig · choo → chöm · gaa → göng · chöne → chönn · wele → well · Er hät gseit, er seig müed.
examples: Si hät gseit, si heig kei Ziit.
She said she had no time.
De Chef hät gseit, er seig in ere Sitzig.
The boss said he was in a meeting.
Er hät gfröget, öb mir au chömed.
He asked if we were coming too.
lessons.tip: In conversation people also just use the indicative: Er hät gseit, er hät kei Ziit. But the subjunctive sounds typically Zurich.

ex.prompt: Er hät gseit, er ___ kei Hunger. (haa)
Translate: He said he was tired.
ex.answer: Er hät gseit er seig müed

lessons.more: Yes/no questions are introduced with 'öb': Si hät gfröget, öb ich Ziit heig. With question words the word stays: Er hät gfröget, wo ich wohni. 'wohni', 'machi' (I live, I do) are also subjunctive forms you often hear.

lessons.title: Verb order in subordinate clauses
lessons.rule: In subordinate clauses the verbs go to the end, like in Standard German. But with several verbs the order is often different: the auxiliary comes first: ..., will er nöd hät chöne choo.
lessons.structure: will ich kei Ziit ha · dass er hät müese schaffe · wänn du wotsch choo · öb si cha choo
examples: Ich chume nöd, will ich mues schaffe.
I'm not coming because I have to work.
Er hät gseit, dass er nöd hät chöne schlafe.
Do you know if she wants to come along?
lessons.tip: In Zurich German 'will' means 'because', not 'want'. 'To want' is 'wele'.

ex.prompt: Ich gaa hei, ___ ich müed bi.
Translate: I'm not coming because I have to work.
ex.answer: Ich chume nöd will ich mues schaffe

lessons.more: In a Zurich German subordinate clause, the auxiliary can precede the modal and the infinitive: dass si hät wele choo. In the perfect tense, keep the modal in the infinitive: hät müese.

lessons.title: Passive: es wird gmacht
lessons.rule: The passive is formed with 'wärde' + participle, like in Standard German. Present: Das wird gmacht. Perfect: Das isch gmacht worde. In everyday speech people often prefer 'mer' (one): Da redt mer Dütsch.
lessons.structure: ich wirde · du wirsch · er/si/es wird · mir wärded · ihr wärded · si wärded · Das Huus wird renoviert. · Es isch verchauft worde.
lessons.tip: Zurich German has no simple past. To say the house was built, use the perfect passive: S Huus isch baut worde.
lessons.more: Many participles are shorter than in Standard German: gmacht, gseit, gstole, baut (without ge-), gschribe. With a modal: Das mues gmacht wärde. In newspapers and announcements you often hear the passive in Standard German; in conversation rather 'mer' or 'si' (they): Si mached d Strass nöi.

head: Tense
Zurich German
English meaning
rows: This is how we do it here.

reading.title: Es Gspröch im Tram
reading.text: Geschter im Tram hät mir e Frau verzellt, si **seig** grad us Amerika zrugg. Si hät gseit, Züri **seig** vill **sauberer wie** New York. Ich han gfröget, **öb** si wider zrugg **wöll**. Si hät gseit, si chönn nöd, **will** si **mues** schaffe. Ires alte Huus **isch** letscht Jahr **verchauft worde**.
reading.tr: Yesterday on the tram a woman told me she had just come back from America. She said Zurich was much cleaner than New York. I asked if she wanted to go back. She said she couldn't because she had to work. Her old house was sold last year.

ex.explain: si seig grad us Amerika zrugg
seig is used in reported speech.

lessons.title: Future with the present tense
lessons.rule: Zurich German rarely uses a future tense. Use the present tense with a time word such as morn, nächschti Wuche or spöter.
lessons.structure: Morn gang ich go schaffe. · Nächscht Jahr zügled mir.
examples: Tomorrow we are going to the cinema.
lessons.tip: Wird + infinitive exists, but it usually sounds like a guess: Er wird scho chuu.

ex.prompt: Which sentence is most natural for “I will call you tomorrow”?

ex.explain: Ich schriib = I write / will write.

ex.prompt: Say that tomorrow you are going to Zurich.

lessons.title: Possession with em … sis
lessons.rule: Zurich German often shows possession with the dative + possessive pronoun instead of the genitive: em Vatter sis Auto, de Mueter iri Tasche.
lessons.structure: em Peter sis Velo · de Anna iri Wohnig · de Chind iri Spilsache
examples: Das isch em Peter sis Velo.
De Lehrerin iri Tasche isch rot.
Mim Brüeder sini Fründin chunnt hüt.
My brother’s girlfriend is coming today.
lessons.tip: Use sis/sini for a male owner and iri/ires for a female owner.

ex.explain: Female owner, masculine noun: ire Hund.

ex.prompt: Das isch em Vatter ___ Huus. (his, neuter)
ex.explain: Male owner, neuter noun: sis Huus.

ex.prompt: Match the owner with the phrase.

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs: sich freue
lessons.rule: Reflexive verbs use mi, di, sich, eus, eu, sich. Common ones: sich freue (be happy), sich aalegge (get dressed), sich verliebe (fall in love).
lessons.structure: ich freu mi · du freusch di · er freut sich · mir freued eus
examples: Ich freu mi uf s Wuchenänd.
I am looking forward to the weekend.
lessons.tip: sich freue uf = look forward to; sich freue über = be happy about.

ex.prompt: Say you are looking forward to the holidays.
ex.answer: Ich freu mi uf d Ferie

lessons.title: Adjective endings
lessons.rule: Before a noun, adjectives take short endings: en schöne Tag, e schöni Frau, es schöns Huus. After de, d and s the endings are -i (feminine, plural) or -e (masculine).
lessons.structure: en guete Fründ · e gueti Idee · es guets Gfühl · di neue Schue
lessons.tip: Neuter after es often ends in -s: es guets Ässe, es chliises Huus.

ex.prompt: Match the article with the right adjective.

reading.title: Es Fäscht am Samstig
reading.text: Am Samstig **gömmer** a em Lukas **sis** Fäscht. Ich **freu mi** scho sit Wuche! Ich bring **en guete** Wii und **e chliini** Überraschig mit. **Em Lukas sini** Schwöschter macht **es grosses** Buffet.
reading.tr: On Saturday we are going to Lukas’s party. I have been looking forward to it for weeks! I am bringing a good wine and a small surprise. Lukas’s sister is making a big buffet.

ex.explain: en guete Wii und e chliini Überraschig.

lessons.title: Linking a description with wo
lessons.rule: In Zurich German, wo can introduce a relative clause about a person or thing. The same marker can link clauses to masculine, feminine and neuter nouns.
lessons.structure: noun + wo + relative clause
examples: D Frau, wo dä Brief gschribe hät, isch mini Nochberin.
The woman who wrote the letter is my neighbour.
S Buech, wo du mer gää hesch, isch spannend.
The book you gave me is interesting.
lessons.tip: Here wo links the description to the preceding noun. In a question such as Wo wohnsch?, it asks about location.

ex.prompt: Which sentence means “The man who called yesterday is here”?
options: De Maa, wo geschter aaglüüte hät, isch da.
De Maa hät gfragt, wo du wohnsch.
De Maa isch geschter da gsi.
ex.explain: Wo links de Maa to the description of the person who called.

ex.prompt: Supply the relative marker. „D Lüüt, ___ da schaffed, kenned sich guet.“
ex.explain: The relative marker stays wo with the plural noun d Lüüt.

lessons.title: Expressing a purpose with zum
lessons.rule: A Zurich German purpose clause can start with zum and end with an infinitive. The words between them say what the action involves.
lessons.structure: main action + zum + complement + infinitive
examples: Ich bi i d Stadt gange, zum es Billett löse.
I went into town to buy a ticket.
Si hät aaglüüte, zum en Termin abmache.
She called to arrange an appointment.
lessons.tip: Dialect writing varies. Practise recognising the purpose construction even if a writer spells individual words differently.

ex.prompt: Which ending explains the purpose of the call? „Er hät aaglüüte, ___.“
options: will er scho det gsi isch
ex.explain: Zum introduces what he wanted to achieve by calling.

ex.prompt: What does „Si isch früener gange, zum de Zug verwütsche“ tell you?
options: She caught the train and then left.
She left earlier in order to catch the train.
She left because the train had already gone.
ex.explain: The zum clause describes the purpose. Whether she caught it remains open.

lessons.title: Hearing qualified agreement
lessons.rule: Scho can mean already in a time expression. In replies such as Ja, scho, aber …, it can acknowledge a point before the speaker adds a reservation.
lessons.structure: scho + time expression · Ja, scho, aber + reservation
examples: Ich bi scho am Sibe det gsi.
I was already there at seven.
Ja, scho, aber mir händ fascht kei Ziit.
Yes, that is true, but we have hardly any time.
lessons.tip: Use the next clause and the tone of the reply to decide whether scho is about timing or about agreement.

ex.prompt: You propose moving a meeting to Friday. A colleague replies, „Ja, scho, aber am Friitig sind nöd alli da.“ What is the reservation?
options: Some people are unavailable on Friday.
Everyone has already agreed to Friday.
ex.explain: Aber introduces a practical concern about Friday attendance.

ex.prompt: Which line uses scho to mark time?
options: Das stimmt scho, aber es hilft üs nöd.
Mir sind scho vor em Zmittag aacho.
Ja, scho, aber es git no es Problem.
ex.explain: Vor em Zmittag anchors scho to when the speakers arrived.

lessons.title: Reading and paraphrasing a tactful refusal
lessons.rule: In a conversation about scheduling, a speaker can signal a refusal by describing the timing as difficult and offering another option. The offer makes the intended response clearer.
lessons.structure: Das wird schwierig. · Würd dir … passe?
examples: Hüt wird’s schwierig. Würd dir morn passe?
Today is difficult. Would tomorrow work for you?
Ich glaub, das langt mer hüt nümme. Chömer das verschiebe?
I don’t think I can fit that in today. Can we reschedule?
lessons.tip: If the speaker gives no alternative, the wording can leave the decision open. Look for a clear commitment before recording a time as agreed.

ex.prompt: A colleague replies, „Das langt mer hüt nümme. Gömmer morn?“ Which update preserves the meaning?
options: Hüt passt nöd. Morn isch en Vorschlag.
Si hät ganz abgseit und will sich nümme träffe.
ex.explain: Today is declined and tomorrow is proposed. Tomorrow has yet to be agreed.

ex.prompt: Which reply actually confirms an appointment tomorrow?
options: Ja, morn am Drüü passt mer.
ex.explain: The last reply confirms both the day and the time.

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The Italian alphabet
lessons.rule: The Italian alphabet has 21 letters. J, K, W, X and Y only appear in foreign words. Italian is read the way it is written, and every vowel is pronounced.
lessons.structure: c / g before e, i = ch / j | ch / gh = k / g | h = silent | z = ts or dz
lessons.tip: Double consonants are held longer: pala (shovel) vs. palla (ball).

alphabet.sound: k, or ch before e, i
g, or j before e, i

options: k, or ch before e, i
ex.explain: C c: k, or ch before e, i – casa.

ex.prompt: Which letter sounds like: silent (makes c and g hard)?
ex.explain: H h: silent (makes c and g hard) – hotel.

options: k, or ch before e, i

ex.prompt: Match the letter and its sound
pairs: k, or ch before e, i

lessons.title: How Italian sounds
lessons.rule: Italian is written the way it is spoken and the vowels are always clear. c and g change their sound before e and i.
lessons.structure: ci, ce → ch (ciao) | chi, che → k (chiesa) | gi, ge → j (gelato) | gn → ny (gnocchi) | double letters → hold them longer (nonno)
lessons.tip: Double consonants change the meaning: nono (ninth) and nonno (grandfather).

ex.prompt: Match the spelling and the sound

lessons.title: Ciao! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: Say your name with "mi chiamo" and where you are from with "sono di".
lessons.structure: Mi chiamo … | Sono di … | Piacere!
lessons.tip: With strangers: "Come si chiama?"

ex.prompt: I am from Milan. → ___ di Milano.

lessons.title: essere and avere
lessons.rule: 'essere' (to be) describes identity and origin, 'avere' (to have) possession. Both are irregular.
lessons.structure: essere: sono, sei, è, siamo, siete, sono · avere: ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno
lessons.tip: The pronoun is usually dropped: 'Sono stanco' means 'I am tired'.
lessons.more: The subject pronoun is usually dropped because the verb form is enough: Sono stanco. avere is used for age and many states: ho 30 anni, ho fame, ho freddo, ho ragione. 'c'è' and 'ci sono' (there is / there are) come from essere. Careful: è (is) has an accent, e (and) doesn't.

lessons.title: Article
lessons.rule: Masculine: il (before s+consonant and z: lo), feminine: la. Before a vowel: l'. Plural: i / gli / le.
lessons.structure: il libro, i libri · lo studente, gli studenti · la casa, le case · l'amico, gli amici
lessons.tip: The ending -o is usually masculine, -a feminine. Words in -e have to be learned.

ex.explain: Use lo before s followed by a consonant.

lessons.more: The masculine article depends on how the word begins: il before a normal consonant, lo before s + consonant, z, gn, ps, y (lo studente, lo zio), l' before a vowel. In the plural il becomes i, lo and l' become gli. Feminine: la / l' and le. Indefinite: un, uno, una, un'.

reading.title: Mi chiamo Giulia
reading.text: Ciao! **Sono** Giulia e **sono** di Milano. **Ho** ventotto anni. **Il** mio ragazzo **è** svizzero, **ha** un negozio a Lugano. **Lo** studente che vive con noi **è** tedesco. **Abbiamo** **un** gatto e **una** casa piccola.
reading.tr: Hi! I'm Giulia and I'm from Milan. I'm twenty-eight. My boyfriend is Swiss, he has a shop in Lugano. The student who lives with us is German. We have a cat and a small house.

lessons.title: Verbs in -are
lessons.rule: Regular -are verbs: drop -are, then add the personal ending.
lessons.structure: parlare → parlo, parli, parla, parliamo, parlate, parlano
lessons.tip: The stress in 'parlano' is on the first syllable: PAR-la-no.
lessons.more: Drop -are and add the ending: parl-are → parl-o. Stress: in parlano it falls on the first syllable (PARlano), not on the ending. Verbs in -care and -gare add an h to keep the hard sound: cerchi, paghiamo.

lessons.title: piacere
lessons.rule: As in Spanish: the thing liked is the subject. One thing → piace, several → piacciono.
lessons.structure: mi / ti / gli / le / ci / vi + piace / piacciono
lessons.tip: With a verb always 'piace': Mi piace cucinare.

ex.explain: Use piacciono when the thing liked is plural.

ex.prompt: We like music: ___ piace la musica.

lessons.more: With piacere, the thing that pleases is the subject: Mi piace la pizza, Mi piacciono gli spaghetti. With verbs always singular: Mi piace leggere. gli means 'to him' (in speech also 'to them'), le means 'to her' and politely 'to you'. For emphasis: A me piace, a te no.

reading.title: Il sabato
reading.text: Il sabato **parlo** con mia madre al telefono. Poi **mangiamo** insieme. **Mi piace** cucinare e **mi piacciono** i dolci. Mio fratello **lavora** in un bar. A lui non **piace** il caffè, ma lo **prepara** benissimo!
reading.tr: On Saturdays I talk to my mother on the phone. Then we eat together. I like cooking and I like desserts. My brother works in a bar. He doesn't like coffee, but he makes it brilliantly!

lessons.title: Verbs in -ere and -ire
lessons.rule: Regular -ere and -ire verbs have almost the same endings. Some -ire verbs insert -isc- (capire, finire).
lessons.structure: prendere: prendo, prendi, prende, prendiamo, prendete, prendono · dormire: dormo, dormi, dorme, dormiamo, dormite, dormono · capire: capisco, capisci, capisce, capiamo, capite, capiscono
lessons.tip: -isc- is only used with io, tu, lui/lei and loro, not with noi and voi.

ex.prompt: Translate: You (pl.) are writing a letter.

lessons.more: -ere and -ire verbs have almost the same endings, they only differ for voi: prendete / dormite. Many -ire verbs add -isc- in the stressed forms: capire → capisco, capisci, capisce, capiscono (but capiamo, capite). Likewise: finire, preferire, pulire.

lessons.title: andare and fare
lessons.rule: andare (to go) and fare (to do, make) are irregular and very common.
lessons.structure: andare: vado, vai, va, andiamo, andate, vanno · fare: faccio, fai, fa, facciamo, fate, fanno
lessons.tip: Cities with a, countries with in: vado a Roma, vado in Italia.
lessons.more: andare a + city, andare in + country or region: Vado a Roma, Vado in Italia. Many places take in: in ufficio, in banca, in centro. fare appears in many expressions: fare colazione (to have breakfast), fare la spesa (to go grocery shopping), fa caldo (it's hot).

lessons.title: c'è and ci sono
lessons.rule: c'è (there is, singular) and ci sono (plural) say what there is in a place.
lessons.structure: C'è un bar. · Ci sono due bar. · Non c'è latte. · C'è ...?
examples: Is there a pharmacy near here?
There are a lot of tourists.
lessons.tip: c'è = ci + è. In the plural it is not contracted: ci sono.
lessons.more: c'è (there is) and ci sono (there are) introduce something: C'è un problema. For the location of something known use essere: Il bar è in piazza. To ask, just use intonation: C'è una farmacia qui vicino?

lessons.title: il mio, la mia
lessons.rule: In Italian the article usually comes before the possessive. Exception: family members in the singular without anything added.
lessons.structure: il mio libro · la mia casa · i miei amici · le mie amiche · but: mia madre, mio padre · i miei genitori
lessons.tip: loro always keeps the article: la loro madre.
lessons.more: In Italian the possessive is normally preceded by the article: il mio libro, la tua casa. Exception: single family members without additions: mia madre, tuo fratello. But in the plural or with a diminutive it returns: i miei fratelli, la mia sorellina. 'loro' never changes: il loro, la loro.

lessons.title: nel, al, del
lessons.rule: The prepositions di, a, da, in, su merge with the definite article.
lessons.structure: a + il = al · di + il = del · da + il = dal · in + il = nel · su + il = sul · in + la = nella · a + la = alla
examples: The book is in the drawer.
lessons.tip: With con and per people usually don't merge today: con il, per la.
lessons.more: The prepositions a, da, di, in, su merge with the definite article. The form follows the article: il → al, lo → allo, la → alla, l' → all', i → ai, gli → agli, le → alle. con and per do not merge in modern Italian.

reading.title: In centro
reading.text: Oggi **vado** in centro con **i miei** amici. In piazza **c'è** un mercato e **ci sono** tante bancarelle. **Facciamo** la spesa e poi **prendiamo** un aperitivo **al** bar **della** stazione. **Mia** sorella **dorme** ancora!
reading.tr: Today I'm going into town with my friends. On the square there's a market and lots of stalls. We do the shopping and then have an aperitif at the station bar. My sister is still asleep!

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 100
lessons.rule: The tens lose their last vowel before uno and otto: ventuno, ventotto. A final tre gets an accent: ventitré. Age uses avere: ho 20 anni.
lessons.structure: uno, due, tre … dieci | undici, dodici, tredici, quattordici, quindici, sedici | diciassette, diciotto, diciannove | venti · trenta · quaranta · cinquanta · cento
lessons.tip: Euro does not change in the plural: un euro, quindici euro.

ex.explain: venti loses the i before uno.
One word, with an accent on the final é.

lessons.title: The time and days
lessons.rule: Ask "Che ore sono?". One o’clock, noon and midnight are singular (è l’una, è mezzogiorno); the other hours are plural (sono le due). Days and months are written in lower case.
lessons.structure: È l’una · Sono le tre · le tre e un quarto · le tre e mezza · le quattro meno un quarto · mezzogiorno | lunedì · a maggio · alle otto
lessons.tip: lunedì = this Monday; il lunedì = every Monday.

ex.explain: Only one o’clock is singular: è l’una.

ex.prompt: The lesson starts at eight. → La lezione comincia ___ otto.

lessons.title: Plural of nouns
lessons.rule: Masculine -o → -i, feminine -a → -e, -e → -i (both genders). Stressed endings and loanwords stay the same.
lessons.structure: libro → libri · casa → case · fiore → fiori · città → città · bar → bar · amico → amici · amica → amiche
lessons.tip: With -ca and -ga an h is added so the sound stays the same: amica → amiche.
lessons.more: -o → -i, -a → -e, -e → -i. Unchanged are words with a final accent (la città, le città), foreign words (il bar, i bar) and short forms (la foto, le foto). Words in -co and -go: mostly -chi / -ghi, but amico → amici, medico → medici. Some become feminine in the plural: l'uovo → le uova, il braccio → le braccia.

lessons.title: Adjective agreement
lessons.rule: Adjectives in -o have four forms (-o, -a, -i, -e). Adjectives in -e have only two (-e, -i). They usually come after the noun.
lessons.structure: un ragazzo alto · una ragazza alta · ragazzi alti · ragazze alte · un libro interessante · libri interessanti
lessons.tip: Before a noun bello behaves like the article: un bel ragazzo, un bello spettacolo, dei bei libri.

ex.explain: Use bel before an ordinary consonant.

lessons.more: Adjectives in -o have four forms (alto, alta, alti, alte), adjectives in -e only two (grande, grandi). They usually come after the noun. bello and buono change before the noun like the article: un bel ragazzo, un bello spettacolo, dei begli occhi, un buon vino.

lessons.title: volere, potere, dovere
lessons.rule: The modal verbs are irregular. They are followed by the infinitive.
lessons.structure: volere: voglio, vuoi, vuole, vogliamo, volete, vogliono · potere: posso, puoi, può, possiamo, potete, possono · dovere: devo, devi, deve, dobbiamo, dovete, devono
lessons.tip: Ask politely with vorrei (I would like).
lessons.more: Modal verbs take an infinitive without a preposition: Voglio partire. The conditional is polite: Vorrei un caffè, Potrebbe aiutarmi? In the passato prossimo they take the auxiliary of the following verb: Ho dovuto lavorare, Sono dovuto partire.

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs
lessons.rule: Reflexive pronouns come before the verb. With an infinitive they are attached at the end.
lessons.structure: chiamarsi: mi chiamo, ti chiami, si chiama, ci chiamiamo, vi chiamate, si chiamano
lessons.tip: With a modal verb you can choose: Mi devo alzare or Devo alzarmi.

ex.explain: Pronoun attached to the infinitive: alzarmi.

lessons.more: The reflexive pronoun goes before the verb: Mi alzo alle sette. With an infinitive it is attached and the -e is dropped: Devo alzarmi presto. In the passato prossimo all reflexive verbs take essere and the participle agrees: Lei si è alzata.

lessons.title: lo, la, li, le
lessons.rule: Direct object pronouns come before the conjugated verb and replace the direct object.
lessons.structure: lo (him, it) · la (her) · li (them, masculine) · le (them, feminine) · before a vowel: l'
lessons.tip: In the passato prossimo the participle agrees: L'ho vista (seen her).
lessons.more: lo, la, li, le replace the direct object and go before the verb: Lo conosco. With an infinitive they are attached: Voglio comprarlo. In the passato prossimo the participle agrees with la, li, le: La pizza? L'ho mangiata. I libri? Li ho letti.

reading.title: Una mattina difficile
reading.text: Luca **si alza** tardi. **Deve** andare al lavoro, ma non **trova** le chiavi. Le chiavi? Non **le** vede da nessuna parte. **Vuole** chiamare un taxi, ma **i** taxi sono tutti occupati. Alla fine **prende** la bicicletta. **Gli amici** ridono.
reading.tr: Luca gets up late. He has to go to work, but he can't find the keys. The keys? He can't see them anywhere. He wants to call a taxi, but the taxis are all taken. In the end he takes his bike. His friends laugh.

lessons.title: Passato prossimo with avere
lessons.rule: The most common past tense: avere + participle. -are → -ato, -ere → -uto, -ire → -ito. Many participles are irregular.
lessons.structure: ho mangiato · hai venduto · ha dormito · fare → fatto · prendere → preso · vedere → visto · leggere → letto
lessons.tip: The h in ho, hai, ha, hanno is not pronounced.
lessons.more: Participle: -are → -ato, -ere → -uto, -ire → -ito. Many common verbs are irregular: fatto, detto, preso, messo, visto, letto, scritto, aperto, bevuto. With avere the participle normally does not agree: Maria ha mangiato.

lessons.title: Passato prossimo with essere
lessons.rule: Verbs of movement and change of state (andare, venire, partire, nascere, restare) and all reflexive verbs form the passato prossimo with essere. The participle agrees.
lessons.structure: sono andato/a · siamo partiti/e · è nata · mi sono alzato/a
lessons.tip: essere itself forms: sono stato/a (I have been).
lessons.more: Most verbs of movement and change (andare, venire, partire, arrivare, uscire, entrare, nascere, morire, diventare, restare) and all reflexive verbs take essere. The participle agrees like an adjective: Anna è partita, i ragazzi sono arrivati.

lessons.title: Imperfetto
lessons.rule: The imperfetto describes habits and states in the past. Infinitive without -re + -vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano.
lessons.structure: parlare → parlavo · leggere → leggevo · dormire → dormivo · essere: ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano · fare → facevo
examples: As a child I played football.
It was raining when I went out.
lessons.tip: imperfetto = scenery, passato prossimo = event.

ex.explain: Use faceva for weather in the background of a story.

lessons.more: The imperfetto describes background, habits and states: Da bambino giocavo a calcio. The passato prossimo tells the completed action: Leggevo quando è arrivato Marco. Almost all verbs are regular; irregular are essere (ero), fare (facevo), bere (bevevo), dire (dicevo).

lessons.title: Futuro semplice
lessons.rule: The futuro: infinitive without -e + endings. With -are the a becomes e. Some stems are irregular.
lessons.structure: -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno · parlare → parlerò · prendere → prenderò · essere → sarò · avere → avrò · andare → andrò · fare → farò
examples: I will be at home at eight.
What are you going to do?
lessons.tip: In everyday life Italians often use the present for near plans: Domani vado a Roma.
lessons.more: In -are verbs the a becomes e in the future: parlare → parlerò. Important irregular stems: sar- (essere), avr- (avere), andr- (andare), farò (fare), verr- (venire), vorr- (volere), potr- (potere). The future also expresses guesses: Sarà a casa (he's probably at home).

lessons.title: stare + gerundio
lessons.rule: What is happening right now: stare + gerund. -are → -ando, -ere/-ire → -endo.
lessons.structure: sto, stai, sta, stiamo, state, stanno + parlando / leggendo / dormendo · fare → facendo · bere → bevendo
examples: What are you doing right now?
lessons.tip: stare also means to be (somewhere): Come stai? How are you?

ex.prompt: Translate: The children are sleeping right now.

lessons.more: stare + gerund describes what is happening right now: Sto mangiando. -are becomes -ando, -ere and -ire become -endo. Irregular: fare → facendo, bere → bevendo, dire → dicendo. stare per + infinitive means 'to be about to': Sto per uscire.

reading.title: Un'estate in Sicilia
reading.text: Da bambino **andavo** ogni estate in Sicilia dai nonni. **Faceva** caldo e **giocavo** sempre al mare. L'anno scorso **sono tornato** con mia moglie. **Abbiamo mangiato** benissimo. L'anno prossimo **ci torneremo** con i bambini. **Sto** già **pensando** al viaggio!
reading.tr: As a child I went to my grandparents in Sicily every summer. It was hot and I always played by the sea. Last year I went back with my wife. We ate wonderfully. Next year we'll go back with the children. I'm already thinking about the trip!

ex.prompt: Con chi è tornato l'anno scorso?

lessons.title: Comparing
lessons.rule: più / meno + adjective + di (before nouns and pronouns) or che (before adjectives, verbs, prepositions). Irregular: buono → migliore, cattivo → peggiore.
lessons.structure: Roma è più grande di Firenze. · È più facile parlare che scrivere. · il più bello · buono → migliore · bene → meglio
examples: Luca è più alto di me.
È la città più bella d'Italia.
It is the most beautiful city in Italy.
lessons.tip: così ... come or tanto ... quanto means as ... as.

ex.prompt: Il treno è più veloce ___ autobus.
È più bello leggere ___ guardare la TV.

lessons.more: più / meno + adjective + di before nouns and pronouns: Marco è più alto di me. Before verbs, adjectives and with a preposition use che: È più facile leggere che scrivere. Equality: (così) ... come, (tanto) ... quanto. Irregular: buono → migliore, cattivo → peggiore, bene → meglio.

lessons.title: ci and ne
lessons.rule: ci replaces places and complements with a (there, about it). ne replaces quantities and complements with di (of it). Both come before the verb.
lessons.structure: Vai a Roma? Sì, ci vado. · Quanti figli hai? Ne ho due. · Ne parliamo domani.
examples: Vuoi del pane? Sì, ne voglio un po'.
Do you want some bread? Yes, a little.
lessons.tip: With quantities the number stays: Ne compro tre.

ex.explain: Use ne for a quantity of something.

ex.prompt: Translate: I have three of them.

lessons.more: ci replaces places and phrases with a: Vai a Roma? Sì, ci vado. Penso al lavoro → Ci penso. ne replaces quantities and phrases with di: Quanti caffè? Ne prendo due. Parliamo del film → Ne parliamo. Set phrases: Ci vuole un'ora (it takes an hour), Me ne vado (I'm leaving).

lessons.title: Imperative with tu
lessons.rule: In the tu imperative -are verbs end in -a, -ere/-ire verbs in -i. Negative: non + infinitive. Pronouns are attached at the end.
lessons.structure: parlare → Parla! · prendere → Prendi! · dormire → Dormi! · Non parlare! · essere → Sii! · avere → Abbi! · andare → Va'! · fare → Fa'!
lessons.tip: With one-syllable forms (da', di', fa', sta', va') the pronoun's consonant is doubled: Dammi! Fammi vedere!
lessons.more: The tu command: -are → -a (Parla!), -ere and -ire → -i (Prendi! Dormi!). In the negative use non + infinitive: Non parlare! Pronouns are attached: Dimmi! Fallo! With the short forms da', di', fa', sta', va' the consonant doubles: dammi, fammi, vacci.

lessons.title: Condizionale: vorrei
lessons.rule: The condizionale expresses wishes, polite requests and advice. Stem as in the futuro + -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero.
lessons.structure: volere → vorrei · potere → potrei · essere → sarei · avere → avrei · parlare → parlerei · andare → andrei
examples: I would like a glass of water.
If I were you, I would go.
lessons.tip: The stem is the same as in the futuro: sarò → sarei, verrò → verrei.
lessons.more: The conditional expresses wishes, polite requests and advice: Vorrei un tavolo per due. Al tuo posto, partirei. It has the same irregular stems as the future: sarei, avrei, andrei, verrei. Endings: -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero.

lessons.title: Congiuntivo after penso che
lessons.rule: After opinion, wish and doubt (penso che, credo che, voglio che, spero che) the congiuntivo is used. The singular forms are the same.
lessons.structure: -are: che io parli, tu parli, lui parli, noi parliamo, voi parliate, loro parlino · -ere/-ire: che io prenda ... loro prendano · essere: sia · avere: abbia · fare: faccia
lessons.tip: Same subject → di + infinitive: Penso di venire. Different subject → che + congiuntivo.

ex.explain: Use the subjunctive abbia to express an opinion here.

ex.prompt: Translate: I want you to stay.

lessons.more: The congiuntivo follows opinions, wishes, doubt and feelings: penso che, credo che, voglio che, spero che, è importante che. With the same subject use di + infinitive: Penso di partire. All three singular forms are the same, so the pronoun is often added: che io sia, che tu sia.

reading.title: Consigli per Roma
reading.text: Roma è **più** grande **di** Firenze, ma secondo me è **la più** bella. Il Colosseo? **Ci** vai la mattina presto. Musei? Ce **ne** sono tantissimi. **Vorrei** darti un consiglio: **prendi** la metro e **non prendere** il taxi. **Penso che** tu **abbia** bisogno di almeno una settimana.
reading.tr: Rome is bigger than Florence, but I think it's the most beautiful. The Colosseum? Go there early in the morning. Museums? There are loads. I'd like to give you some advice: take the metro and don't take a taxi. I think you need at least a week.

ex.prompt: Penso che tu ___ bisogno di una settimana. (avere)

lessons.title: Pluperfect
lessons.rule: The trapassato prossimo describes what had already happened before another past event. Formation: imperfetto of avere or essere + participle.
lessons.structure: avevo mangiato · ero partito/a · Quando sono arrivato, il film era già cominciato.
examples: Quando sono arrivato, avevano già mangiato.
When I arrived, they had already eaten.
Non ero mai stato a Roma.
I had never been to Rome.
Mi ha detto che aveva perso le chiavi.
He told me he had lost his keys.
lessons.tip: avere or essere is chosen as in the passato prossimo.

ex.prompt: Quando siamo arrivati, il treno ___ partito.
Translate: I had already read the book.

lessons.more: It is often used in reported speech: Ha detto che era stato malato. With essere the participle agrees: Le ragazze erano già uscite.

lessons.title: Combined pronouns
lessons.rule: When an indirect (mi, ti, gli ...) and a direct pronoun (lo, la, li, le, ne) meet, the indirect comes first and becomes me, te, ce, ve. gli and le become glie- and merge: glielo.
lessons.structure: me lo · te la · ce li · ve le · glielo · gliela · me ne · Te lo do. · Glielo dico.
examples: The book? I'll lend it to you.
The letter? I sent it to her yesterday.
Will you give me two of them?
lessons.tip: glielo means 'it to him', 'it to her' and politely 'it to you'. Context decides.

ex.prompt: Il caffè? ___ lo preparo subito. (a te)

lessons.more: With the infinitive and positive commands the combination is attached: Voglio dirtelo. Dammelo! In the passato prossimo the participle agrees with lo, la, li, le: Gliel'ho data (la chiave).

lessons.title: Imperfect subjunctive
lessons.rule: The imperfect subjunctive follows expressions of opinion or wish in the past or conditional: Pensavo che fosse a casa. Vorrei che tu venissi. Formation: imperfetto stem + -ssi, -ssi, -sse, -ssimo, -ste, -ssero.
lessons.structure: parlare → parlassi · prendere → prendessi · dormire → dormissi · essere → fossi · avere → avessi · fare → facessi · dare → dessi · stare → stessi
examples: I thought you were on holiday.
Era importante che tutti lo sapessero.
It was important that everyone knew.
lessons.tip: io and tu have the same form: che io fossi, che tu fossi. The pronoun helps understanding.

ex.prompt: Translate: I thought he was right.

lessons.more: Sequence of tenses: main clause in the present → present subjunctive (Penso che sia). Main clause in the past or conditional → imperfect subjunctive (Pensavo che fosse, Vorrei che fosse). The endings are almost the same for all three verb groups.

lessons.title: If clauses
lessons.rule: For unreal conditions se takes the imperfect subjunctive and the main clause the conditional: Se avessi tempo, verrei. For a real condition the present is enough: Se piove, resto a casa.
lessons.structure: Se piove, resto a casa. · Se avessi soldi, comprerei una casa. · Se fossi in te, partirei.
examples: Se avessi più tempo, imparerei il giapponese.
If I had more time, I'd learn Japanese.
Se fossi in te, non lo farei.
If I were you, I wouldn't do it.
Cosa faresti se vincessi la lotteria?
What would you do if you won the lottery?
lessons.tip: Never use the conditional after se: Se avessi (not 'Se avrei').

ex.prompt: Translate: If I had money, I would travel.

lessons.more: Three types: reality (Se piove, resto), possibility (Se piovesse, resterei), unreal past (Se fosse piovuto, sarei restato). In speech the imperfetto is often used for the third type: Se lo sapevo, venivo.

lessons.title: si: impersonal and passive
lessons.rule: With si + verb in the 3rd person you say what people generally do or what is done: Si mangia bene qui. With a plural noun the verb is plural: Si vendono case.
lessons.structure: Si parla italiano. · Si vendono biciclette. · Qui non si può fumare. · Come si dice ...? · In Italia si cena tardi.
examples: How do you say 'Velo' in Italian?
lessons.tip: With reflexive verbs si becomes ci si: Ci si alza presto (people get up early).
lessons.more: On signs si is attached: affittasi, vendesi, cercasi. Adjectives go into the plural: Quando si è giovani, si è felici. In the passato prossimo si always takes essere: Si è mangiato bene.

lessons.title: Gerund and recognising the passato remoto
lessons.rule: The gerund alone (without stare) expresses simultaneity, manner or cause: Camminando, ho visto Luca. The passato remoto is the narrative tense of literature and the south; you should be able to read it: parlò, andò, fu.
lessons.structure: Studiando, si impara. · Essendo stanco, sono rimasto a casa. · Passato remoto: parlò, credette, partì · fu (essere) · ebbe (avere) · fece (fare) · disse (dire)
examples: Essendo tardi, abbiamo preso un taxi.
As it was late, we took a taxi.
Dante was born in Florence in 1265.
lessons.tip: The subject of the gerund must be the same as in the main clause. At first you only need to recognise the passato remoto, not use it.

ex.prompt: ___ in bici, ho visto un incidente.
___ stanco, sono andato a letto. (essere, gerund)
Translate: You learn by making mistakes.

lessons.more: Compound gerund: avendo/essendo + participle for prior action: Avendo finito, sono uscito. Regular passato remoto: -ai, -asti, -ò, -ammo, -aste, -arono (parlare). In northern Italy people almost only use the passato prossimo in speech.

reading.title: Una lettera dalla nonna
reading.text: Quando sono arrivato, la nonna **aveva** già **preparato** il pranzo. Mi ha dato una lettera: '**Te l'ho** scritta ieri.' Diceva: 'Vorrei che tu **venissi** più spesso. **Se avessi** più tempo, **verrei** io a Zurigo.' In paese **si dice** che la nonna **fu** la prima donna a guidare una macchina. **Leggendo** la lettera, ho sorriso.
reading.tr: When I arrived, grandma had already made lunch. She gave me a letter: 'I wrote it to you yesterday.' It said: 'I'd like you to come more often. If I had more time, I'd come to Zurich myself.' In the village they say grandma was the first woman to drive a car. Reading the letter, I smiled.

lessons.title: Relative pronoun cui
lessons.rule: Use cui after a preposition instead of che: con cui, di cui, a cui, in cui. Il cui / la cui means “whose”.
lessons.structure: la persona con cui parlo · il libro di cui ti ho parlato
examples: La ragazza con cui esco è di Napoli.
The girl I go out with is from Naples.
Il film di cui parliamo è vecchio.
The film we are talking about is old.
La città in cui vivo è piccola.
The city I live in is small.
lessons.tip: Never use che directly after a preposition.

ex.prompt: Questo è il problema ___ ti parlavo.
La casa in ___ abito è vecchia.
Say this is the friend you trust.
ex.answer: Questo è l’amico di cui mi fido

lessons.title: Irregular comparatives
lessons.rule: Buono, cattivo, grande and piccolo have special forms: migliore (better), peggiore (worse), maggiore (bigger/older), minore (smaller/younger). As adverbs, bene → meglio, male → peggio.
lessons.structure: Questo vino è migliore. · Parli meglio di me.
examples: Mio fratello maggiore vive a Roma.
My older brother lives in Rome.
lessons.tip: Migliore is an adjective (with a noun). Meglio is an adverb (with a verb).

ex.prompt: Match the base form with the comparative.

lessons.title: Congiuntivo after conjunctions
lessons.rule: Conjunctions such as benché, sebbene (although), affinché, perché (so that), prima che (before) and a meno che (unless) take the subjunctive.
lessons.structure: Benché piova, esco. · Te lo dico affinché tu lo sappia.
examples: Although it is late, I am still working.
I speak slowly so that you understand.
Esco prima che arrivi la pioggia.
I’m going out before the rain comes.
lessons.tip: Perché + indicative means “because”; perché + subjunctive means “so that”.

ex.prompt: Say you go out although it is raining. Use benché.

lessons.title: Futuro anteriore
lessons.rule: The futuro anteriore (avere/essere in the future + participle) describes an action completed before another future moment. It can also express a guess about the past.
lessons.structure: Quando avrò finito, uscirò. · Sarà già partito.
examples: Dopo che avrò mangiato, ti chiamerò.
After I have eaten, I’ll call you.
When you arrive, I will already have gone out.
He must have missed the train.
lessons.tip: Choose essere or avere just as in the passato prossimo.

ex.prompt: Dove ___ messo le chiavi? (guess: avere, io)
ex.explain: A guess about the past: avrò messo.

ex.prompt: Match the verb with the auxiliary.

reading.title: Una cena speciale
reading.text: Sabato organizzo una cena per mia sorella **minore**. **Benché** **sia** un po’ stanca, voglio cucinare il **migliore** risotto della mia vita. L’amico **con cui** cucino arriverà alle sei. **Quando avremo finito**, apriremo una bottiglia di vino.
reading.tr: On Saturday I’m organising a dinner for my younger sister. Although I’m a bit tired, I want to cook the best risotto of my life. The friend I cook with will arrive at six. When we have finished, we will open a bottle of wine.

ex.prompt: Why is sia in the subjunctive?
L’amico con ___ cucino arriverà alle sei.

lessons.title: Separating reported claims from predictions
lessons.rule: The present conditional can mark an unverified report. The past conditional after a past reporting verb can instead place an event in the future relative to that past moment.
lessons.structure: secondo le fonti + sarebbe … · disse che sarebbe arrivato
examples: Secondo la stampa, l’accordo sarebbe imminente.
According to the press, the agreement is reportedly imminent.
Disse che sarebbe arrivata il giorno dopo.
She said that she would arrive the following day.
lessons.tip: Look for a source phrase or a past time frame to identify which reading is intended.

ex.prompt: Which sentence presents the information as a report that still needs confirmation?
options: Secondo alcune fonti, ci sarebbero già tutte le firme.
Il comitato ha confermato il risultato.
ex.explain: The source phrase and conditional work together to mark the report as provisional.

ex.prompt: Supply the missing auxiliary. „Disse che ___ tornato il giorno dopo.“
ex.explain: Tornare takes essere, and the past conditional expresses the future in the past here.

lessons.title: Choosing precise relative links
lessons.rule: Cui follows a preposition in a relative clause. Il cui and its variants express a possessive link, with the article agreeing with the possessed noun.
lessons.structure: preposition + cui · il/la/i/le cui + possessed noun
examples: È il fascicolo a cui mi riferivo.
It is the file I was referring to.
È una ricercatrice i cui risultati sono noti.
She is a researcher whose results are well known.
lessons.tip: Choose the preposition from the verb: riferirsi a, dipendere da, contare su.

ex.prompt: Which option completes „il criterio ___ dipende la scelta“?
Supply the article only. „Una proposta ___ cui finalità restano incerte.“
ex.explain: Finalità is plural here, as shown by restano, and it is feminine.

lessons.title: Distinguishing addition from replacement
lessons.rule: Nonché adds a further item in formal writing. Anziché replaces an expected or contrasted option. Confusing them can reverse the practical meaning of an instruction.
lessons.structure: X, nonché Y · X anziché Y
examples: Occorrono il modulo, nonché una copia del documento.
The form is required, along with a copy of the document.
Send a copy instead of the original.
lessons.tip: In procedural writing, check whether the reader must provide both items or substitute one for the other.

ex.prompt: Which instruction asks for two items?
options: Allegate la ricevuta anziché il modulo.
Allegate il modulo, nonché la ricevuta.
Allegate il modulo o la ricevuta.
ex.explain: Nonché adds the receipt to the form.

ex.prompt: What does „Si è scelto di rinviare anziché annullare“ establish?
options: The event was cancelled and postponed.
The decision was to cancel it.
Postponement was chosen in place of cancellation.
ex.explain: Anziché introduces the alternative that was set aside.

lessons.title: Interpreting restrained judgement
lessons.rule: A qualified negative can be more tactful than a direct negative. Non del tutto and tutt’altro che differ sharply in strength even when they modify the same adjective.
lessons.structure: non del tutto + adjective · tutt’altro che + adjective
examples: La risposta non è del tutto convincente.
The answer is not entirely convincing.
La risposta è tutt’altro che convincente.
The answer is far from convincing.
lessons.tip: Read the entire qualifier before judging the speaker’s stance. An indirect formulation can still express a strong objection.

ex.prompt: Which assessment is the strongest criticism?
options: La procedura è tutt’altro che trasparente.
La procedura è in gran parte trasparente.
La procedura non è del tutto trasparente.
ex.explain: Tutt’altro che rejects the description much more strongly than non del tutto.

ex.prompt: What does „La spiegazione lascia a desiderare“ convey?
options: The explanation will be given later.
ex.explain: Lasciare a desiderare is a conventional expression of dissatisfaction.

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The Irish alphabet
lessons.rule: The traditional Irish alphabet has 18 letters (no j, k, q, v, w, x, y, z except in loanwords). A long-mark called the fada (á, é, í, ó, ú) makes a vowel long.
lessons.structure: á é í ó ú = long vowels | s before e, i = sh | bh / mh = v or w | c = always k
lessons.tip: Consonants are "broad" next to a, o, u and "slender" (softer) next to e, i – that changes how they sound.

alphabet.sound: s, or sh before e, i

ex.explain: Á á: aw as in "law" – lá.

ex.prompt: Which letter sounds like: k (always hard)?
Match the letter and its sound

lessons.title: How Irish sounds
lessons.rule: Irish spelling follows its own rules. The accent (síneadh fada) makes a vowel long, and h after a consonant changes or softens it.
lessons.structure: á é í ó ú → long vowels | bh, mh → v or w | dh, gh → often silent or like y | ch → throaty, like "loch"
lessons.tip: Listen first, then read. Irish spelling makes sense once you know these patterns.

ex.explain: Sláinte! is said when drinking a toast.

ex.prompt: Match the spelling and the sound

lessons.title: Dia duit! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: Say your name with "Is mise …" and where you are from with "Is as … mé".
lessons.structure: Is mise … | Is as … mé | Cad is ainm duit?
lessons.tip: The answer to "Dia duit" is "Dia is Muire duit".

ex.explain: Go raibh maith agat = thank you.

lessons.title: Tá: to be
lessons.rule: 'Tá' (is, am, are) describes states and places. In Irish the verb comes at the start of the sentence.
lessons.structure: Tá + subject + complement
lessons.tip: Word order verb, subject, object: the verb always comes first.

ex.prompt: ___ sé go maith. (He is doing well.)

lessons.title: The article an
lessons.rule: Irish has only one definite article: 'an' (plural 'na'). There is no indefinite article.
lessons.structure: an + noun · with feminine nouns often lenition: bean → an bhean
lessons.tip: 'cat' on its own already means 'a cat'.

lessons.title: Is: the copula
lessons.rule: For identity, profession and nationality you don't use 'tá' but the copula 'is'. Then comes the noun, then the person.
lessons.structure: Is + noun + pronoun · Is múinteoir mé. · Is dochtúir í. · Negative: Ní múinteoir é.
lessons.tip: After 'is', he and she are 'é' and 'í', not 'sé' and 'sí'.

ex.prompt: ___ múinteoir é. (He is not a teacher.)

lessons.title: Níl and An bhfuil?
lessons.rule: The negative of 'tá' is 'níl', the question starts with 'An bhfuil ...?'. Irish has no word for yes and no: you answer with the verb.
lessons.structure: Tá mé. · Níl mé. · An bhfuil tú ...? · Answer: Tá. (yes) / Níl. (no)
lessons.tip: The answer repeats the verb of the question. This applies to all verbs.

ex.prompt: An bhfuil tú go maith? Yes: ___.

lessons.title: ag: to have
lessons.rule: There is no verb for 'to have'. You say: 'Tá X agam' (X is at me). The preposition 'ag' merges with the pronoun.
lessons.structure: agam · agat · aige · aici · againn · agaibh · acu · Tá carr agam. · Níl airgead agam.
lessons.tip: These merged forms are called prepositional pronouns. They exist for many prepositions.

ex.prompt: Match ag to its pronoun forms.

lessons.title: mo, do, a + lenition
lessons.rule: After mo (my), do (your) and a (his) the first consonant is lenited: an h comes after the first letter. Before a vowel mo becomes m' and do becomes d'.
lessons.structure: cara → mo chara · teach → do theach · máthair → a mháthair (his mother), but a máthair (her mother) · athair → m'athair
lessons.tip: a + lenition = his, a without lenition = her. The lenition shows who is meant.

lessons.title: Bhí: was
lessons.rule: The past of 'tá' is 'bhí'. Negative: 'ní raibh'. Question: 'An raibh ...?'.
lessons.structure: Bhí mé · Ní raibh mé · An raibh tú ...? · Antwort: Bhí. / Ní raibh.
lessons.tip: Here too: answer with the verb, Bhí (yes) or Ní raibh (no).

ex.prompt: Yesterday it was cold: ___ sé fuar inné.

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 10
lessons.rule: When counting (without a noun) 'a' comes before the number. Before a vowel an h is added.
lessons.structure: a haon · a dó · a trí · a ceathair · a cúig · a sé · a seacht · a hocht · a naoi · a deich
examples: a haon, a dó, a trí!
lessons.tip: a haon and a hocht take an h because they start with a vowel.

lessons.title: dhá + singular
lessons.rule: Before a noun the numbers change: 'dhá' (2). After 2 to 6 the noun is singular and lenited. After 7 to 10 eclipsis follows.
lessons.structure: cat → dhá chat · trí chat · cúig chat · seacht gcat · ocht gcat · bád → dhá bhád · seacht mbád
lessons.tip: After numbers the noun usually stays singular: dhá chat, not dhá cait.

lessons.title: seo and sin
lessons.rule: 'seo' (this here) and 'sin' (that there) come after the noun with the article. On their own they start the sentence.
lessons.structure: an fear seo (this man) · an bhean sin (that woman) · Seo é mo chara. · Sin í mo mháthair.
examples: Is maith liom an teach seo.
lessons.tip: For people: Seo é (m) / Seo í (f): this is him / her.

ex.prompt: ___ é mo dheartháir. (This is my brother.)
ex.explain: Use seo é to introduce a man.

ex.prompt: That is my mother: ___ í mo mháthair.
ex.explain: Introducing → sin í or seo í.

lessons.title: Question words
lessons.rule: The most important question words come at the start. After 'Cá' (where) comes 'bhfuil' with eclipsis.
lessons.structure: Cá bhfuil? (where is) · Cé? (who) · Cad? (what) · Cathain? (when) · Cén fáth? (why) · Cé mhéad? (how much)
lessons.tip: 'Cé' takes an h before é, í, iad: Cé hí sin? (Who is she?)

ex.prompt: Where is the station? ___ an stáisiún?
___ mhéad atá air? (How much does it cost?)

lessons.title: le: with
lessons.rule: 'le' (with) merges with pronouns into liom, leat, leis ... You need these forms for company and many expressions.
lessons.structure: Tar liom! (Come with me!) · An bhfuil tú ag teacht linn? · Labhair sé léi. (He spoke to her.)
examples: An mbeidh tú ag teacht linn?
lessons.tip: Thank you literally means 'may good be at you': Go raibh maith agat (ag, not le).

ex.prompt: He spoke to her: Labhair sé ___.
Translate: Are you coming with us?
ex.answer: An bhfuil tú ag teacht linn

lessons.title: present
lessons.rule: In the present regular verbs take -ann (broad stem) or -eann (slender stem). For 'I' there is a separate form: -aim / -im.
lessons.structure: ól (to drink): ólaim · ólann tú · ólann sé · ólaimid · ólann sibh · ólann siad · bris (to break): brisim · briseann sé
lessons.tip: Broad = last vowel a, o, u. Slender = last vowel e, i. The ending adapts.

lessons.title: past
lessons.rule: The past is formed by lenition of the stem. If the verb starts with a vowel or f, d' is added in front.
lessons.structure: cuir → chuir mé · bris → bhris sé · dún → dhún siad · ól → d'ól mé · fan → d'fhan sé
lessons.tip: In the past there is no ending for I: chuir mé (not chuiraim).

lessons.title: Níor and Ar?
lessons.rule: Negative in the past: 'níor' + lenition. Question: 'Ar' + lenition. The d' disappears.
lessons.structure: Níor chuir mé · Níor ól sé · Ar chuir tú? · Ar ól tú? · Antwort: Chuir. / Níor chuir.
lessons.tip: Again the answer is the verb: Ar ól tú é? D'ól. / Níor ól.

ex.prompt: Ar dhún tú an fhuinneog? No:

lessons.title: future
lessons.rule: The future takes -faidh (broad) or -fidh (slender). Negative with ní + lenition, question with an + eclipsis.
lessons.structure: ól → ólfaidh mé · cuir → cuirfidh sé · dún → dúnfaidh siad · Ní chuirfidh mé · An ólfaidh tú?
lessons.tip: Eclipsis after 'an': a letter is put in front, e.g. c → gc: An gcuirfidh tú?

lessons.title: Beidh: will be
lessons.rule: The future of 'tá' is 'beidh'. Negative: 'ní bheidh'. Question: 'An mbeidh ...?'.
lessons.structure: Beidh mé · Ní bheidh mé · An mbeidh tú ...? · Antwort: Beidh. / Ní bheidh.
lessons.tip: Now you have all three tenses of 'to be': tá, bhí, beidh.

ex.prompt: Tomorrow it will be sunny: ___ sé grianmhar amárach.
I won't be there: ___ mé ann.

lessons.title: Is maith liom
lessons.rule: 'To like' uses the copula and 'le' (with): Is maith liom (it is good with me). 'le' also merges with the pronoun.
lessons.structure: liom · leat · leis · léi · linn · libh · leo · Is maith liom tae. · Ní maith liom caife. · An maith leat ...?
lessons.tip: Is breá liom means I love, so it is stronger than is maith liom.

ex.prompt: I like tea: Is maith ___ tae.
He doesn't like coffee: ___ maith leis caife.
ex.explain: Use ní for the negative copula.

ex.prompt: An maith ___ é? (Do you like it?)

lessons.title: Tá ocras orm
lessons.rule: In Irish, feelings and states sit 'on' you: Tá ocras orm (hunger is on me). 'ar' merges with the pronoun.
lessons.structure: orm · ort · air · uirthi · orainn · oraibh · orthu · ocras (hunger) · tart (thirst) · tuirse (tiredness) · áthas (joy)
lessons.tip: 'Cad atá ort?' (What's wrong with you?) follows this pattern too.

ex.prompt: Match ar to its pronoun forms.

lessons.title: Tá mé ag ithe
lessons.rule: What is happening right now: tá + person + ag + verbal noun. The verbal noun is a separate form you have to learn.
lessons.structure: ith → ag ithe · ól → ag ól · obair → ag obair · léigh → ag léamh · rith → ag rith · déan → ag déanamh
examples: What are you doing right now?
lessons.tip: Literally: I am at working. Very similar to 'am Arbeiten' in Swiss German.

ex.prompt: I'm eating right now: Tá mé ___.
ex.explain: Use ag followed by the verbal noun.

ex.prompt: He is reading right now: Tá sé ag ___.
Translate: We are drinking tea right now.

lessons.title: Adjectives
lessons.rule: The adjective comes after the noun. After a feminine noun the adjective is lenited.
lessons.structure: carr mór (m) · bean mhór (f) · lá breá (m) · oíche bhreá (f) · cailín beag (cailín is masculine!)
lessons.tip: Gender is grammatical: cailín (girl) is masculine, so cailín beag has no lenition.

lessons.title: Imperative
lessons.rule: The imperative is the bare stem. For several people add -aigí / -igí. Prohibitions with 'ná' (with h before a vowel).
lessons.structure: suigh → Suigh síos! · Suígí síos! · éist → Éist! · Éistigí! · Ná hól! · Ná bí buartha!
lessons.tip: 'Ná' adds an h before a vowel: ól → Ná hól é!

ex.explain: Use ná for a negative command.
Use ná bí to say “do not be”.

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The Portuguese alphabet
lessons.rule: Portuguese has 26 letters plus ç and vowels with accents. The tilde (ã, õ) makes a vowel nasal, as if you speak through your nose.
lessons.structure: ã / õ = nasal | ç = s | lh = ly | nh = ny | j = zh | s at the end = sh
lessons.tip: In European Portuguese unstressed vowels are often very short or almost silent.

alphabet.sound: k, or s before e, i
eh, or almost silent at the end
g, or zh before e, i
o, or oo at the end
tapped r, throaty at the start
s, z between vowels, sh at the end

ex.prompt: Match the letter and its sound

lessons.title: How Portuguese sounds
lessons.rule: Portuguese has nasal vowels and a few special letters. In Portugal, unstressed vowels are often very short.
lessons.structure: ão, õe, -em → nasal (pão) | ç → s (coração) | lh → "lli" (trabalho) | nh → ny (vinho)
lessons.tip: In Portugal, s at the end of a word sounds like sh: "dois" = "doish".

ex.prompt: Match the spelling and the sound

lessons.title: Olá! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: In Portugal you say your name with "chamo-me" and where you are from with "sou de".
lessons.structure: Chamo-me … | Sou de … | Muito prazer!
lessons.tip: Men say obrigado, women say obrigada (thank you).

ex.prompt: I am from Porto. → ___ do Porto.

lessons.title: o, a, um, uma: articles and gender
lessons.rule: Every Portuguese noun is masculine or feminine. The article agrees with the noun in gender and number: o / os (masculine), a / as (feminine), um / uns, uma / umas.
lessons.structure: o livro · os livros | a casa · as casas | um livro · uma casa
examples: Os amigos e as amigas chegam.
lessons.tip: Most nouns in -o are masculine and most in -a are feminine. Learn the article with every new word: o dia (the day) is masculine although it ends in -a.

ex.explain: casa is feminine singular → a casa.
livros is masculine plural → os livros.

ex.prompt: Match the article and the noun

lessons.title: ser: to be (who and what)
lessons.rule: ser describes identity, origin, profession and lasting characteristics.
lessons.structure: eu sou · tu és · ele/ela/você é · nós somos · eles/elas/vocês são
examples: De onde és? Sou da Suíça.
Where are you from? I am from Switzerland.
lessons.tip: In Portugal, tu is used with friends and family. With strangers people often use você or just the verb in the 3rd person: "O senhor é de Lisboa?"

ex.explain: A lasting quality → ser: Lisboa é bonita.

lessons.title: estar: to be (how and where)
lessons.rule: estar describes temporary states (tired, ill, happy today) and where someone or something is.
lessons.structure: eu estou · tu estás · ele/ela/você está · nós estamos · eles/elas/vocês estão
lessons.tip: Compare: "Ele é simpático" (that is his character) and "Ele está contente" (that is how he feels now).

reading.title: No café
reading.text: A Emma está num café em Lisboa. Ela pede um café e uma sandes. O empregado é simpático e pergunta: «Quer leite?» A Emma diz: «Não, obrigada.» Ela paga com cartão.
reading.tr: Emma is in a café in Lisbon. She orders a coffee and a sandwich. The waiter is friendly and asks: "Do you want milk?" Emma says: "No, thank you." She pays by card.

ex.explain: In a café, o empregado is the waiter.

lessons.title: Regular verbs: -ar, -er, -ir
lessons.rule: Regular verbs drop -ar, -er or -ir and add a personal ending.
lessons.structure: falar: falo · falas · fala · falamos · falam | comer: como · comes · come · comemos · comem | abrir: abro · abres · abre · abrimos · abrem
lessons.tip: The subject pronoun is usually left out because the ending already shows the person: "Falo" = "I speak".

lessons.title: Questions: quem, o que, onde, quando, porquê
lessons.rule: Question words come at the start. In speech, a yes/no question often keeps statement word order and only the intonation rises.
lessons.structure: Onde trabalhas? | O que fazes? | Quem é? | Quando chegas? | Porque estudas? → Porque…
lessons.tip: porque (why / because) is written as one word. At the very end of a question it becomes porquê: "Estudas português porquê?"

ex.prompt: ___ é aquela senhora? – É a minha professora.

lessons.title: há: there is, there are
lessons.rule: há (from haver) means "there is" and "there are". It never changes for singular or plural.
lessons.structure: Há + um/uma + singular | Há + plural | Não há…
lessons.tip: há also means "ago" or "for" with time: "Moro aqui há dois anos" = I have lived here for two years.

ex.explain: Existence → há, also with a plural.
há does not change: não há.

reading.title: Um novo vizinho
reading.text: O Tom mora agora num apartamento novo. O apartamento é pequeno, mas tem uma varanda. No prédio há uma vizinha simpática. O Tom pergunta: «Onde fica o supermercado?» Ela responde: «Fica perto, na rua ao lado.»
reading.tr: Tom now lives in a new flat. The flat is small, but it has a balcony. In the building there is a friendly neighbour. Tom asks: "Where is the supermarket?" She answers: "It is nearby, in the next street."

ex.prompt: What does he ask the neighbour?

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 100
lessons.rule: One and two change with gender: um livro, uma casa; dois livros, duas casas. From 21 the tens and units are joined with e: vinte e um. In Portugal 16, 17 and 19 are dezasseis, dezassete, dezanove (in Brazil: dezesseis, dezessete, dezenove).
lessons.structure: um/uma, dois/duas, três … dez | onze, doze, treze, catorze, quinze | dezasseis … vinte | vinte e um · trinta · quarenta · cinquenta · cem
lessons.tip: Age uses ter: tenho 20 anos.

lessons.title: The time and days
lessons.rule: Ask "Que horas são?". One o’clock is singular (é uma hora), the other hours plural (são duas horas). The weekdays from Monday to Friday are counted: segunda-feira is Monday.
lessons.structure: É uma hora · São três horas · três e um quarto · três e meia · quatro menos um quarto · meio-dia | na segunda-feira · em maio · às oito
lessons.tip: In everyday speech -feira is often dropped: segunda, terça, quarta.

ex.explain: One o’clock is singular and feminine: é uma hora.
The week starts on Sunday (domingo), so Monday is the second day.

lessons.title: gostar de: to like
lessons.rule: gostar always needs de before what you like. de joins with articles: de + o = do, de + a = da.
lessons.structure: gostar de + noun / infinitive | gosto do… · gosto da…
lessons.tip: To say what you would like now, use gostaria de: "Gostaria de um café" (I would like a coffee).

lessons.title: Pretérito perfeito: finished actions
lessons.rule: The pretérito perfeito tells what happened at a finished moment in the past (yesterday, last week, in 2020).
lessons.structure: falar: falei · falaste · falou · falámos · falaram | comer: comi · comeste · comeu · comemos · comeram | ir / ser: fui · foste · foi · fomos · foram
lessons.tip: In Portugal, falámos (with an accent) is the past and falamos is the present.

ex.explain: A finished action yesterday → perfeito: trabalhei.
ir in the past, nós → fomos.

ex.prompt: Match the infinitive and the past form (eu)

lessons.title: ir + infinitive: plans
lessons.rule: For plans and the near future, Portuguese mostly uses the present of ir + an infinitive.
lessons.structure: vou · vais · vai · vamos · vão + infinitive
examples: I am going to study tonight.
We are going to travel in July.
Are you going to have dinner with us?
lessons.tip: Do not add a: "Vou comer" (not "vou a comer").

ex.explain: A plan for tomorrow → vou + infinitive.

ex.prompt: Build: "We are going to travel in July."

reading.title: Um fim de semana
reading.text: No fim de semana passado, a Júlia visitou amigos no Porto. No sábado foram ao mercado e compraram fruta e queijo. Depois jantaram num pequeno restaurante perto do rio. A Júlia gostou muito da cidade. No próximo mês vai voltar e vai ficar uma semana inteira.
reading.tr: Last weekend Júlia visited friends in Porto. On Saturday they went to the market and bought fruit and cheese. Then they had dinner in a small restaurant near the river. Júlia liked the city a lot. Next month she is going to come back and stay a whole week.

ex.prompt: What is Júlia going to do next month?
ex.explain: "vai voltar e vai ficar uma semana inteira".

ex.prompt: What do they do after the market?
options: They have dinner in a restaurant

lessons.title: Pretérito imperfeito: habits and background
lessons.rule: The imperfeito describes what used to happen, what was going on and how things were.
lessons.structure: -ar: falava · falavas · falava · falávamos · falavam | -er/-ir: comia · comias · comia · comíamos · comiam | ser: era · eras · era · éramos · eram
examples: Quando era criança, brincava lá fora.
When I was a child, I used to play outside.
We used to live near the sea.
lessons.tip: Typical signals: quando era criança, antigamente (in the past), todos os dias (every day), sempre.

ex.prompt: Quando era pequeno, ___ todos os dias.

ex.explain: A description in the past → era.

ex.prompt: Match the infinitive and the imperfeito form (eu)

lessons.title: Perfeito or imperfeito?
lessons.rule: In one story, the perfeito moves the action forward (what happened) and the imperfeito paints the background (what was going on).
lessons.structure: imperfeito (background) + quando + perfeito (event)
examples: I was reading when he phoned.
Chovia e depois saiu o sol.
It was raining and then the sun came out.
Estava cansada, por isso fui para casa.
I was tired, so I went home.
lessons.tip: Ask yourself: is it a scene or an event? Scene → imperfeito. Event → perfeito.

ex.prompt: Eu ___ o jantar quando a campainha tocou.
Ontem ___ às sete e saí logo.
___ muito frio, por isso ficámos em casa.
Build: "I was reading when he phoned."

lessons.title: Futuro simples: will
lessons.rule: The simple future adds -ei, -ás, -á, -emos, -ão to the whole infinitive. It is used in writing, formal speech and predictions. In everyday speech, ir + infinitive is more common.
lessons.structure: falarei · falarás · falará · falaremos · falarão | fazer → farei · dizer → direi · trazer → trarei
lessons.tip: The future can also express a guess about now: "Onde estará o Rui?" = Where might Rui be?

ex.prompt: Amanhã ___ sol em todo o país.
Match the infinitive and the future (eu)

reading.title: Procurar casa
reading.text: A Nina procurava casa há semanas. Todos os dias via anúncios na internet, mas os apartamentos eram pequenos ou ficavam longe do trabalho. Ontem encontrou finalmente um apartamento bonito, com muita luz, a dez minutos do escritório. O único problema é o preço: é caro. Amanhã falará com o banco e depois decidirá.
reading.tr: Nina had been looking for a home for weeks. Every day she looked at adverts online, but the flats were small or far from work. Yesterday she finally found a nice flat with lots of light, ten minutes from the office. The only problem is the price: it is expensive. Tomorrow she will talk to the bank and then decide.

ex.prompt: How long has Nina been looking?
What is the problem with the flat?
ex.explain: "O único problema é o preço: é caro."

options: How long something has been going on
ex.explain: há + time = for (a period up to now).

lessons.title: Object pronouns: o, a, lhe, me, te
lessons.rule: Object pronouns replace people or things. In European Portuguese they normally come after the verb with a hyphen. They move before the verb after não, question words and many conjunctions.
lessons.structure: conheço-o · vejo-a · dou-lhe | não o conheço · quem te disse? · acho que me viu
examples: I will write to him/her tomorrow.
Não a vejo há muito tempo.
I have not seen her for a long time.
lessons.tip: o / a / os / as = direct object (him, her, it, them). lhe / lhes = to him, to her, to them.

ex.explain: Marta is a direct object and feminine → a.

ex.prompt: Dei o livro ao Rui. → Dei-___ o livro.

ex.explain: After não, the pronoun goes before the verb.
Affirmative sentence → pronoun after the verb.

lessons.title: por or para?
lessons.rule: por expresses cause, means, exchange and route (through). para expresses goal, destination, recipient and deadline.
lessons.structure: por: obrigado por · por telefone · pela cidade | para: para Lisboa · para ti · para sexta
examples: I work for a Swiss company.
I study to pass the exam.
lessons.tip: por + o = pelo, por + a = pela.

ex.explain: Reason for thanks → por + o = pelo.

ex.prompt: What does por / para express here?

lessons.title: Comparisons: mais, menos, tão
lessons.rule: Comparisons use mais / menos … (do) que and tão … como. Some adjectives have their own forms.
