lessons.structure: mais rápido (do) que | menos caro (do) que | tão útil como | bom → melhor · mau → pior · grande → maior
examples: É mais rápido do que eu.
É tão útil como o outro.
It is as useful as the other one.
lessons.tip: Never say "mais bom". Use melhor.

ex.prompt: O comboio é ___ rápido do que o autocarro.
ex.explain: Comparison of superiority → mais … do que.

ex.prompt: A Ana é tão alta ___ a irmã.
Este restaurante é ___ do que o outro.
Build: "It is as useful as the other one."
ex.answer: É tão útil como o outro

lessons.title: Condicional: would
lessons.rule: The conditional adds -ia, -ias, -ia, -íamos, -iam to the infinitive. It is used for polite requests, wishes and hypothetical situations.
lessons.structure: gostaria · poderia · faria (fazer) · diria (dizer)
lessons.tip: In everyday speech many people use the imperfeito instead: "Queria um café" sounds natural and polite.

ex.prompt: ___ de reservar uma mesa para dois.
Match the infinitive and the conditional (eu)

reading.title: Mobilidade sustentável
reading.text: Muitas cidades investem em bicicletas e transportes públicos, mas a mudança continua lenta. Para muitas pessoas, o carro ainda é mais cómodo do que o autocarro, sobretudo fora do centro. Os especialistas dizem que seria mais fácil mudar de hábitos se os transportes fossem tão rápidos como o carro. Por isso, algumas cidades criaram vias só para autocarros e baixaram o preço dos passes. Os primeiros resultados são positivos, mas ninguém lhes chamaria uma revolução.
reading.tr: Many cities invest in bicycles and public transport, but change is still slow. For many people the car is still more convenient than the bus, especially outside the centre. Experts say it would be easier to change habits if public transport were as fast as the car. That is why some cities have created bus-only lanes and lowered the price of passes. The first results are positive, but nobody would call them a revolution.

options: They created bus lanes and lowered pass prices
ex.explain: "criaram vias só para autocarros e baixaram o preço dos passes".

ex.prompt: What do many cities invest in?

lessons.title: Conjuntivo presente: wishes and doubt
lessons.rule: The present subjunctive follows expressions of wish, need, feeling, judgement and doubt + que. Take the eu form of the present, drop -o and swap the vowel: -ar → -e, -er/-ir → -a.
lessons.structure: falar → fale · fales · fale · falemos · falem | ter → tenha | ser → seja | ir → vá
examples: It is important that you study.
lessons.tip: After achar que / pensar que (I think that) use the indicative. After não acho que use the subjunctive.

lessons.title: se: real and hypothetical conditions
lessons.rule: Real future conditions use se + futuro do conjuntivo. Hypotheses use se + imperfeito do conjuntivo + condicional.
lessons.structure: Se tiver tempo, vou. | Se tivesse tempo, viajaria mais. | Se soubesse, teria vindo.
examples: If I have time, I will go.
If I had time, I would travel more.
Se eu soubesse, não teria vindo.
If I had known, I would not have come.
lessons.tip: The futuro do conjuntivo is special to Portuguese: se puder, quando chegares, se fizer bom tempo.

ex.prompt: Se ___ bom tempo amanhã, vamos à praia.
ex.explain: A real future condition → futuro do conjuntivo: fizer.

lessons.title: Personal infinitive
lessons.rule: Portuguese infinitives can take personal endings when the subject must be clear: -es, -mos, -em (eu and ele have no ending).
lessons.structure: falar · falares · falar · falarmos · falarem | é melhor sairmos · antes de chegares · para fazermos
examples: It is better for us to leave early.
I brought the book for you to read.
lessons.tip: Use it after prepositions (para, antes de, depois de, sem) and after impersonal phrases like é melhor, é importante.

ex.prompt: Build: "It is better for us to leave early."

lessons.title: Connectors: embora, contudo, portanto
lessons.rule: Connectors structure contrast, cause and conclusion. embora (although) needs the subjunctive. contudo and no entanto (however), portanto (therefore) and visto que (since) take the indicative.
lessons.structure: Embora + conjuntivo, … | …; contudo, … | …, portanto … | Visto que + indicativo, …
examples: Although it is difficult, I carry on.
Choveu muito, portanto o jogo foi adiado.
It rained a lot, so the match was postponed.
lessons.tip: Use contudo or no entanto in writing instead of repeating mas.

ex.prompt: Embora ___ tarde, vou terminar o texto.
O projeto é caro; ___, vale a pena.
Match the connector and its meaning

reading.title: Migração e língua
reading.text: A aprendizagem da língua influencia a participação social dos imigrantes, mas depende também da educação e do emprego. Embora muitos países ofereçam cursos gratuitos, nem todos os recém-chegados conseguem frequentá-los, porque trabalham por turnos ou têm filhos pequenos. É importante que os horários sejam flexíveis e que as aulas tenham lugar perto de casa. Contudo, a língua não se aprende apenas na sala de aula: é no trabalho, na escola dos filhos e entre vizinhos que ela ganha vida. Portanto, uma política de integração eficaz deve criar oportunidades para as pessoas se encontrarem.
reading.tr: Learning the language influences immigrants’ social participation, but it also depends on education and employment. Although many countries offer free courses, not all newcomers manage to attend them, because they work shifts or have small children. It is important that timetables are flexible and that classes take place close to home. However, a language is not learned only in the classroom: it comes alive at work, at the children’s school and among neighbours. An effective integration policy must therefore create opportunities for people to meet.

ex.prompt: Why can some newcomers not attend courses?
options: They work shifts or have small children
ex.explain: "trabalham por turnos ou têm filhos pequenos".

ex.prompt: What does learning the language influence?
What else does it depend on?
ex.explain: "depende também da educação e do emprego".

units.title: Start here · Sounds and first words

lessons.title: The Serbo-Croatian alphabet
lessons.rule: Serbo-Croatian (Bosnian, Croatian, Montenegrin, Serbian) has 30 letters, one for every sound. Serbian also uses Cyrillic, with exactly the same sounds. Read every letter as written – there are no silent letters.
lessons.structure: c = ts | č / ć = hard / soft ch | dž / đ = hard / soft j | lj = ly | nj = ny | š = sh | ž = zh
lessons.tip: dž, lj and nj are single letters: konj (horse) has 3 letters: k-o-nj.

ex.prompt: Which letter sounds like: hard ch as in "church"?
ex.explain: Č č: hard ch as in "church" – čaj.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and its sound

lessons.title: Sounds and letters
lessons.rule: Every letter has exactly one sound, and words are read the way they are written. Learn these letters and you can read everything.
lessons.structure: č, ć → ch | š → sh | ž → zh (as in "measure") | đ, dž → j | j → y | c → ts | lj → "lli" | nj → ny
examples: finger: r can work as a vowel
lessons.tip: Serbian is also written in Cyrillic. This course uses the Latin letters.

ex.prompt: Match the letter and the sound

lessons.title: Zdravo! Introduce yourself
lessons.rule: Say your name with "zovem se" and where you are from with "ja sam iz".
lessons.structure: Zovem se … | Ja sam iz … | Drago mi je!
lessons.tip: With strangers ask politely: "Kako se zovete?"

ex.prompt: My name is Ana. → ___ se Ana.

lessons.title: biti: to be
lessons.rule: biti (to be) has short forms that you use almost all the time. They never stand first in a sentence. To start with the verb, use the long form (jesam) or a question with je li / da li.
lessons.structure: ja sam · ti si · on/ona/ono je · mi smo · vi ste · oni/one/ona su | not: nisam · nisi · nije · nismo · niste · nisu
lessons.tip: The pronoun is often left out: "Student sam." means "I am a student." The negative is one word: nisam, nije.

ex.explain: The negative of je is nije.

ex.prompt: Match the person and the form

lessons.title: Gender: on, ona, ono
lessons.rule: Every noun has a gender. Most nouns ending in a consonant are masculine, in -a feminine and in -o or -e neuter. Words like "this" agree: ovaj, ova, ovo.
lessons.structure: ovaj grad (m) · ova kuća (f) · ovo selo (n) | dobar grad · dobra kuća · dobro selo
lessons.tip: Some masculine nouns for people end in -a: tata (dad), kolega (colleague). They take masculine adjectives: dobar tata.

ex.prompt: Match the noun and its gender

lessons.title: Present tense: -am, -im, -em
lessons.rule: Present tense endings follow three patterns. Learn the ja form and the oni form of each new verb; the rest follows.
lessons.structure: čitati: čitam · čitaš · čita · čitamo · čitate · čitaju | govoriti: govorim · govoriš · govori · govorimo · govorite · govore | pisati: pišem · pišeš · piše · pišemo · pišete · pišu
lessons.tip: There is only one present tense: "čitam" means both "I read" and "I am reading".

ex.explain: Verb + li makes a yes/no question.

lessons.title: Asking questions
lessons.rule: Yes/no questions use verb + li, or da li / je li at the start. Question words come first.
lessons.structure: Govoriš li…? · Da li govoriš…? · Je li to…? | tko/ko · što/šta · gdje · kada · zašto · kako
examples: Why are you learning the language?
lessons.tip: Who and what differ by country: tko / što in Croatia, ko / šta in Serbia and Bosnia. Both are understood everywhere.

lessons.title: Saying no: ne and nemam
lessons.rule: Put ne before the verb. A few verbs join ne into one word: nisam (I am not), nemam (I do not have), neću (I will not).
lessons.structure: ne + verb: ne razumijem | biti → nisam | imati → nemam | htjeti → neću
lessons.tip: Double negatives are correct: "Nitko ne zna." / "Niko ne zna." = Nobody knows.

ex.prompt: I do not have a car. → ___ auto.
I am not at home. → ___ kod kuće.
I do not understand. → Ja ___ razumijem.
ex.explain: ne goes directly before the verb.

lessons.title: ima and nema: there is, there is not
lessons.rule: ima means "there is / there are". nema means "there is not". After nema, the thing that is missing goes into the genitive: nema kruha / hleba (there is no bread).
lessons.structure: Ima + noun | Nema + genitive | Ima li…?
examples: There are a lot of people.
lessons.tip: "Nema problema" is one of the most useful phrases in the whole region.

ex.prompt: Is there a pharmacy here? → ___ li ovdje ljekarna / apoteka?
There are many tourists. → ___ puno turista.
ex.explain: ima does not change for plural.

lessons.title: Accusative: the direct object
lessons.rule: The direct object is in the accusative. Feminine -a becomes -u. Masculine words for people and animals add -a. Masculine things and neuter nouns stay the same.
lessons.structure: knjiga → knjigu | brat → brata | grad → grad | selo → selo
lessons.tip: Ask "koga?" (whom?) for people and "što? / šta?" (what?) for things.

ex.explain: A masculine thing stays the same.

lessons.title: Locative: where something is
lessons.rule: After u (in) and na (on, at) for a location, nouns take the locative: -u for masculine and neuter, -i for feminine.
lessons.structure: u + grad → u gradu | u + škola → u školi | na + more → na moru | u + Zagreb → u Zagrebu
examples: In summer we are at the seaside.
lessons.tip: Some places take na instead of u: na poslu (at work), na fakultetu (at university), na moru (at the seaside).

ex.explain: Feminine -ka → -ci in the locative: u banci.

lessons.title: Numbers and nouns
lessons.rule: Numbers change the noun after them. With 2, 3 and 4 use the genitive singular. From 5 upwards (and with puno, malo) use the genitive plural.
lessons.structure: jedan grad | dva / tri / četiri grada | pet gradova | jedna knjiga | dvije / dve knjige | pet knjiga
lessons.tip: Feminine "two" is dvije (ijekavian) or dve (ekavian).

lessons.title: Perfect tense: what happened
lessons.rule: The past is built with the short forms of biti + a past participle. The participle agrees with the subject: -o / -la / -lo, plural -li / -le / -la.
lessons.structure: raditi → radio (m) · radila (f) | ja sam radio/radila · mi smo radili | negative: nisam radio
examples: We did not watch the film.
lessons.tip: In ekavian speech the masculine forms end the same: radio, video. Ijekavian: vidio, htio; ekavian: video, hteo.

ex.prompt: (A woman says) Jučer sam ___ kod kuće.
He did not come. → On ___ došao.
Build: "We did not watch the film."

lessons.title: Future: ću + infinitive
lessons.rule: The future uses the short forms of htjeti (ću, ćeš, će…) + infinitive. When the verb comes first, the infinitive joins the form: radit ću (Croatian spelling) or radiću (Serbian spelling).
lessons.structure: ja ću raditi · ti ćeš raditi · on će raditi · mi ćemo · vi ćete · oni će | Radit ću. / Radiću.
lessons.tip: Questions and short answers use the long form: Hoćeš li doći? – Hoću! (Yes, I will.)

ex.explain: At the start of a question use the long form hoćeš.
The negative future is one word: neću.

ex.prompt: Match the person and the future form

lessons.title: Word order: the second position
lessons.rule: Short words like sam, si, je, ću, se, mi, ga, li are clitics. They always stand in the second position of the sentence, after the first word or phrase.
lessons.structure: Ja sam ga vidio. · Vidio sam ga. · Jučer sam ga vidio. | not: Sam ga vidio.
examples: I will write to you tomorrow.
lessons.tip: Several clitics follow a fixed order: li, then verb forms (sam, ću), then pronouns (mi, ga), then se. Exception: je goes last.

ex.explain: Verb clitic (sam) before pronoun clitic (ga), both in second position.
se goes in the second position: Zove se Ana.
Participle first, then sam, then ga.

lessons.title: Aspect: finished or ongoing
lessons.rule: Most verbs come in pairs. The imperfective describes an ongoing or repeated action, the perfective a single completed one. Perfectives often add a prefix.
lessons.structure: pisati → napisati | čitati → pročitati | piti → popiti | kupovati → kupiti
lessons.tip: Perfective verbs in the present tense usually express the future or appear after da / ako: "Ako dođeš…" (If you come…).

ex.prompt: Yesterday I read the whole book. → Jučer sam ___ cijelu knjigu.
I read every evening. → Svaku večer ___.

ex.explain: The prefix na- makes pisati perfective.

lessons.title: Modal verbs: moći, morati, htjeti
lessons.rule: Modal verbs are followed by an infinitive (more common in Croatia) or by da + present tense (more common in Serbia and Bosnia). Both are correct.
lessons.structure: mogu raditi = mogu da radim | moram ići = moram da idem | hoću znati = hoću da znam
examples: I want to know the truth.
lessons.tip: moći: mogu, možeš, može, možemo, možete, mogu. The ja and oni forms are the same.

ex.prompt: I can come tomorrow. → Sutra ___ doći.
Which is also correct for "Mogu raditi"?

lessons.title: Dative: to whom
lessons.rule: The dative shows to whom something is given or said. It also expresses liking with sviđati se: "Sviđa mi se" = I like it (it pleases me).
lessons.structure: dati + dative: dajem Ani, pišem bratu | short forms: mi, ti, mu, joj, nam, vam, im | Sviđa mi se…
examples: I am giving the book to Ana.
I am writing to my brother.
lessons.tip: In "Sviđa mi se grad", the city is the subject. For more things: "Sviđaju mi se planine."

ex.prompt: I am giving Marko a present. → Dajem ___ poklon.
Do you like it? → Sviđa li ___ se?
ex.explain: The short dative of ti is ti.

ex.prompt: She likes the mountains. → ___ se sviđaju planine.
Match the pronoun and its short dative

lessons.title: Instrumental: with whom, by what means
lessons.rule: The instrumental answers "with whom?" (after s / sa) and "with what? / by what means?" (without a preposition). Endings: -om / -em for masculine and neuter, -om for feminine.
lessons.structure: s prijateljem | sa sestrom | autobusom | olovkom
examples: I am going to the cinema with a friend.
I am writing with a pencil.
lessons.tip: Use sa before words starting with s, z, š, ž or when it is easier to say: sa sestrom, sa mnom (with me).

ex.prompt: I am going with my sister. → Idem ___ sestrom.
We are travelling by train. → Putujemo ___. (vlak / voz)

ex.explain: Means of transport → instrumental without preposition.

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs with se
lessons.rule: Many verbs need se: zvati se (to be called), smijati se (to laugh), nadati se (to hope). se stands in the second position, like the other clitics.
lessons.structure: zovem se · smijemo se · vidimo se | Kako se zoveš? · Vidimo se sutra!
lessons.tip: Ijekavian smijati se, ekavian smejati se (to laugh): the meaning is the same.

ex.prompt: What is your name? → Kako ___ zoveš?
See you on Monday! → Vidimo ___ u ponedjeljak!
ex.explain: vidjeti se = to see each other.
vidjeti se in the mi form.

lessons.title: Comparatives: bigger, better
lessons.rule: Most comparatives end in -iji or -ji, often with a sound change. "Than" is od + genitive or nego / negoli.
lessons.structure: nov → noviji | star → stariji | velik → veći | mali → manji | dobar → bolji | loš → lošiji | najbolji = the best
examples: Ovaj film je bolji nego onaj.
This film is better than that one.
That is the most beautiful city.
lessons.tip: lijep → ljepši (ijekavian), lep → lepši (ekavian). The superlative adds naj-.

ex.prompt: This house is bigger. → Ova kuća je ___.
Ana is older than Ivan. → Ana je starija ___ Ivana.
Match the adjective and the comparative

lessons.title: Conditional: would
lessons.rule: The conditional uses bih, bi, bi, bismo, biste, bi + past participle. It expresses wishes, polite requests and hypothetical situations.
lessons.structure: ja bih volio/voljela · ti bi · mi bismo | Kad bih imao vremena, putovao bih.
examples: Kad bih imala vremena, učila bih više.
If I had time, I would study more. (woman)
lessons.tip: Polite requests: "Možete li…?" is fine, "Biste li mogli…?" is even more polite.

ex.prompt: (A man says) I would like to travel. → Volio ___ putovati.
Could you (formal) help me? → ___ li mi mogli pomoći?
Build: "Could you help me?" (to a friend, man)

lessons.title: Relative clauses: koji, koja, koje
lessons.rule: koji (who, which, that) agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to. Its case depends on its role inside the relative clause. The clause is always separated by commas.
lessons.structure: čovjek koji radi · žena koja pjeva · dijete koje spava | knjiga koju čitam (accusative)
examples: Čovjek koji radi ovdje je moj ujak.
The man who works here is my uncle.
The book that I am reading is excellent.
Grad u kojem živim je mali.
The city I live in is small.
lessons.tip: Ijekavian čovjek / dijete, ekavian čovek / dete.

ex.prompt: The woman who sings… → Žena ___ pjeva…
The book that I am reading… → Knjiga ___ čitam…
The child who is sleeping… → Dijete ___ spava…
Match the noun and the relative pronoun
